title: Video consistency and reliability: set pieces, cut audit, joins, cheap Retry
description:
Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. ADR: docs/adr/0002-audited-cuts-and-set-pieces.md. From the 2026-11-14 grilling session. Follows TreeTutor-tq7 (Remotion validator fix).

## Decisions so far

- Manim validator checks only literal colour/font text, like the fixed Remotion validator; Manim cuts are checked when written.
- Instructions explain the validator rules up front. Two tries per cut; the repair sees the real error with paths stripped, and doubles as the cut audit.
- Set pieces: the plan gives each recurring object a look; one call writes shared components every Remotion cut must use.
- One cut audit per cut, all in parallel, before the cut plays; code plus 960x540 frames per sentence end and the last frame; aligns to the plan, not the neighbour; a broken fix falls back.
- Joins: continuing cut = hard cut; scene change = plan-chosen @remotion/transitions effect played one side at a time.
- Pen is for emphasis only; freehand stays; visible pen tip.
- Retry rewrites only failed cuts; errors read 'Cut N of M: reason'.

title: Attachments: images, PDFs and text files
description:
Spec: docs/attachments-spec.md. Spec D of four, from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Images, PDFs and plain-text files via paperclip, paste and drop; attachment belongs to its question; deleted with its conversation; no app caps, provider context errors shown.
- Chat model reads images natively (Claude, Codex; custom endpoint models via an Accepts images switch, default off). No smart-model description step.
- Non-vision chat model: tesseract.js OCR automatically, language data downloaded on first use; OCR icon explains limits; OCR unavailable means send refused.
- PDFs via pdfjs-dist structure: visible text as text, embedded images >= 10% of the page as images, full-page scan sent as image with its invisible OCR text ignored; vector diagrams keep only labels.
- Custom endpoints send images only on their own turn; later turns use [image: name]. Children get text and image names through inherited context only.
- Only widely used, maintained libraries; normal semver ranges.
- Image input shapes (D1, verified live on codex-cli 0.167.2 and Claude Code 2.1.325): Codex turn/start input item { type: 'localImage', path } (optional detail auto|low|high|original) after the text item; Claude -p adds --input-format stream-json on image turns with one user message whose content holds text plus { type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type, data } }. Resumed Claude sessions keep the image; text-only turns stay plain stdin. Details on TreeTutor-9lj.1.

## Fog
- None open (D1 resolved by TreeTutor-9lj.1).

title: Visual asking and motion: one Ask button, chips, step-through
description:
Spec: docs/visual-asking-and-motion-spec.md. Spec C of four, from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- One visible Ask button per ready visual opens the shared floating ask box with the whole visual as source; Try a different version and Enlarge move into a ... menu. Tagged-part clicks and the tagging prompt rule are removed.
- Child chips under each visual in branch family ink.
- Shared sandbox step-through helper with transitions and reduced motion; prompt prefers it for staged ideas.
- No explanatory paragraphs inside visuals; result lines in primary text at reading size.

title: Titles and origin: model-written titles and the origin strip
description:
Spec: docs/titles-and-origin-spec.md. Spec B of four, from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Titles written once by the quick thinking model when the first question is sent: root from the question, child from inherited context plus question. Question text shows meanwhile and stays on failure or unset model. Rename always wins. No Retitle.
- Origin strip at the top of every child: parent address chip (jumps to the source), the source (passage, suggested term or visual title, kind not labelled) and the learner's question. Long sources two lines plus Show all.

title: Setup and tutor style: typed effort, empty first run, tutor style
description:
Spec: docs/setup-and-tutor-style-spec.md. Spec A of four (A, B, C, D), from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Typed effort only for custom endpoint models; 1-32 letters, digits, - or _; remembered per endpoint and model; endpoint errors surface in the reply and the selection stays.
- Fresh install: no model profile, no default provider; only Send is blocked; Settings shows Not set. Existing installs unchanged.
- Tutor style: learner-editable, stored null until edited, prepended to the fixed safety and media rules; default text drafted in the spec for owner review.
- From /teach: default style teaches only what is needed then checks understanding, with occasional predict-then-reveal. Familiarity-pitched explanations, per-tree mission and citations are later.

## Fog
- Owner may still edit the default tutor style text.

title: Triage settings, provider and usage verify scripts into unit and component tests
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-zml

## What to build

Replace these fixture browser scripts with cheaper tests: verify-settings-window, verify-custom-endpoint, verify-dialog-identity, verify-model-roles, verify-model-switch, verify-request-failures, verify-usage-dashboard.

Triage rule for each script, in order:
1. Its checks are already covered by a unit or integration test: delete the script.
2. Its checks are logic (state transitions, request bodies, ordering, labels, formatting, keyboard maps, layout maths): move that logic into a plain .ts module next to the component if it is not already one, unit test it under test/, and delete the script.
3. Its checks need rendered React (what is shown, aria attributes, focus target, click handlers): write a component test with the jsdom harness, and delete the script.
4. Its checks need a real browser (pixel geometry, CSS cascade, pointer gestures, scrolling, media playback): keep the script only if it is in the smoke set (verify-first-conversation, verify-branch-first, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-settings-window, verify-video-player). Otherwise delete it and add one line per lost check to the "Not covered" list in docs/agents/testing.md.
Scripts in verify-all's known map (TreeTutor-cpi) follow the same rule; do not debug them in the browser.

verify-settings-window is in the smoke set. Endpoint and request-failure checks that only inspect HTTP responses belong in integration tests next to the existing endpoint tests.
design: Extraction moves code without changing behaviour; the component imports the new module. Keep every id, class and aria attribute. Delete scripts with plain file removal and remove their entries from verify-all's live/known maps and from scripts/verify/lib when a fixture loses its last user. Do not run npm run verify; run only the new test files while working and npm test once at the end.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each of these scripts is deleted or, if in the smoke set, kept: verify-settings-window, verify-custom-endpoint, verify-dialog-identity, verify-model-roles, verify-model-switch, verify-request-failures, verify-usage-dashboard
- [ ] A ticket comment maps every deleted script to the test file(s) now covering it, or to its "Not covered" lines
- [ ] Every new test file runs in under 1 s (node --test <file>)
- [ ] npm test and npm run build pass; npm test wall time grows by less than 1 s
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Kept verify-settings-window (smoke). Deleted verify-custom-endpoint, verify-dialog-identity, verify-model-roles, verify-model-switch, verify-request-failures, verify-usage-dashboard and orphaned lib/custom-endpoint-{fixture,server}.mjs. Server/HTTP checks already covered: test/providers/endpoints, endpoint-switch, chat-defaults-*, provider, test/store/profiles, test/usage/usage-history, test/media/artifacts-retry/videos-requests, test/map/tree-list (delete copy). New: src/settings/models.ts menuGroups (model-menu grouping, not-connected titles, saved-missing disabled item, repair action) used by ChatPage + unit test test/shell/model-menu.test.mjs; component tests test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs, test/shell/model-roles.test.mjs, test/usage/usage-dashboard.test.mjs (fake api, mocked Date). title: Test strategy: fast unit tests replace per-task browser verification
description:
Owner request of 2026-11-13. Verification costs too many tokens, too much time and too much CPU per task. Rebuild how the project tests, not only where the files live. This epic runs before the rest of TreeTutor-p1k: the remaining splits (Store, createApp, ChatPage, TreeOverview) need a fast test net first.

Measured at 8b6ea4f:
- npm test: 248 tests, about 20 s wall, 580% CPU, 514 MB peak RSS. Slowest files: artifacts.test 21 s, suggestions.test 12 s, startup.test 10 s, videos.test 5 s.
- scripts/verify: 71 fixture scripts plus 12 live scripts, about 22k lines. Each one builds the app and drives Chromium through agent-browser. 11 fail at HEAD (TreeTutor-cpi), several are flaky under the parallel pool.
- .ralph-tui/prompt.hbs tells agents "Prefer integration checks", and open p1k tickets name 4 to 8 browser scripts each as acceptance.

## Notes

Test tiers, cheapest first. Every ticket uses the cheapest tier that proves its acceptance:
1. Unit (default): plain functions from src/**/*.ts and server modules; no HTTP, no SQLite file, no real timers. Milliseconds per test.
2. Component: React components rendered into jsdom in node --test (harness from this epic). For what is shown, aria, focus and handlers.
3. Integration: createApp or Store in-process with a temp database and fake providers. Only for HTTP, storage and provider-boundary behaviour.
4. Browser (E2E): a smoke set of at most 5 fixture scripts, run by release tickets or by hand. Never acceptance for a routine ticket.
Live-provider scripts stay manual and unchanged.

## Decisions so far

- Unit over integration over E2E (owner, 2026-11-13).
- Smoke set: verify-first-conversation, verify-branch-first, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-settings-window, verify-video-player.
- TreeTutor-cpi (11 failing fixture scripts) is superseded: each script is triaged by its area ticket instead of debugged in the browser.
- Component tests use jsdom (already a dependency) and the esbuild transform vite already ships; no new dependency.

## Fog

- Some browser-only checks (pixel geometry, CSS cascade) will lose coverage. Triage tickets list each one in docs/agents/testing.md so the owner can promote any back into the smoke set.

title: Speed up npm run verify: parallel runs, ignored output, no retries for known failures
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-p1k

## What to build

40 verify scripts write PNG screenshots and result JSON straight into docs/verification/ (411 files, 24 MB, tracked in Git). Every run rewrites them, so each Ralph ticket leaves dozens of changed binaries that get committed or must be restored by hand. Send all verify output to an ignored folder (.verify-output/) by default. Write to docs/verification/ only when VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1 is set, for release or design evidence.

Also make the full suite faster. Today it runs 84 browser scripts one at a time for about 20 minutes. verify-narrated-video-live (180s) and verify-smart-video-live (57s) need real narration or video providers but are not in the live skip set. Scripts that always fail (break-down-ui, compact-chat, different-version, narrated-playback, passage-selection, smart-video-live, video-library, video-recovery in the last run) are each retried once, costing double time.
design:
Add one shared helper under scripts/verify/lib/ that returns the output folder (docs/verification when VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, otherwise .verify-output) and creates it. Replace every hard-coded 'docs/verification' path in scripts/verify/ with it. Add .verify-output/ to .gitignore. Keep the existing tracked files in docs/verification/ as the last recorded evidence; do not delete them. Scripts that compare against a tracked baseline (for example large-map baselines) keep reading the baseline from docs/verification/.

verify-all runs scripts with a worker pool of min(4, cpus/2) by default (VERIFY_JOBS overrides; VERIFY_JOBS=1 restores serial order). Ports are already random (listen(0)). Before enabling the pool, give every script a unique agent-browser session (for example `<name>-${process.pid}`); about 20 scripts have no per-process session name. Print each result line when its script finishes and keep the final table in file order. Add the two *-live video scripts to the live set. For each script that still fails on the commit before this change, fix it if the cause is small, otherwise add it to known with the one-line reason, so it is not retried.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] grep finds no hard-coded docs/verification write path in scripts/verify/ outside the helper
- [ ] Running three verify scripts (for example verify-states, verify-settings-window, verify-video-player) leaves git status clean
- [ ] The same scripts with VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1 update docs/verification/ as before
- [ ] npm test passes
- [ ] npm run verify finishes in under 8 minutes on this machine, with no result change versus VERIFY_JOBS=1 except timing
- [ ] Every agent-browser script uses a per-process session name
- [ ] verify-narrated-video-live and verify-smart-video-live are in the live set
- [ ] Every remaining failure is in known with a reason; npm run verify reports no FAIL rows
notes:
Result (2026-11-13): verified.
- Output: scripts/verify/lib/output.mjs returns docs/verification with VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, else ignored .verify-output/. No hard-coded docs/verification write path left in scripts/verify (only 2 reads of the tracked narrated-video-native-codex.json input).
- verify-states, verify-settings-window and verify-video-player left git status clean. With VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, states + video-player updated 8 docs/verification files (restored afterwards).
- Pool: min(4, cpus/2) jobs, VERIFY_JOBS overrides. Every agent-browser script uses a pid session. Both *-live video scripts are in the live set.
- known is now a map of script to one-line reason (TreeTutor-cpi). Dropped smart-video-live (now live). verify-visual-sandbox and verify-tree-overview fail intermittently and stay known.
- Decision: verify-all puts an agent-browser wrapper first on PATH. Clicks go to lib/agent-browser-shim.mjs, which retries for up to 5s when agent-browser refuses a click because the control is covered (the map overlay during layout, the main flake under load). Other commands go straight to the real binary, because a Node start on every call made the Tab-loop script custom-endpoint go from 56s to over 300s. Tradeoff: running scripts by hand gets no retry.
- Decision: each script runs in its own process group (detached), and the group is killed on exit. A forked fixture server that outlived a timed-out custom-endpoint run kept stderr open and hung verify-all.
- Fixed load races in verify-inherited-context (it failed even serially), verify-contents-collapse, verify-map-message-jump and verify-visual-themes (the narrow-fit check ran before reflow).
- Timing: parallel full suite 211s and 198s (0 FAIL; 0 and 1 FLAKY). Serial VERIFY_JOBS=1 took 724s with the same pass/known/skip sets, apart from flakes (2 FLAKY plus the visual-themes race, since fixed; passed 3/3 afterwards). npm test: 246 pass, 0 fail. All fixture checks; no live providers.

title: Usage page redesign
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-2li

## What to build

The Usage page shows one range picker driving everything; the total with its input, output and cache read split, which doubles as the chart legend; the chart with a per period / cumulative switch; and one breakdown table that switches between by model and by task, with a share bar per row. Calls without reported counts are shown, never estimated. Same data as today. Matches the Usage mockup.
design: Follow docs/mockups/usage.html within the existing Paperback/Astryx surface. Keep the existing range API, local-calendar buckets, selected-year control and chart keyboard/text alternatives. Place one exact total above a split that doubles as the legend; keep chart and breakdown switches beside their headings. Use one breakdown table with six columns; Calls includes all attempts and labels unreported calls inline. Share bars divide reported row tokens by reported range tokens; unreported-only rows have dashes and zero reported share (no estimates). Pass existing server provider labels from Settings. Hide stale range results while a new selection loads, so total, chart and table always use the same response. Scope: UsageDashboard, Settings caller/copy, usage CSS, browser verification and its related Settings assertion; no storage/API/provider behavior change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Range, total, chart and breakdown agree for every range
- [x] Breakdown switches between model and task; each row shows its share
- [x] Unreported calls are labelled, never estimated
- [x] Usage dashboard verify script updated and passes in dark and light
notes:
Verified 2026-11-13. Implemented the Usage mockup using the existing range endpoints and accounting helpers. One exact total and measured split now form the chart legend; chart and single model/task breakdown switches sit beside their headings. Six-column table shows reported-token share bars and total calls with unreported attempts labelled inline. Unreported-only counts are dashed with zero reported share; chart announces missing counts without fabricated bars. Selected-year control, calendar ranges, exact hover/focus readouts, arrow/Home/End navigation and expandable values table remain. Existing server provider labels reach Usage through Settings (named endpoint fixture verified). Request selection guards hide stale results during range changes. No API/storage/provider changes or new dependencies.

Decisions/tradeoffs: exact figures rather than compact k values retain precision; shares use only reported tokens, so unreported attempts never imply token usage. Calls include measured plus unreported attempts. Desktop table fits all columns; narrow layout uses the existing Astryx keyboard-scrollable table instead of dropping data. Existing dark/light theme tokens and one-frame design retained.

Validation: npm run build passed (TypeScript plus Vite; existing large-chunk warning). npm test passed. node --test test/usage.test.mjs test/usage-ranges.test.mjs passed. node scripts/verify-usage-dashboard.mjs passed 17 recorded steps, dark/light at 1400x900 and390x844: Today/Week/Month/Year/All time totals and splits agree with per-period/cumulative charts and both breakdown groupings; exact shares, all tasks, named endpoints, previous-year selection/text values, keyboard/hover, desktop fit/narrow overflow containment, delayed response race, unreported-only and empty ranges, zero inference calls. node scripts/verify-settings-window.mjs passed12 steps including page navigation/deep links/focus/Escape and narrow Usage. git diff --check passed.

Enter the API key again so the saved key is never sent to a new host." Name uniqueness excludes self. test(id) lists models only, stores lastTest {ok,models,at}|{ok:false,error,at} in the owner-only endpoints file (survives restart); a result is dropped if the endpoint changed meanwhile. title: Settings redesign, model profiles and custom endpoints
description:
Owner feedback of 2026-11-13, settled in a grilling session. Settings becomes four pages, model profiles swap the three model roles at once, several named custom endpoints replace the single one, question bubbles follow the theme, surfaces follow one frame per object, and the quick thinking model keeps topics broad. Visual reference (done, not part of this epic): the mockups in docs/mockups (settings.html with its States section, usage.html, read.html, knowledge.html; the one-frame rule is written at the top of mock.css).

Tests use the existing seams only: the server HTTP seam (createApp with a temporary Store and fake providers, including the fake OpenAI-compatible server) and one browser verify script per UI ticket in the existing scripts/verify-* style, dark and light.

## Decisions so far

- Settings: separate pages Interface, Models, Connections, Usage; Map help and the Vim toggle merge into a Keyboard section.
- Model profile: named model plus effort for chat model default, smart model and quick thinking model. One always active; starts as "Default" from current settings; last one cannot be deleted. title: Knowledge map: topics as translucent regions
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Each topic is drawn as a translucent, labelled region around its concepts, so the learner sees which area is which. The layout pulls concepts toward their topics; a concept in several topics sits between them. No k-means: topics are the clusters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pure test: each concept lies inside the region of every topic it belongs to
- [ ] Region labels sit at region centres and stay readable in light and dark
- [ ] Verify script passes
design: Extend the existing d3-force layout and native concept buttons. Topic memberships define the clusters directly; sorted topic anchors sit on a circle, and each concept is attracted to the mean of its topics' anchors. Fixed anchors reserve centre-label space. Render each region as a padded circle about its anchor, with radius equal to the furthest member distance plus POINT_SPACE. This guarantees every member is inside every assigned topic. Circles may overlap and include nearby nonmembers; avoiding hull/cluster heuristics keeps geometry pure and small. Reuse theme series inks for translucent fills and opaque deep-field labels with primary text for light/dark contrast. Fit includes full regions; membership changes relayout, familiarity corrections preserve the viewport. No dependencies, schema/API changes, k-means or extra features.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure test: each concept lies inside the region of every topic it belongs to
- Region labels sit at region centres and stay readable in light and dark
- Verify script passes
notes:
Verified 2026-11-13. Implemented topic regions in src/knowledgeLayout.ts, src/KnowledgePage.tsx and src/layout.ts. Topic memberships are the clusters: deterministic sorted anchors, attraction to the average of all assigned topic anchors, and collision space reserved at each centre for labels. Each padded circular region encloses every member; shared concepts remain inside every assigned topic. Regions use the existing four theme series inks with translucent fills, behind links/points. Full topic names sit at exact region centres, use primary text on opaque deep-field ground, retain 14px screen size while zooming, and wrap at word boundaries (long tokens can wrap). Fit map includes complete regions; topic-only refresh invalidates layout; familiarity corrections preserve layout and viewport.

Acceptance evidence:
- test/knowledge-layout.test.mjs: all 5 pure tests pass; deterministic with reversed concept/link/topic order, non-overlap with isolated concepts, empty/single, containment including 5-topic membership and a concept with the same name as its topic, topic attraction and shared-concept placement.
- npm test: 253/253 pass, 0 skipped/failures.
- npm run build: TypeScript and Vite pass; existing large-chunk warning only. Final built assets confirmed current.
- node scripts/verify-knowledge.mjs: pass against production Chromium via agent-browser, isolated temporary SQLite Store and seeded graph/provider fixture; no live model calls. Verifies rendered member containment, translucent distinct theme inks, full region fit, centre alignment, no label/point overlap, DOM Range bounds and intact words (not just textContent), fixed screen text size, AA topic-label contrast 15.19 dark / 13.12 light, phone fit at 390px, topic-only membership refresh, and existing keyboard, pan/zoom, correction, merge/failure-retry and persistence flows. Evidence: docs/verification/knowledge-results.json, knowledge-verify-results.txt and updated knowledge*.png captures.
- Impeccable finish review: initial label truncation then split-word issue repaired; final disposition ship scores the sole label finding resolved at desktop and both phone fixtures. Documenter rechecked final styles: ordinary extension, no design-system changes. Detector ran once: existing 16px visual-viewer heading and turn-rail width transition findings only, outside Knowledge changes. Existing stale radius/card-era DESIGN.md/brief/sidecar prose left untouched.

Decision/tradeoff: padded circles intentionally overlap and may include nearby nonmembers; exact membership is authoritative, without k-means or hull heuristics. No dependency/schema/API changes. One browser attempt started before the rebuild completed and hit the stale-build guard; retried successfully only after confirming current assets. Validation is fixture browser + pure/integration tests, not native provider release evidence. Unrelated initial .beads/issues.jsonl changes preserved; no staging, Git commit, push or sync. Commit pending Ralph.

All 12 theme/Appearance pairs match host text and series ink in SVG and actual canvas pixels. System Appearance follows emulated OS changes. The same iframe window and script instance, Step 1 control state and saved visual source survive every switch; provider calls remain zero. A real ffmpeg-encoded 0.2-second solid-colour fixture MP4 retains exact HTTP-served bytes and saved metadata across every switch. Narrow 390px layout fits.

title: Start compaction when the branch form opens
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Opening the branch form on a passage starts compaction in the background, since compaction never sees the question. Closing the form cancels the run. Submitting reuses the finished or in-flight result, so the child usually goes straight to "Thinking…". If the parent gains a message before submit, the prepared result is discarded and compaction reruns. Every run, including cancelled ones, is recorded in Usage history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: prepare then submit makes exactly one compaction call
- [ ] Prepare then cancel aborts the call; no child is created
- [ ] Prepare, parent changes, submit: compaction reruns
- [ ] Usage history records the quick-thinking compaction calls
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: prepare then submit makes exactly one compaction call
- Prepare then cancel aborts the call; no child is created
- Prepare, parent changes, submit: compaction reruns
- Usage history records the quick-thinking compaction calls
- npm test passes
notes:
Done: compaction starts when the branch form opens.
Server (server/app.mjs): new POST /api/trees/:id/prepare (same anchor body as /branches minus the question; validated by the shared anchorOf helper) starts one quick-thinking compaction per parent, held in the in-memory `prepared` map {key, passage, controller, run}. POST /api/trees/:id/unprepare with the anchor aborts it only if it is for that passage, so a close that races the next form's prepare can't cancel the new run. POST /branches reuses the prepared run (finished or in flight) when key = JSON([compaction prompt, quick selection]) still matches. The prompt includes the parent's messages and the passage, so a new parent message, a different passage or changed quick-thinking settings all discard the run and compaction reruns. Tree delete and shutdown abort prepared runs. The compaction body is split into compact(prompt, quick, controller); startCompaction(child, ..., reuse) adopts the run's controller, so Stop/delete on the child still abort it.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx): an effect keyed on the branch parent and anchor (not the question) posts prepare on open and unprepare on cleanup. Cleanup after submit does nothing because /branches already took the entry.
Defaults: one prepared run per parent (a new form replaces it). A failed prepared run is never reused: reopening or submitting runs again. The tradeoff is one extra quick-thinking call after a failure, in exchange for a fresh attempt instead of a guaranteed failed child. Prepare errors are ignored on the client; submit reports them.
Evidence (fixtures, synthetic provider): test/branch.test.mjs new HTTP test covers: prepare+submit = exactly 1 compaction call and the child gets that snapshot; the compaction text has no question; cancel aborts the call and creates no child; closing another passage does not cancel; a parent message before submit aborts the prepared run and reruns it with the new message; /api/usage records all 4 compaction calls, cancelled ones included. npm test 241/241 pass; tsc clean.
Browser (fixture): new scripts/verify-branch-prepare.mjs PASS (form open starts compaction, Escape aborts it with no child, reopen+submit reuses the run, 2 calls both in Usage). verify-branch-first, verify-branch-streaming, verify-passage-popup, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-first-conversation all PASS. verify-compaction-retry was updated for the extra form-open call (failures 3, compactions 4) and PASSes. verify-visual-branch now counts tutor turns separately from form-open compaction and PASSes. Before this change (HEAD baseline): verify-passage-selection fails (element outside viewport) and verify-suggestion-branching fails (still expects a failed branch to create no child, obsolete since got.6). verify-chat-management and verify-passage-corrections are flaky on HEAD and still flaky here.

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

If compaction fails, the child stays open with an inline error explaining what failed and a Retry button. Retry runs compaction again and then answers the learner's question. The child is never silently answered without inherited context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: a failing fake compaction leaves the child saved, no tutor reply, and an error status readable from the child
- [ ] Retry endpoint or action reruns compaction then the reply; a second failure shows the error again
- [ ] Deleting the failed child still works
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: a failing fake compaction leaves the child saved, no tutor reply, and an error status readable from the child
- Retry endpoint or action reruns compaction then the reply; a second failure shows the error again
- Deleting the failed child still works
- npm test passes
notes:
Done (compaction failure keeps the child with Retry).
Server (server/app.mjs): extracted quickFor/compactionPrompt/startCompaction from POST /branches (same behaviour). A failed compaction stays in the compactions map with its error. GET /api/trees/:child returns compaction {status:'compacting'|'failed', error} while the snapshot is still '' (if no entry exists, e.g. after a restart: failed, 'context was not prepared. Retry to prepare it again.'). The child's first send still streams the compaction error as a failed empty reply, and the tutor is never called. Later plain sends return 409 (use Retry). POST /retry on a child with a failed or lost compaction rebuilds the prompt from the parent as it is now plus the saved passage, picks quick thinking again from the child's provider/model, starts compaction and then streams compacting -> thinking -> reply. A repeat failure shows the error again. A missing parent gets 409.
Defaults/tradeoffs: Retry reads the parent's current messages rather than the original snapshot input (the prompt isn't stored, and this also works after a restart). quickFor's 502 text no longer says 'Focused chat not created' because it is shared with Retry.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx): the failed-reply status line shows tree.compaction.error plus 'The focused chat is kept; no reply was written without its context.' next to the existing Retry reply button.
Evidence (fixture provider, no live inference): new HTTP test in test/branch.test.mjs checks a failed compaction (child saved, compaction.error readable on GET, no tutor call, empty failed reply), a 409 on a plain send, a second failure via retry, a successful retry (compacting<thinking<answer, snapshot received) and deleting a failed child. npm test: 240/240 pass. Browser: new scripts/verify-compaction-retry.mjs on the built UI PASS (inline error x2 with Retry, then answer). scripts/verify-branch-first.mjs still PASS.

title: Branch first: open the child at once, then compact (happy path)
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Submitting a branch question opens the child conversation immediately, showing the passage and the learner's question bubble, with a status line "Compacting parent context…", then "Thinking…", then the streaming reply. The waiting time is the same, but nothing appears frozen. The child row and branch are saved before compaction finishes; its inherited context is filled in once compaction completes and is fixed from then on. The composer stays locked until the reply starts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: POST branches returns the child before a held fake compaction finishes; the child is listed in /api/state
- [ ] The child's first reply starts only after compaction finishes and receives the compacted inherited context
- [ ] Stream or state shows a compacting status before thinking/streaming
- [ ] Verify script or manual check: the child opens within one frame of submit and shows the status line sequence
- [ ] Existing branch tests updated and passing; npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: POST branches returns the child before a held fake compaction finishes; the child is listed in /api/state
- The child's first reply starts only after compaction finishes and receives the compacted inherited context
- Stream or state shows a compacting status before thinking/streaming
- Verify script or manual check: the child opens within one frame of submit and shows the status line sequence
- Existing branch tests updated and passing; npm test passes
notes:
Done (branch-first, happy path).
Server (server/app.mjs, store.mjs): POST /branches validates as before (anchor, parent model/effort, quick-thinking selection), builds the compaction prompt from the parent at that moment, saves the child + branch row with snapshot '' and returns 201 at once. Compaction runs detached in an in-memory map `compactions` (child -> {controller, done, settled, error}); store.compacted() writes the snapshot only WHERE snapshot='' (fixed once). /api/state lists `compacting` child ids. The child's messages stream sends saved -> status "compacting" -> (awaits compaction) -> status "thinking" -> reply; the reply receives the reloaded branch with the compacted snapshot. Stop/delete/shutdown abort the compaction. Parent is no longer active during compaction.
Defaults chosen: '' as pending-snapshot marker (no schema migration; column is NOT NULL). Failure path minimal until TreeTutor-got.7: child kept, its first reply fails with "Context preparation failed. <reason>..."; a child left with '' and no running compaction (e.g. after restart) gets 409 on send. got.7 adds Retry.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx, turn.ts): submitBranch opens the child from the POST response (no extra GET), then sends the question and refreshes concurrently; reply bubble shows "Compacting parent context…" / "Thinking…" from status events; composer stays locked (active) until the reply ends.
Evidence (fixture provider, no live inference): new HTTP test in test/branch.test.mjs holds compaction: POST returns child with empty snapshot, child listed in /api/state with compacting=[child], stream shows compacting before thinking before reply text, provider gets snapshot only after release. Existing tests updated via test/branch-first.mjs compacted() helper (branch, chat-defaults, credential-boundary, openai, visual-branch); old 502-on-compaction-failure assertions now assert kept child + failed first reply. npm test: 232/232 pass (twice).
Browser: new scripts/verify-branch-first.mjs (built UI, held fake compaction) PASS x4: child opens 20-25 ms after submit (branch POST 6-9 ms, rest is React mounting the chat, i.e. the first paint after the response), status lines Compacting parent context… -> Thinking… -> Focused answer., composer locked while waiting, snapshot filled after release. Tradeoff: no optimistic client-side placeholder child; strict <16.7 ms would need one. scripts/verify-passage-popup.mjs: removed its old "compaction failure keeps popup, no branch" step (behaviour replaced; got.7 should add failure checks) -> PASS. Also PASS: verify-first-conversation, map-identity, subtree-folding, branch-streaming, inherited-context, keyboard-journey (flaky once), contents (flaky once). verify-passage-selection fails identically on a HEAD baseline build (viewport click), unrelated. Regenerated docs/verification screenshots restored to HEAD except passage-popup-ui.json (check text changed).

title: Compaction keeps the passage area and visual descriptions
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Inherited context keeps what the learner branched from. The compaction prompt asks for the sentences around the passage in detail while the rest of the parent is compressed. Visual, diagram and video requests in the parent reach compaction as one line "[Visual: title — description]" (Diagram/Video likewise), never as code or JSON, so a child can ask about a visual. The learner's new question is still never sent to compaction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: the captured compaction request contains the new passage-detail instruction
- [ ] A parent reply with a visual request reaches compaction as "[Visual: <title> — <description>]" and contains no request JSON or visual code
- [ ] The branch question is absent from the compaction request
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: the captured compaction request contains the new passage-detail instruction
- A parent reply with a visual request reaches compaction as "[Visual: <title> — <description>]" and contains no request JSON or visual code
- The branch question is absent from the compaction request
- npm test passes
notes: Done. compactionMessages (server/diagrams.mjs) replaces tutorContext for compaction: completed messages only; each pending/ready artifact of the parent becomes one line "[Visual|Diagram|Video: title — description]" at its stored reply position (null -> end). Failed/canceled/interrupted media omitted (matches earlier failed-artifact privacy test). Artifact ids dropped from compaction: child cannot open parent artifacts anyway. COMPACT prompt now asks for close detail around the passage, compression elsewhere, and explains the media lines. Tests: new HTTP test in test/visuals.test.mjs (real visual block via fake providers; asserts instruction, exact marker line, no JSON/intent/SVG/branch question); artifacts + videos tests updated to the marker form. npm test: 231 pass, 0 fail (fixture providers, no live model).

title: Anchor the child conversation prompt to its passage
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

A child asked "what is this?" explains the passage. For Claude, Codex and custom endpoint providers, the child's system prompt states that the learner's first message asks about the selected passage, that "this", "it" and "that" refer to the passage unless the learner says otherwise, and that the tutor should explain the passage even if the inherited context says it was skipped. Seen live on 2026-11-13: passage "DKIM signing details", question "what is this", and the tutor did not connect them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test per provider seam (fake provider or fake OpenAI endpoint capturing the request): a child's first turn includes the passage and the new instruction
- [ ] Root conversations do not get the instruction
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test per provider seam (fake provider or fake OpenAI endpoint capturing the request): a child's first turn includes the passage and the new instruction
- Root conversations do not get the instruction
- npm test passes
notes: Implemented 2026-11-13. server/diagrams.mjs exports tutorSystem(tree), now used by claude.mjs, codex.mjs, openai.mjs (was 3 copies). Branch trees get: first message asks about the selected passage; "this"/"it"/"that" mean the passage unless the learner says otherwise; explain it even if inherited context says it was skipped. Roots unchanged. Decision: one shared builder so the 3 providers cannot drift. Evidence (fixtures, no live model call): test/child-prompt.test.mjs, an HTTP test through createApp per provider: Claude (stream-json protocol fixture, --system-prompt), Codex (app-server fixture, thread/start baseInstructions), custom endpoint (fake OpenAI, system message). Root turn has no instruction; the child first turn "what is this" has the instruction plus snapshot+selectedPassage. npm test: 239/239 pass.

title: End the turn when the reply text ends, not when visuals finish
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

While a visual or diagram is still generating, the learner can already act: Responding clears, suggestions are picked, and branching works. The server sends done and removes the tree from active as soon as the reply text is complete, then lets visual jobs finish on their own. The focused chat shows each pending visual with its own progress in place and swaps in the result (or failure card) when its job ends, without a reload. Suggestions ignore visual and video content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: with a visual job held open by a fake provider, the message stream ends with done, the tree is not in active in /api/state, and POST branches does not return 409
- [ ] Suggestions run before the held visual finishes
- [ ] When the held visual is released it becomes ready and the client view shows it without a reload (verify script or state-polling test)
- [ ] A visual that times out after the turn ended shows its failure card; the reply stays completed
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: with a visual job held open by a fake provider, the message stream ends with done, the tree is not in active in /api/state, and POST branches does not return 409
- Suggestions run before the held visual finishes
- When the held visual is released it becomes ready and the client view shows it without a reload (verify script or state-polling test)
- A visual that times out after the turn ended shows its failure card; the reply stays completed
- npm test passes
notes: Done 2026-11-13. server/app.mjs: per-reply visual queue (still max 3) now starts each visual through startDrawing(artifact, streamSignal), the detached job runner used by Retry. The message stream no longer waits for visual jobs: done is sent and the tree leaves active when the reply text ends. Stop during streaming still cancels pending visuals (cancelVisuals plus the parent-signal abort); after done, only delete or shutdown stop them. Detached jobs show up in /api/state videos, so the existing ChatPage polling (1.5 s tree refetch) swaps in ready or failed cards without a reload. Suggestions already get only the stripped reply text. Tradeoff: no new per-visual progress UI; the existing pending shimmer is reused. Evidence (fixtures, no live provider): new test/visual-detach.test.mjs (held visual: stream ends with done, tree not active, state.videos holds the tree, branches returns 201, suggestion call made before release with no visual content, release becomes ready via polling; timeout after done gives failed + "timed out" while the reply stays completed). It hangs against HEAD app.mjs. Two visuals.test.mjs tests now wait for the visual to settle after done. npm test 236/236 passed; build OK; scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs (fixture) all PASS, including Stop aborting workers.

title: Parse tag-style visual, diagram and video requests
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

A tutor reply that wraps its request JSON as <treetutor-visual>{json}</treetutor-visual> (or treetutor-diagram / treetutor-video) becomes a visual, diagram or video exactly like the fenced ```treetutor-visual form. Small typos in the opening tag, such as a stray quote (<treetutor-video">) or spaces, are tolerated. A block whose JSON cannot be read shows the existing "request could not be read" failure card with Retry instead of raw text. The tutor prompt keeps asking for the fenced form. Seen live with the opencode model on 2026-11-13: both tags showed as raw text and no video artifact was created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: a reply containing the tag-style visual block from the epic notes creates a visual artifact at that position and the raw tag text is not in the saved reply
- [ ] Same for <treetutor-video"> with a stray quote and for treetutor-diagram
- [ ] Tag-style block with broken JSON produces the unreadable-request card, not raw text
- [ ] Existing fenced-form tests still pass
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: a reply containing the tag-style visual block from the epic notes creates a visual artifact at that position and the raw tag text is not in the saved reply
- Same for <treetutor-video"> with a stray quote and for treetutor-diagram
- Tag-style block with broken JSON produces the unreadable-request card, not raw text
- Existing fenced-form tests still pass

notes: Implemented: server/diagrams.mjs diagramReply accepts tag form <treetutor-visual|diagram|video>{json}</...> alongside fences; opening/closing tag tolerate stray quotes/whitespace; streaming hides a partial '<treetutor-' prefix. Tag blocks have no header so 'extra' is empty. Prompt unchanged (still asks for fence). Evidence (fixture HTTP test test/tag-requests.test.mjs): visual, '< "treetutor-diagram" >', '<treetutor-video">' each create one artifact at position 8, raw tag absent from stream and saved reply; broken JSON -> failed 'Visual request could not be read: the request was not valid JSON'. npm test 234/234 pass. title: Smoother tutoring flow, themes and knowledge map
description:
Owner feedback of 2026-11-13, settled in a grilling session. Make the tutoring flow feel smoother (no waiting on branches or visuals), fix requests shown as raw text, fix children that lose track of their passage, and give the app rounder corners, predefined themes and a knowledge map.

## Notes

Tests use the existing seams only: the server HTTP seam (createApp with a fake provider and a temporary Store, as in the branch and visuals tests), pure module tests (layout, theme tokens), and one browser verify script per UI item in the existing scripts/verify-* style.

## Decisions so far

- Visuals and diagrams get 300 s; video composition gets 600 s. Render and narration budgets already scale with length and stay.
- A turn ends when the reply text ends. Visuals generate in place on their own; they never hold Responding, suggestions or branching.
- Compaction sees each visual or video only as "[Visual: title — description]" so the learner can ask about it in a child; never its code.
- The child's system prompt says its first learner message asks about the passage ("this"/"it" mean the passage) and to explain it even if the parent skipped it. Compaction keeps the sentences around the passage in detail and compresses the rest.
- The request parser accepts the fenced form and the tag-style form (<treetutor-visual>{json}</treetutor-visual>, same for diagram and video), tolerating stray quotes or spaces in the opening tag. Unreadable JSON shows the existing "request could not be read" card with Retry, never raw text. The prompt still asks for the fence.
- Branch first: the child opens at once with passage and question; a status line goes "Compacting parent context…", "Thinking…", then streaming. Compaction failure keeps the child with an inline error and Retry.
- Compaction starts when the branch form opens (it never sees the question); closing the form cancels it; submit reuses it.
- New chat saves nothing until the first send. Existing empty learning trees are removed once at startup.
- Contents collapses with a left chevron at its top-left into a thin rail with a right chevron; saved per browser.
- Clicking any question or reply bubble in a conversation node opens that message at the top of the focused chat. The focused chat gets a right-edge turn rail with one tick per learner question.
- Radii: inner 6 px, element 8 px, container 12 px, page 16 px, chat bubbles 16 px, pills stay full.
- Themes (glossary: Theme, separate from Appearance): Paperback (default), Forest, Harbor, Dusk, Ember, Graphite, each light and dark; picked from swatch cards in Settings → Interface; saved per browser; bubble tint uses the theme's inks; visuals receive the theme palette; rendered videos keep their colours.
- Knowledge view becomes a pannable, zoomable force-layout map: concept points with familiarity rings, concept link lines, topics as translucent labelled regions (no k-means), concept labels hidden when zoomed out, existing detail panel on click.

- TreeTutor-got.16: Ember (terracotta/gold) and Graphite (gray/cobalt), both light/dark, are implemented and verified: full tests/build, token parity/AA and production browser swatch/application/reload/tint/Appearance/narrow checks pass; six new theme captures retained.

## Fog

- The owner's 9router/opencode proxy appears to inject its own coding-agent system prompt; TreeTutor cannot control it and was not inspected.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Decisions so far — TreeTutor-got.15: Harbor (slate/teal) and Dusk (plum/violet) reuse the existing theme picker with both variants, Paperback default, existing tint slots and house geometry. All 246 tests, build, theme freshness, picker/Appearance browser checks pass; production UI evidence uses isolated fixtures. Implementation commit remains pending with Ralph.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Decisions so far — TreeTutor-got.17: visuals receive current theme/Appearance; prompt palettes derive from generated Astryx CSS. Existing frames recolour in place (including canvas redraw event) and keep learner controls; encoded video bytes stay fixed. All 251 tests, production build, 12-pair browser matrix and original sandbox verification pass. Fixture evidence is recorded in the child; no native provider inference required. Ralph commit pending.

title: Redesign finish review and DESIGN.md
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-y36 (spec: the redesign mockup and its surface contract)

## What to build

Close out the redesign the way the direction contract requires: run the Impeccable finish review against the contract and the mockup, fix material findings, record the verdict, write DESIGN.md from the shipped app and update the shipped surface contract so it describes Paperback Series instead of Lecture-hall Slate. Every shipping raster carries its provenance.

- [ ] Finish review verdict recorded on the epic, with any skipped findings named.
- [ ] DESIGN.md and the shipped surface contract describe the shipped design.
- [ ] Matches the named mockup screen in both the dark default and the light appearance.
- [ ] Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast in both appearances; every control is keyboard reachable with a visible paper-coloured focus ring.
- [ ] No current label, action or failure state is lost.

notes:
Verified result (2026-11-13): Impeccable finish review of the Paperback Series redesign. Verdict SHIP after two fix rounds. Record: docs/verification/finish-review.md.
- Full review (fresh finish-reviewer, code-led; the critique reference was the paperback-seasonal sketch plus mockup captures): disposition fix, 7 findings. Ground, type, material, band, Contents, Read inks, Library, narrow and dialogs match.
- Fixed: (1) The docked map pane kept the full Map view's viewport, so the tree landed off-pane. src/TreeOverview.tsx now watches the canvas width. When the Map/Read switch or the seam resizes an untouched map, it refits the whole tree with a 75% zoom floor (40% was unreadable, verdict 1 partial) and then re-reveals the selected node. A navigated map keeps its exact viewport, which verify-canvas-navigation and verify-chat-expand enforce; a first centre-shift attempt broke them and was removed. Saved viewports restore on reload as before. (6) The Knowledge/Videos Return row sits on the 70rem content column, and secondary actions there are outlined hairline buttons (src/layout.ts).

(3,4) Settings small-caps labels, segmented Appearance and swatch row: accepted in y36.9's own review. (5) Root heading: not a defect, it renders and the column opens scrolled to the latest reply. (7) The idle "Saved" label was dropped by decision in y36.3; the composer hint was removed before the redesign (dx0.1).
- Verdict 2: fix 1 resolved, no regressions, ship (scope: the scored fixes only).
- DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json overwritten from the shipped build by the impeccable-documenter. Decision: overwrite, not merge, because Slate was replaced wholesale. The detector against the new DESIGN.md leaves only the documented 16px .visual-viewer h2 one-off. The documenter flagged drift it did not canonise: Astryx neutral leftovers (purple text slot, red/orange/teal/cyan badges, blue info, default success/warning, --shadow-inset-*).
- Shipped surface contract .impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md rewritten for Paperback Series (direction, per-screen rules, kept behaviour notes). The mockup brief now points to it.
- Provenance: impeccable embed-prompt --scan dist src reports 0 rasters, 0 missing. The app ships no rasters.
Evidence (production build, seeded SQLite fixture, synthetic provider, agent-browser Chromium; no native model call): capture-finish dark/light at 1440x900 and 390x844. Saved as docs/verification/finish-*-{dark,light}-desktop.png and finish-2-chat-{dark,light}-narrow.png. npm test 223/223; npm run build passes (existing chunk-size advisory); tsc clean; git diff --check clean. Verify scripts PASS: layout-restore, canvas-navigation, canvas-positions, chat-divider, chat-expand, focused-chat-layout, map-identity, full-map, knowledge, contents, narrow (AA text and a paper focus ring in both appearances), vim-bindings, library, large-map, map-gestures, keyboard-journey. map-identity was stale since y36.10 (it waited for the removed "Start a learning tree" copy) and now waits for "Your first tree starts with a question.". Scripts refreshed their own captures under docs/verification (contents, knowledge, full-map, focused-chat).

title: Narrow layout
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-y36 (spec: the redesign mockup and its surface contract)

## What to build

At phone width the app shows Read as a single column, the contents outline as a drawer and the map as its own view, with the band condensed. Nothing scrolls sideways. Mockup screen: Narrow.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At 390px no screen scrolls horizontally.
- [ ] The contents drawer opens and closes by keyboard and returns focus.
- [ ] Matches the named mockup screen in both the dark default and the light appearance.
- [ ] Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast in both appearances; every control is keyboard reachable with a visible paper-coloured focus ring.
- [ ] No current label, action or failure state is lost.
- [ ] npm test and npm run build pass; existing verification scripts that touch this surface are updated and pass; dark and light screenshots saved under docs/verification.
notes:
Verified result (2026-11-13): narrow layout at <=48rem (mockup Narrow).
- Band condenses to Contents (bars), TreeTutor wordmark (17px), Search learning trees, New chat (icon). The tree switcher, view tabs and gear move into an Astryx Drawer (side start, 320px, modal): Read, Map, Library, Knowledge, Videos; the open tree's Contents outline (figures and context meter included); and Settings. Choosing anything in the drawer closes it. Escape, Close and scrim return focus to the Contents button. Settings opened from the drawer returns focus there too.
- Read is one full-width column with no inline Contents. The Map stays its own full-width view (unchanged). The map-layout failure alert keeps its Retry and wraps onto a second band row instead of scrolling sideways.
- Removed: the old in-column Contents toggle (orphaned by the drawer; Contents.tsx no longer has expanded state), the rule that hid the wordmark on narrow screens, and a stale chat-header left indent left over from the old sidebar toggle.
- Decisions/tradeoffs: on narrow screens the tree switcher's "<title> · Learning trees" button becomes the drawer's Library entry, and the tree title shows in the Contents head (mockup). The drawer mounts only at narrow width because Astryx keeps drawer children mounted while closed. Crossing the breakpoint closes the drawer. title: Conversation addresses and branch family inks
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-y36 (spec: the redesign mockup and its surface contract)

## What to build

Every conversation in a learning tree has an address: the trunk is 1, its children 1.1, 1.2, and so on down (1.1.2). Each first-level branch family takes one series ink in order (amber, leaf, rust, lichen, then repeats) and every descendant keeps its family's ink; the trunk wears paper. On the current screens, the passage underline and its address chip, the branch line on the map and the conversation node band all show the family ink. Address and ink come from one shared pure function with a test, so every later screen reads the same answer. Mockup screens: Read and Map.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A test covers addresses and inks for a trunk, more than four families (ink repeats) and deep descendants.
- [ ] Addresses stay stable when a sibling is added after them, and the order rule for siblings is written down in the GLOSSARY.
- [ ] Passage underline, address chip, branch line and node band of one family share one ink.
- [ ] Matches the named mockup screen in both the dark default and the light appearance.
- [ ] Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast in both appearances; every control is keyboard reachable with a visible paper-coloured focus ring.
- [ ] No current label, action or failure state is lost.
- [ ] npm test and npm run build pass; existing verification scripts that touch this surface are updated and pass; dark and light screenshots saved under docs/verification.
notes:
Result (2026-11-12): conversationAddresses(trees) in src/treeList.ts is the one pure source of address + family ink (0 = trunk/paper, 1-4 = series ink cycling amber, leaf, rust, lichen); inkStyle(ink) sets --ink/--ink-on. Siblings are ordered by created then id, so a later sibling never renumbers earlier ones (GLOSSARY: Address, Branch family; deleting a branch renumbers its later siblings).
- Read: explored passage underline wears --ink; an aria-hidden address chip (sup.passage-address) follows the underline as a sibling with zero-width atomic data-o/data-e, so selection offsets, highlights and u.textContent are unchanged. The explored aria-label now ends ", <address>".
- Map: the conversation node header is a full-width ink band (node-band) with the address; branch lines and the focused branch take the family ink (focused branch is still wider). Trunk band = paper.
- Decisions/tradeoffs: inside a node band the focus ring uses --ink-on (paper-ink on the trunk band), because a paper ring would vanish on the paper trunk band, the same rule the mockup uses for the shell band. The address text is full opacity because amber light at 0.8 opacity measured 4.31:1 (<AA). Band ink-on vs ink measured AA 5.71-16.1 in both appearances.
Evidence (fixtures, built app, agent-browser): npm test 217/217 pass (new: tree-list addresses/inks incl. 5 families, deep descendants, later siblings; markdown chip/ink/offsets). npm run build passes. verify-map-identity updated (ink/address assertions, Read check) and passes; screenshots docs/verification/map-reference-{dark,light}.png and read-inks-{dark,light}.png. verify-canvas-positions updated (ignores chip text in prefix counts) and passes. title: Paperback Series redesign (Seasonal Inks)
description:
Bring the shipped app to the Paperback Series redesign, Seasonal Inks colourway, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-12. The static mockup of every screen and component lives in docs/mockups/ (open index.html; tick Component labels to see each part's name). The direction contract is .impeccable/surfaces/docs-mockups-index-html.md.

## Notes

A learning tree is a volume. The trunk wears paper; each first-level branch family takes one series ink (amber, leaf, rust, lichen, repeating), shared by its passage underline, address chip, branch line and conversation node band. Conversations carry addresses (1, 1.1, 1.1.2). Leaf green is the only action colour, paper is focus, rose red is failure only. The reply owns the centre. No behaviour is removed.

## Decisions so far

- Phase label reuses phase:ui-refresh.
- The shared foundation (theme tokens, fonts, addresses and inks, the shell band) lands before any screen.

## Fog

- No model context-window size exists today; the contents context meter needs one (see its ticket).
notes:
Contents context-window source (TreeTutor-y36.5): use native per-model runtime metadata, not a guessed static alias table. Claude: a single entry in result.modelUsage supplies contextWindow (server/claude.mjs); Codex: thread/tokenUsage/updated.tokenUsage.modelContextWindow (server/codex.mjs). The server accepts only positive safe integers and records the limit on the completed reply with its provider and resolved model (messages.usage JSON, no schema migration). Numerator is the last completed tutor call input + cacheRead + output, not cumulative cost or suggestion/media usage. Display is explicitly Last completed reply. Missing count is unavailable; missing/ambiguous limit or a different current provider/model means measured tokens only, no percentage or bar. Tradeoff: historical replies and custom endpoints without reported window metadata remain tokens-only until a matching measured reply; native session compaction, unsent text and future prompt overhead are not predicted. Protocol-shaped fixture coverage exercises both CLI adapters and SQLite/HTTP persistence; this is not a fresh native-provider evidence claim.
Finish review verdict (TreeTutor-y36.12, 2026-11-13): SHIP after two fix rounds. Fixed: the docked map refits untouched maps with a 75% floor, and the Knowledge/Videos column alignment and outlined secondary buttons. Skipped findings (reasons accepted by the reviewer): top-down orthogonal map, Contents on Map and Read-address return (PRD map behaviour, y36.7); Settings small-caps, segmented Appearance and swatch row (y36.9 review); root heading (not a defect); 'Saved' label (y36.3 decision) and composer hint (removed pre-redesign). DESIGN.md rewritten from the build; shipped contract .impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md now Paperback; 0 shipping rasters. Record: docs/verification/finish-review.md.
