notes:
Verified TreeTutor-egp.4 (2026-11-15). All issue acceptance checks pass.

Implementation and routine decisions:
- server/tools/searxng.mjs uses the current managed instance by default; only an explicit custom instance override is persisted in SQLite (new searxng_settings row). Saving the displayed managed port keeps the override NULL, so later ephemeral managed ports follow automatically. Settings-only HTTP(S) base URLs allow local/private instances intentionally but refuse embedded credentials, query and fragment. Model arguments supply only a query, never the server URL.
- Settings > Connections > Search displays the selected URL with Save search URL, Test search and Use app-managed instance. Test runs a JSON search on the draft without saving. Errors distinguish disabled/non-JSON output (including SearXNG's HTTP 403), other HTTP failures, invalid results and network failure; managed startup reasons remain readable. Initial settings-load failure has Retry. Errors use the house rose token. Explicit test-result success feedback follows this issue's requirement over the general silence-on-success guidance.
- Default runner offers web_search/find_images only after a successful JSON search probe on each capable turn. Custom endpoints retain read_page while search is unavailable. Native provider lists only receive app find_images when capable and search is reachable, preserving provider-owned web search. Actual Claude/Codex app-tool delivery remains egp.3; their current adapters stay unchanged. No cache/background poll: one extra constant-query probe per capable turn trades latency for avoiding stale readiness. Requests have a 30s budget, 5 MiB response bound, 2000-character query limit and 10-result output; Stop aborts transport. No new dependency.
- Web results contain title/url/snippet. Image-category results contain imageUrl/thumbnail/title/sourceUrl. Tool description requests standard linked Markdown image syntax. Saved successful image results also supply credit links for plain Markdown images. Image/reference rendering keeps source offsets and old syntax-only reveal, avoids nested anchors, rejects non-HTTP(S)/credential URLs, uses lazy loading/no-referrer and retains source links after an app 'Image is no longer available' placeholder replaces a failed image. Empty-alt image links have an accessible name. CSP now allows HTTP(S) reply images; visual/player sandbox policies remain unchanged. Images load directly, with no saved copies. Resources database/citation UI remains later scope.

Its child served http://127.0.0.1:45143; createApp with the default runner and a fresh temporary store served http://127.0.0.1:45697. The saved override was unset. This verifies managed service + real custom endpoint; the prerequisite egp.7 already owns native npm-start provisioning evidence.

3. Fake SearXNG runner tests prove provider-specific lists, images category, encoded queries, result shapes/filtering/cap, unavailable hiding and recovery, JSON-disabled/HTML/schema/HTTP/network diagnoses, validation and Stop closing a held request. HTTP boundary tests prove managed defaults, draft Test without saving, custom override persistence/reopen/no managed fallback/reset, unchanged sandbox CSP and the default runner's real function-calling transport with a fake OpenAI model and stored tool results.

Markdown/component tests prove image/reference links, source mapping, unsafe URLs, raw offsets/reveal, broken-image placeholder/source retention, empty-alt naming, Settings loading/success/errors/save/reset and load Retry. These use synthetic URLs/error events; no native browser appearance claimed.

title: App tools for Claude and Codex
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Delivery to providers".

## What to build

Serve the runner's tools over a localhost streamable HTTP MCP server built with the official MCP SDK; each turn gets a fresh secret token sent as a header, bound to the turn context and revoked at turn end; requests without a live token are refused. Claude, when tools are on: allow its own WebSearch and WebFetch plus the app MCP tools it lacks, drop the single-turn limit, keep strict MCP config, no setting sources and no slash commands. Codex, when tools are on: web search live, register the app MCP server for read_page and the other app tools; shell, patch, JS REPL, apps and skills stay off, sandbox read-only; usage sums every model call of the turn. First verify the installed Codex CLI supports streamable HTTP MCP; otherwise use a stdio bridge to the same runner.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Claude and Codex replies can search the web and call app tools; tool events reach the reply
- [x] MCP requests without a live per-turn token are refused; tokens die at turn end
- [x] Codex usage counts all model calls of a tool turn
- [x] With tools off both adapters send their old arguments
- [x] Adapter tests with the protocol fixture cover arguments, config and events; MCP server tests cover token checks
notes:
Verified result (2026-11-15): all TreeTutor-egp.3 acceptance checks pass. Native evidence: docs/verification/tutor-tools-native.json. Implementation remains local on master; no staging, commit, push, pull or sync. Ralph owns the commit.

Implementation and decisions:
- Official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.2, pinned in package/lock. One lazy app-owned streamable HTTP MCP listener on 127.0.0.1, stateless per-request SDK transport. Uses the SDK low-level Server to preserve the runner's existing authoritative JSON Schemas, validated through its AJV provider.
- Each native app-tool turn registers a cryptographically random 256-bit Bearer header bound to that turn's offered definitions, runner closure, conversation/reply and abort signal. Missing/wrong/ended tokens get 401. Revocation happens on completion, error, startup failure or Stop; active requests and tools abort. Unknown/unoffered tools and invalid arguments are refused. Host and Origin checks prevent browser/DNS-rebinding access; no CORS. MCP credentials are redacted from runner events and results.
- App-owned MCP lifetime is closed on app shutdown. Tools remain chat-only; isolated quick/smart/media calls retain their tool-free behavior. Native providers are tool-capable; model/tool switches remain the separate egp.2 deliverable. An absent nativeTools flag and empty/absent app tool list keep the adapters' old launch arguments.
- Claude enables only its built-in WebSearch/WebFetch plus specifically allowed app MCP names, removes --max-turns 1 and keeps strict MCP config, empty setting sources and disabled slash commands. Native WebSearch/WebFetch and runner tool events reach the existing reply stream/activity storage. Claude gets app find_images when SearXNG is ready; its native fetch replaces read_page.
- Codex receives live native web search and the app MCP tools (read_page plus find_images when ready). Each tool turn uses a fresh app-server subprocess and resumes its saved thread. This small startup cost guarantees fresh headers and isolates simultaneous turns without changing runtime config on a loaded thread. Tools-off uses the existing client and arguments. Shell, patch, JS REPL, code mode and apps remain disabled; thread sandbox stays read-only and approvalPolicy never. Unsolicited server-initiated tool/approval requests remain refused.
- Native probing showed that this installed Codex needs supports_standalone_web_search=true on the app's subscription provider plus features.standalone_web_search=true for native live search. Its app MCP server needs default_tools_approval_mode=approve; this applies only to the explicitly offered, authenticated app tools. Neither change broadens filesystem permissions or grants third-party approval. features.skills is ignored by Codex 0.169.0, so tool turns also disable skills.include_instructions, skills.bundled and skill_search. Native rollout inspection confirmed no skills instructions block.
- Codex usage uses the thread total minus a baseline established from the first current-turn total/last update, counting every model call without duplicating repeated notifications or including earlier turns. Cumulative snapshots also preserve reported usage on failure/Stop. Tools-off keeps last-call behavior. Claude continues using its aggregate result usage.
- Tool activity updates now persist completed streamed arguments, rather than retaining the initial empty native tool input. Both provider-native web events and app runner events include status/output/timing. Missing native Codex search result text remains unavailable; action metadata is retained instead of invented.

Native verification (real installed CLIs, no model/protocol fixtures):
- Codex 0.169.0 advertises streamable HTTP in mcp add --help. A real app-server discovered this SDK server as connected/bearerToken and called read_page over HTTP with a synthetic runner, without inference. A stdio bridge is unnecessary for this installed CLI.
- Claude Code 2.1.325 / Haiku: native WebSearch and app find_images both completed using actual managed SearXNG a7128d5d1d5af2837a68fbeaaee9c3e8391aa9cf. Model answered with the official Python site and found logo images. Native usage: input 6940, output 197, cacheRead 3476.
- Codex / gpt-6.1-terra: native web_search and app read_page of https://www.python.org/about/ both completed. Three reported model calls summed to input 18222, output 164, cacheRead 8960. The real page's returned text includes its public fallback; no page contents or model fact-checking beyond tool delivery are claimed.
- Both native providers resumed their actual saved sessions in a new process and successfully called the app tools again with new MCP connections. Resumed-turn totals exclude previous-turn usage. Auth stayed in its existing app-owned directory, protected by the existing lock; no credentials relocated.
- Earlier native Codex attempts exposed missing approval/search configuration. Both task-owned defects were fixed and the final native checks passed; no quota/auth failures were used as blockers.

Automated verification:
- test/providers/native-tools.test.mjs: 9 checks pass, covering tools-on/off CLI arguments/config, events and result text, startup failure, Stop, token rotation, concurrent Codex runners, reply stream/persistence and full usage totals.
- test/tools/mcp.test.mjs: SDK clients exercise token refusal, Host/Origin checks, per-turn context isolation, offered-tool/schema checks, revocation, secret redaction, tool failures and cancellation. Store tests prove streamed input updates, persistence and deletion.
- Focused provider, endpoint loop, image, effort, usage and runner tests pass. Updated stale prompt and single-process fixture assertions; fixture thread IDs are now unique across subprocesses. All six cross-provider switches and isolated diagram/video adapter boundaries pass after these fixture updates. No media rendering implementation changed.
- npm test -- --test-concurrency=2 was run at the end, then rerun after repairing task-related stale tests. Final run: 554 passed, 5 opt-in skips, 2 unrelated failures. The unchanged video-audit cancellation fixture stalled with a canceled artifact and was terminated after 107 seconds so the suite could finish; its standalone bounded rerun passed all 5 tests in 1.45 seconds. The other failure is token-lint reporting raw color rgb( in the concurrently added src/shell/ThemedFavicon.tsx comment. All task-related tests passed in the final full run. First-run timing failures during a simultaneous production build passed in the focused and final runs.
- npm run build passed (tsc and Vite; existing large-bundle advisories only). Changed task files pass Prettier, check-size and git diff --check. Repository-wide format:check still flags unchanged test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs; git diff HEAD for that file is empty.
- No browser verify, npm run verify or real video rendering check was required or run. Only this task's docs/verification/tutor-tools-native.json was added; unrelated verification files were not regenerated.

Unrelated work preserved: favicon/logo changes appeared during this run in index.html, public/, server/http/routes/assets.mjs, src/shell/main.tsx and src/shell/ThemedFavicon.tsx. They were not edited or staged by this issue. The initial .beads/issues.jsonl changes were preserved via the final live database export. title: Tool runner tracer: read_page on custom endpoints
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Tutor tool runner".

## What to build

Build the tutor tool runner (which tools a chat model gets this turn; run one tool with a turn context) and its first tool, read_page: fetch on the server, readable text via Mozilla Readability on jsdom, paged by offset; http/https only; refuse loopback, link-local, private and other non-public addresses after DNS resolution and on every redirect. Custom endpoint models whose reported capabilities include tools run a function-calling loop through the runner with no call cap, ended by the reply's Stop. Adapters emit a tool event (id, name, input, status, output, elapsed); a store table keeps tool calls per reply message and deletes them with the conversation. The reply shows a collapsed tool activity line that expands to inputs and raw outputs, and shows the running tool while streaming. Models without tools behave as before.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A tools-capable custom endpoint model can read a page and answer from it
- [ ] read_page refuses localhost, LAN and other non-public targets, directly and through redirects
- [ ] Stop ends the loop and any running tool
- [ ] Tool calls are stored, survive reload and show in the tool activity line
- [ ] Models without tool capability get the old tool-free request
- [ ] Unit tests for the runner and read_page (fake HTTP); integration tests with the fake OpenAI server for the loop, events and abort
notes:
Verified result (2026-11-15): all TreeTutor-egp.1 acceptance checks pass using fake HTTP/OpenAI transport and component/store tests; no live model or browser evidence claimed.

Implementation:
- server/tools/runner.mjs owns the offered tool definitions and execution with {conversation, reply, signal}. Only custom endpoint models reporting tools:true receive read_page; unreported/false and native subscription providers retain tool-free behavior for this slice.
- read_page fetches server-side over http/https, extracts articles via pinned @mozilla/readability 0.6.0 on existing jsdom, returns final URL/title/text and character-offset continuation. Defaults: 20,000 UTF-16 characters/page, 5 MiB body, 30s fetch budget, five HTTP redirects; no model tool-call cap. Unsupported binary content, invalid offsets, HTTP failures and abort surface as tool errors.
- DNS resolves all addresses at socket connection time and refuses any non-public address, including special IPv4/IPv6, mapped loopback, link-local and private ranges. Every redirect gets a fresh checked connection. agent:false is necessary: a regression proved the global HTTP pool could otherwise reuse an unchecked socket and skip DNS validation. Redirect/error bodies are destroyed. Range policy was checked against IANA special-purpose registries; tests use synthetic addresses and local fixtures.
- Custom endpoint streaming assembles fragmented function arguments and multiple calls, executes sequentially, supplies results to subsequent model rounds and runs until the model answers or Stop. Twelve tool rounds verified without a cap. Truncated/filtered tool calls never execute; sparse call indexes do not allocate huge arrays. Timeout failures retain their old failed classification, separate from Stop.
- Conditional fixed prompt permits only offered tutor tools and treats fetched output as untrusted data; tool-free prompts keep their existing prohibition. Exact endpoint-key echoes, including JSON-escaped decoded arguments, are redacted from tool events and refused before execution. Tool errors and outputs are also redacted.
- Tool events carry id/name/input/status/output/elapsed, including one-second running updates, forwarded and saved per reply. Stop closes the page socket and streams a terminal failed tool event before done. Crashed running tools become failed on reopen, without resumption. Retry and conversation deletion cascade-delete tool calls.
- Collapsed Astryx tool activity appears under replies, expands to inputs/raw outputs and elapsed times, and announces running/completed state. Stored activity survives reopen.

Verification:
- Focused runner/read_page tests (fake HTTP), fake OpenAI loop/events/abort tests, store persistence/deletion/crash tests, component/stream tests, plus affected image/prompt/passage/upgrade tests pass.
- Full npm test initially exposed two regressions: schema table-list expectation and TimeoutError classification. Both repaired; focused regressions pass. A subsequent unrestricted full run stalled in the unchanged video-audit fixture; that fixture passed standalone. Final full npm test -- --test-concurrency=2 PASS (exit 0, zero failures, five opt-in skips). No media implementation changed.
- npm run build PASS (tsc and Vite); build fingerprint current. Existing large-chunk Vite advisories only. Changed files all pass Prettier; check-size and git diff --check pass.
- Repository-wide npm run format:check reports unchanged test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs; git diff HEAD for that file is empty. Left this pre-existing formatting issue untouched.
- Independent Standards review: no material findings. Spec review found decoded JSON credential leakage; fixed with recursive decoded-value/key redaction, regression test and reviewer confirmation.
- Impeccable detector: no findings in changed activity code; only existing 11px declarations at reading.css:183,195. Existing DESIGN.md sidecar drift reported and left unchanged.

title: Familiarity from strong evidence
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Tutor style and familiarity".

## What to build

Meeting a concept in a reply counts for little and has a low total ceiling; asking, using and the learner's corrections dominate, and the latest correction still outranks everything. The chat prompt gains a short, bounded list of the learning tree's concepts with strong evidence only: known (corrected known, or used) and shaky (corrected unknown, or asked). Concepts only met are never listed. Suggestion underlines follow the new familiarity.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Many replies mentioning a concept no longer push familiarity near 1
- [ ] Corrections, asking and using move familiarity as before
- [ ] The chat prompt lists known and shaky concepts, bounded, and never met-only ones
- [ ] Knowledge tests cover the new weights, ceiling and prompt list
notes: Familiarity: met weight 0.03 with a 0.12 total ceiling (stays below the 0.35 'some familiarity' band, so underlines stay); asked 0.2, used 0.3, ignored 0.05 unchanged; latest correction still wins. Chat prompt: store.strongConcepts(conversation) walks up to the learning tree root and down all branches, takes concepts with any evidence sourced there, classifies each by latest correction, else latest used (known) / asked (shaky) — decision: when both, latest strong event wins; newest first, max 12 per list; met-only never listed. send.mjs passes it as tree.concepts; tutorSystem appends it as learner data after the rules/branch context (all three adapters use tutorSystem). Suggestion underlines follow automatically (mentioned() uses familiarity()). Tests: test/store/familiarity.test.mjs (new: ceiling, weights, correction, bounded list, tree scope), test/media/tutor-style.test.mjs (prompt block), test/chat/suggestions-knowledge.test.mjs (updated weights, strong list across trees, chat system prompt contains list via fake Claude CLI). npm test: 505 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. title: Answer-first default tutor style
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Tutor style and familiarity".

## What to build

Rewrite the default tutor style: answer the question fully first and never hold an answer behind questions; teach at the learner's level; offer one optional practice step or check-yourself visual after the answer; back specific claims with resources and recommend one primary resource; quiz options of equal length with the right answer's position varied; at most one question per reply, at the end, only when it helps; search only for specific facts, figures, dates, recent events or when unsure. Learners without a saved tutor style get the new default; saved styles are untouched; restoring the default gives the new text.

title: Visual progress states and counts
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Visual progress".

## What to build

A plain module derives each visual's displayed state (drawing, interactive, failed, interrupted) from the artifact status, whether source has arrived and its start time, plus a reply's "n of m visuals ready". The visual frame shows a visible badge: Drawing... with elapsed time, Interactive, or Failed with Retry. A partly drawn visual is dimmed with input blocked until it finishes. State changes are announced in a live status region. The reply footer and the conversation node show the count while any visual is unfinished. Videos are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A streaming visual visibly shows Drawing... with elapsed time and blocks input
- [ ] A finished visual shows Interactive; a failed one shows Failed with Retry
- [ ] Reply footer and conversation node show "n of m visuals ready" until all finish
- [ ] Screen readers hear state changes
- [ ] Unit tests for the state module; component tests for badge, dimming, announcements and counts
notes: Done. src/media/visualProgress.ts: visualProgress(artifact, now) -> drawing/interactive/failed/interrupted + partial (source arrived) + elapsed (startedAt ?? created); visualsReady(artifacts) -> 'n of m visuals ready' while any kind=visual is pending (videos, canceled excluded). VisualFrame: Astryx Badge (Drawing… m:ss ticking 1s / Interactive / Failed / Interrupted, aria-hidden), one persistent sr-only role=status live region announcing state changes, figure aria-busy while drawing, data-partial dims the drawn frame (CSS), iframe inert while pending (blocks pointer+keyboard). Failed keeps Retry visual. Server live() now sends startedAt for pending visual runs (startDrawing records it). Reply footer (ChatThread metadata, .reply-visuals) and conversation node preview (.node-visuals) show the count. Decisions: failed visuals count as finished (count hides when nothing pending); visible failure text aria-hidden since live region carries the same words. Evidence: test/media/visual-progress.test.mjs (unit), test/media/visual-progress-ui.test.mjs (component: badge, dimming, inert, live region, footer+node counts); inline-media test updated to 'Drawing visual:' announcement; npm test 503 pass 0 fail; tsc clean. title: Reads images per model
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Per-model settings".

## What to build

When the app lists a custom endpoint's models it keeps each model's reported capabilities (vision, tools). Per-model overrides of reads images are stored; the value comes from the override, else the reported capability, else the endpoint's old "Accepts images" flag. Attachments go as images or OCR text per model. Settings shows, per custom endpoint, a searchable model list with a Reads images toggle; the endpoint form loses its Accepts images toggle. The model menu shows an image icon on models that read images, including Claude and Codex models.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A vision-capable model reported by the endpoint receives images; a non-vision model receives OCR text, without any setup
- [ ] A per-model override wins over the reported capability and survives restart
- [ ] Unreported models fall back to the old endpoint flag
- [ ] The searchable model list filters hundreds of models and toggles reads images
- [ ] Model menu shows the image icon on models that read images
- [ ] Store, adapter and component tests cover capability capture, fallback order, image routing and the list
notes:
Result (2026-11-15): implemented and verified with fixtures (fake OpenAI server, jsdom); no live endpoint check.
- Adapter: /models entries keep capabilities.vision/tools when reported as booleans (vision/tools on each model).
- Store: new additive table endpoint_models(endpoint, model, reads_images); readsImagesOverride/setReadsImages/forgetModels; cleared with the endpoint (remove, legacy clear).
- Resolution (server/http/roles.mjs imageReading): override ?? reported vision ?? endpoint's old acceptsImages flag; Claude/Codex use provider.readsImages (true). /api/models adds readsImages to every model. Send/Retry with files lists the endpoint's models to resolve the conversation's model (null model -> default); listing failure falls back to override/flag.
- Route: POST /api/settings/endpoints/model {id, model, readsImages} (validated: saved endpoint, 1-500 char model, boolean).
- Endpoint form lost Accepts images; add/edit ignore it; edit keeps the old file value as fallback; list() no longer returns it.
- Settings: per endpoint "Models" button opens a searchable list (50 rows rendered, "Showing 50 of N" note) with a Reads images switch per model; model menu radio items show PhotoIcon (role=img, "Reads images").
- Decisions: reported capabilities are not persisted (re-listed at send when needed) — simpler, endpoint must be reachable to reply anyway. Tutor tools override deferred (not in this issue's scope; table can gain a column).
Tests: test/http/model-images.test.mjs (routing image vs OCR, fallback, override, restart, validation, removal; store unit), test/providers/images.test.mjs (capability capture, legacy flag), test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs (300-model search + toggle, form without switch), test/shell/model-menu.test.mjs (icon flag). npm test: 504 tests, 499 pass, 0 fail; tsc clean.

title: Math written as math in replies
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Math".

## What to build

A fixed app rule (alongside the media rules, outside the editable tutor style) tells the chat model to write every formula as $...$ or $$...$$, never as plain text; observed problem: models express equations without LaTeX at all. The markdown parser also accepts \(...\) and \[...\] at the tokenizer level, so passages keep exact raw offsets and branching from a passage containing math still works.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The chat prompt contains the math rule for every provider
- [ ] \(...\) renders inline math and \[...\] display math
- [ ] Passage offsets across the new math forms are exact and branching works
- [ ] Markdown unit tests cover both forms, escapes and passage offsets
notes:
Implemented: TUTOR_RULES (server/media/diagrams.mjs) gains a fixed Math paragraph (every formula as $...$ / $$...$$, never plain text); tutorSystem appends it after the editable style for Claude, Codex and OpenAI-compatible (endpoint-switch test asserts TUTOR_RULES in all three prompts). src/markdown/markdownText.ts adds a micromark text construct on backslash, before the core escape: \(...\) -> inlineMath, \[...\] -> math (display), value = source minus delimiters, positions exact; \x pairs skipped inside; unclosed or \\( fall back to normal escape. Decision/tradeoff: \[...\] is text-level (inside a paragraph, cannot span a blank line) to keep one small construct; recorded as shortcut comment. Tests: test/chat/markdown.test.mjs fixture gains both forms with selection cases that POST to /api/trees/:id/branches (branching across new math works with exact offsets), plus unit test for offsets in blockquote/list, escapes, unclosed, code spans, render display block/inline; tutor-style test asserts rule. tsc clean. Fixture-only; no live model check.
Verified: npm test 501 tests, 496 pass, 0 fail (5 skipped); tsc --noEmit clean.

title: Switching model profile updates the open conversation
description:
Spec: docs/tutor-tools-and-polish-spec.md, section "Model profile switch".

## What to build

Activating a model profile also sets the chat model and effort of the conversation open in focused chat (the one the model menu shows) to the profile's chat model default, even when that conversation's model was chosen by hand. A streaming reply finishes on its old model; the change applies from the next message. Other conversations and learning trees keep their models. With no conversation open, only the active profile changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Activating a profile changes the open conversation's model and effort, shown in the model menu and used for the next message
- [ ] A reply streaming during the switch completes on its old model
- [ ] Other conversations and learning trees are unchanged
- [ ] Unit or hook test covers the switch with and without an open conversation and during streaming
notes: Done 2026-11-14. ModelProfiles.activate() reports the newly active profile chat selection (picker swap, New, Duplicate) via onActivated -> SettingsWindow.profileActivated -> useChatModel.profileActivated. useChatModel stores the switch for the open tree id and applies it through changeModel (POST /api/trees/:id/model) once that tree is not in state.active, so a streaming reply finishes on its old model and the next message uses the new one. No open tree: nothing beyond the active profile changes; the first-question model already reloads from /api/settings/chat when Settings closes. Decision/tradeoff: client-side deferral, no server change; leaving the conversation before its reply ends drops the pending switch (shortcut comment in code). Tests: test/chat/profile-switch.test.mjs (open conversation incl. hand-picked, no conversation, during streaming; other conversation untouched), test/shell/model-roles.test.mjs asserts onActivated payload. title: Merged repair counts as the audit
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. A failed cut's repair input holds the error, failed code, set pieces, style brief and the previous cut's last frame when it exists, asking to fix the error and check continuity. A repaired cut skips the cut audit. Metered as video stage 'repair'.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: a failed cut gets one repair call with the previous frame and set pieces, then no audit call; usage stage repair.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. Completed the existing partial implementation in server/media/video-cut.mjs, server/media/video-cuts.mjs and server/http/jobs/media.mjs; added test/media/video-repair.test.mjs.

Repairs append REPAIR_NOTE to the existing Remotion/Manim instructions. Input contains validationError, failedCode (raw failed write or current code for a render failure), styleBrief, cut, previousEndState, Remotion setPieces when present and previousLastFrame. The preceding cut's validated private JPEG is attached when available. Instructions fix the actual error and check continuity against the plan, using the preceding frame as context rather than copying its deviations. A successful validated repair marks the cut audited and makes no further audit model call. Metering remains task video with stage repair.

Decision/tradeoff: repaired and kept cuts still take snapshots to supply continuity frames to following cuts, but skip the audit model call. Repairs wait for the preceding snapshot, never its audit answer; first cuts and missing frames use previousLastFrame=false with no attachment. The existing two-attempt limit, provider/auth failure handling and diagnostic path stripping remain. Overflow output is already discarded by the bounded provider reader, so failedCode is omitted in that case. Manim keeps the existing written-look contract rather than receiving React set-piece source. A render failure can occur after the original audit; its repair receives no second audit.

Acceptance evidence (fixture job tests): a write-validation failure gets exactly one repair carrying the failed code, error, style brief, set pieces and previous frame; repaired code is stored, no separate audit follows, log stage=repair once. Adjacent repaired cuts share a frame of repaired code, and cut 1 works without a predecessor. Render-failure repair sees TypeError with [path]:3:4, failed source and preceding frame, succeeds on its second render and receives no further audit. Focused repair/cuts/audit/Manim tests: 26 pass. npm test run once: 481 pass, 5 skipped, 0 fail. npm run test:render: 5 pass with real sandboxed Remotion, multi-cut, Three.js, overlay and mixed Manim renders. These real renders use fixture model output; no live provider inference or visual-quality judgment was performed. npx tsc --noEmit and scoped Prettier checks pass; git diff --check passes. title: Cut audit for Remotion cuts
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md, ADR 0002. Injectable videoSnapshot renders stills of a staged cut in the render sandbox: end of each narration sentence plus last frame, 960x540, private workspace files cleaned up. Once written and narrated, each cut is snapshotted and audited; all audits run at the same time. One Smart call with images gets code, snapshots, set pieces, style brief, cut plan entry, previous cut's planned end state and pre-audit last frame. It aligns to the plan, may replace emphasis marks, returns no change or full replacement code. Replacement is validated and rendered; on failure the pre-audit cut is used; an audit never fails a video. A cut is playable only after its audit settles. Auditing phase with counts; metered as video stage 'audit'. Cancel stops snapshots and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: audit fix replaces a cut before it is playable; broken fix falls back; audits start together; marks can move; cancel during audit; usage stage audit; phases advance only.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Snapshots: injectable videoSnapshot(cutDir, [{frame,file}], signal) beside videoRender; default sandboxSnapshot runs video-render.mjs stills mode (renderStill JPEG, scale 0.5 = 960x540) in the same bwrap sandbox; frames = each sentence endFrame (clamped to audioFrames) and audioFrames (narration last frame, before the pause fade), minus 1, deduped; server-chosen files in cut-N/out, checked regular/<=2MB/inside out; existing out cleanup removes them. Audit: in writeCuts, each Remotion cut once written+narrated is staged, snapshotted and audited inside its own writer, so audits run concurrently; audit i waits only for cut i-1 pre-audit last frame (shared via per-cut resolvers, resolved null on failure/Manim/kept). One Smart call AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS with images (own stills + previous last frame) and JSON input styleBrief, cut plan entry, previousEndState, setPieces, code, emphasis, snapshots count, previousLastFrame. Answer JSON {"change":false} or {"code","emphasis"?} (auditFix: cutSource validation, marks via exported emphasisMark and sentence < count). Fix accepted only if its snapshot render succeeds; otherwise pre-audit code/marks restored. Any non-abort error (snapshot, provider, parse) settles the audit unchanged; audit never fails a video. cut.audited=true; playable() for Remotion now needs audited; cut.emphasis overrides plan marks in stage (MP4) and live /cuts route. Retry keeps audited flag/marks of kept cuts. Phase auditing (server PHASES, client STEPS/SPAN/label "Auditing cuts", detail "n of N cuts audited"); metered stage audit. Cancel aborts snapshot sandbox and audit call through the job signal. Decisions/tradeoffs: snapshot failure of the original cut skips the audit instead of spending the repair (03j.9 owns merged repair); the fix is checked by its snapshot render, a later full-render failure goes to the existing render repair path, not back to the pre-audit code; Manim cuts skip the audit (03j.10); repaired cuts are still audited until 03j.9; test kits default to a no-still snapshot fake so existing call counts are unchanged. Evidence (fixture job tests, test/media/video-audit.test.mjs, 5 pass): audits in flight together; phase auditing and no cut playable during audit; fix + moved marks saved, staged into the MP4 render and served live; inputs/images (2 stills, cut 2 also gets cut 1 last frame); stage=audit logged twice; snapshots removed; validation-failing and render-failing fixes fall back; cancel during snapshot and during audit -> canceled, no media; phase order via job(); auditFix parsing. notes: Done 2026-11-14. title: Continuing cuts and scene-change transitions
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Plan gains per-cut join (continue|scene) and, for scene, transition (fade, slide, wipe, flip, clockWipe, iris, plus direction where it applies); cut 1 is scene; unknown values rejected; old plans read as scene with today's fade. Continuing cut: no exit/entry fade, hard cut. Scene change: @remotion/transitions effect one side at a time (exit over the pause, then entry), never overlapping, same in live player and final MP4 join. Reduced motion uses the short fade. Add @remotion/transitions pinned to the installed Remotion version.
acceptance_criteria: Plan tests accept and reject join/transition values and read old plans as scene; live-player tests cover exit/entry progress per join type and reduced motion; live cut data carries joins.
notes: Implemented 2026-11-15. Plan: cuts take join (continue|scene), transition (fade|slide|wipe|flip|clockWipe|iris), direction (slide/flip: 4 sides; wipe: also diagonals). Validator rejects unknown join/transition/direction, a direction on a non-directional effect, transition on a continue cut, and cut 1 = continue (decision: reject rather than coerce, consistent with 'unknown values rejected'). Missing join/transition reads as scene+fade (old plans). cutJoin() in video-plan.mjs normalises. Timing: cut.timing gains entry (join into the cut; null for cut 1) and exit (join into next cut; last cut fades out as before), replacing transitionIn; kit joinAt() still reads old transitionIn timings. Playback: kit Joined/joinAt used by both CUT_ENTRY (per-cut MP4 render, concat join unchanged) and liveVideo, so live and MP4 match. Exit side plays over the 15-frame pause, entry side over first 15 frames (fade: 8, as before); never overlapping. Decisions: clockWipe/iris have no-op exiting sides in @remotion/transitions, so the outgoing cut plays the entering side reversed; presentation wrapper is constant per cut so the cut never remounts mid-play (idle slide sits 0.01% off by library epsilon). Reduced motion (matchMedia in the player frame) turns every transition into the short fade; continue stays a hard cut. @remotion/transitions pinned 4.0.542. Evidence: node --test video-plan, video-cuts, videos-live, live-player pass (join accept/reject + old plans; joinAt per join type and reduced motion; live slide-out in Thumbnail; every transition renders; live cut data carries entry/exit). npm run test:render 5/5 pass (real sandbox bundles transitions). tsc + vite build OK.

title: Retry rewrites only failed cuts
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Retry without differentVersion reuses the attempt's saved plan, narration, timing and non-failed cuts, copied into the new attempt workspace (never shared). No plan call; only failed cuts are written again. New attempt keeps ownership, cancel and late-output rules. Cut failure error gains 'Retry keeps the other cuts.' Make a different version still plans fresh.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: after one cut fails, Retry makes no plan call and exactly one cut call, keeps other cuts' code and narration, and publishes; different version plans fresh; cancel and late output still rejected.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Retry (route action retry) on a FAILED video passes the pre-retry row to startVideo -> generateVideo({previous}). If its saved source has a plan, generateVideo copies (fs.cp, never shares) video-work/<id>/<oldAttempt>/cut-i into the new attempt workspace for every cut with timing, keeping timing only if public/narration.mp3 came along (else the copy is removed and the cut is narrated again). No plan call; writeCuts takes kept cuts: code kept for cuts not marked failed, timing kept where copied; only missing/failed code is written and only missing timing narrated. New attempt id unchanged, so ownership, cancel and late-output rules hold. A failed attempt now keeps cut public/ and narration.json (canceled/stopped attempts still discard audio) so Retry can reuse narration. cutError appends "Retry keeps the other cuts.". Make a different version (regenerate, new id) still plans fresh. Decisions: reuse only from status failed (a canceled/interrupted attempt may not have settled its workspace, so it plans fresh); differentVersion in a frozen input does not block reuse (the saved plan is already that version); Manim clips are re-rendered (clip not reused); a failed cut first write gets no error text (merged repair is a later ticket); set pieces not applicable yet. Tests (fixture-level job tests): video-cuts "Retry after a failed cut ..." -> after cut 2 of 3 fails, retry makes 0 plan calls and exactly 1 cut call, keeps cut 1/3 code and timing, 0 new narration, publishes; canceled retry with held late cut output stays canceled, no media; retry after cancel plans fresh; regenerate plans fresh. Evidence: node --test test/media/video-cuts.test.mjs 7 pass; npm test 459 pass x4 (one earlier run had an unrelated flake in artifacts-stop diagram 30ms timeout). test:render not run (no render pipeline change).

title: PDFs read by structure
description: PDF attachments are read with pdfjs-dist page by page: visible text becomes text parts; each embedded image covering at least 10% of the page becomes an image part; a page that is one image covering most of the page plus only invisible text is a scan, sent as that image with its hidden OCR text ignored; vector drawings are not rasterised. Image parts then follow D3 (native) or D4 (OCR). Chips summarise delivery (read as text, sent as image, OCR).
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation unit tests with small fixture PDFs: typed text; large figure plus small logo; scanned page with invisible OCR layer; vector-only page; non-vision model path uses OCR.
- Integration: PDF send reaches a fake provider with ordered text and image parts.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Completed 2026-11-14. PDFs are now prepared page by page with pdfjs-dist ^6.5.438 in server/pdf.mjs. Visible operator glyphs become named page text parts, with PDF TextContent restoring whitespace where it matches; invisible and clip-only render modes (3 and 7) are omitted, including saved/restored graphics state. Embedded images drawn over at least 10% of the CropBox become PNG image parts using the decoded original pixels. Transforms, Form XObjects, inline/repeated images, packed grayscale and coloured bitmap stencils are supported. Small/off-page images are skipped. Vector paths are never rasterised; their labels survive, and a page without readable text or qualifying images has an explicit placeholder. Scans naturally yield only their page image with hidden OCR omitted; no separate scan-area heuristic is needed. Malformed/password-protected PDFs refuse preparation with an actionable reason. Original bytes are copied into pdfjs so its worker cannot take away the bytes saved for reopening.

Delivery/storage: server/attachments.mjs sends extracted image parts through the existing native/OCR capability path; non-vision models get OCR text and the existing exact OCR-unavailable refusal. server/http/attachments.mjs retains prepared parts through send/retry and writes derived PNGs beside the original attachment under the conversation folder (owner-only files). Retry reparses the original for the current capability before changing the failed reply; a preparation refusal preserves the saved question/reply and delivery. The existing attachment text column remains the history/compaction source, so no schema change was needed. SSE/GET chip metadata excludes prepared text, parts and image bytes. Original PDFs download unchanged with an inert binary type even for text-only delivery. Deleting the conversation removes originals and derived images through the existing folder lifecycle.

Provider/UI: PDF turns pass ordered text/image parts to all three adapters. Claude stream-json, Codex localImage inputs and OpenAI-compatible content arrays preserve captions/page order; later turns and inherited-context preparation receive text/image names only. Existing text-plus-images callers remain supported. PDF chips identify the PDF and show all applicable read as text / sent as image / OCR labels; mixed OCR still opens the existing accessible explanation popover. Impeccable context and craft guidance applied; detector returned no findings. Existing Astryx components/styles retained.

Routine decisions/tradeoffs: use content-stream order within each page, without geometric column rearrangement. Mixed summaries use comma-separated delivery kinds in the existing field. Reparse on Retry instead of storing another structured representation in SQLite. PNG encoding uses pdfjs's bundled Node canvas factory for embedded pixels only. CMaps, standard fonts, WASM and ICC data resolve from the installed package; worker network fetching and eval are disabled. No application file/page/count limits, smart-model calls, new settings or page rasterisation were added.

Evidence: 25 focused checks passed across PDF preparation, PDF send, existing attachments/OCR, chip components and provider adapters. test/fixtures/pdf holds small deterministic actual PDFs plus a reproducible generator/README: typed text/TJ spacing, large figure plus small logo, full-page scan with deliberately wrong invisible OCR, vectors with/without labels, a four-page ordered document, render-mode restoration, exact 10% and 9.75% boundaries, transformed/off-page images, inline/monochrome/stencil/repeated bitmaps. Tests check actual extracted PNG dimensions and RGB/grayscale/stencil pixels, OCR replacement/refusal with injected recognisers, ordered multipart delivery to a fake provider, all three adapter wire shapes, original downloads, owner-only derived files, hidden-text omission, history/compaction, retry in both capability directions, atomic refusal and conversation cleanup. These are fixtures, not live Claude/Codex or real OCR evidence; this issue requires no new native/browser/render run.

Final gates: npm test passed: 461 total, 456 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. Initial run alongside the build hit the unchanged visual-detach.test.mjs 50 ms timeout race (artifact had already failed before its pending-state HTTP assertion); that file passed in isolation and the full suite passed when retried without the concurrent build. No unrelated test/timeout changes made. npm run build passed including tsc; existing large-chunk warnings remain. Scoped Prettier, check-size and git diff --check pass. Global format:check reports only unchanged src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs; both were verified to differ from Prettier at HEAD as well and left untouched. No docs/verification files regenerated. Existing .beads/issues.jsonl work preserved through local tracker/export. No staging, commit, push or sync; Ralph owns the pending commit.

title: OCR fallback for models that cannot read images
description: When the chat model cannot read images, image parts go through tesseract.js OCR on the server and are sent as text. English language data downloads on first use and is cached in the app data directory. The chip shows OCR with an icon whose popover explains OCR can miss handwriting and diagrams and suggests a model that reads images. If OCR cannot start (for example the download fails), the send is refused with: This model can't read images and OCR language data couldn't be downloaded. Retry is possible on the next send.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation unit tests with an injected recogniser: OCR text replaces image parts for non-vision models; vision models skip OCR; OCR-unavailable refusal.
- Component test for the OCR chip popover.
- Manual opt-in real OCR test script documented, not part of npm test.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Completed 2026-11-14. Implemented OCR fallback for PNG/JPEG/WebP attachments when the selected provider does not read images. server/attachments.mjs now accepts readsImages and an injected recogniser, returns only OCR text parts with delivery ocr for non-vision models, and leaves native images/text files alone. OCR startup failures refuse the entire send before messages/files are saved with the required exact error: This model can't read images and OCR language data couldn't be downloaded. Empty OCR has an explicit no-text placeholder; malformed image recognition gives an actionable image-specific refusal.

Runtime: server/ocr.mjs uses tesseract.js ^7.0.0, lazy English data under <app data directory>/ocr, one worker per app, serial recognition jobs to protect the worker image buffer, failed-start reset and termination so the next send retries, and app shutdown cleanup. Starts the worker with no language then reinitializes English so a failed language download leaves a worker that can be terminated; errorHandler prevents the library throwing an uncaught failure. No OCR/download on native image or text-only turns. server/http/attachments.mjs holds upload/retry preparation to keep send.mjs below the existing 500-line ceiling. Retry prepares original images for the current capability and saves the new delivery/text only after preparation succeeds; refused retries preserve the failed reply. The conversation is active throughout OCR; a second send is refused and Stop prevents later persistence. Original OCR images still open inline through the existing sandboxed asset route. History and compaction receive recognized text, never an image payload for a non-vision model.

UI: src/chat/Attachments.tsx shows Image · OCR and a DocumentMagnifyingGlass icon opening the existing Astryx Popover. Copy explains recognized text can miss handwriting and diagrams and recommends an image-reading model such as Claude or Codex. Help is a separate named button beside the attachment link, avoiding nested interactive controls. Existing Paperback styling/components retained; no extra CSS or UI dependency.

Decisions/tradeoffs: reuse the provider readsImages capability from D3 (including the existing per-endpoint Accepts images setting); English only, no smart model or added provider calls. Reprepare original images on Retry to follow the current capability rather than resend stale image parts; this can repeat OCR work on a retry. One queued worker saves memory at the cost of serial OCR across simultaneous image sends; text/native image calls remain independent. Opt-in real OCR uses a fresh temporary data directory so it proves a first download without modifying the user's app data.

Evidence: test/http/ocr-preparation.test.mjs unit tests inject recognisers for all three image types, native/text bypass, empty OCR, exact unavailable refusal and malformed-image refusal. test/chat/attachments.test.mjs component checks OCR label/icon, separate link/button, popup copy, expanded state and Escape dismissal. test/http/attachments.test.mjs retains native image, storage/history/compaction, atomic refusal and asset coverage with injected OCR unavailable. test/http/ocr-send.test.mjs uses a fake provider/recogniser for atomic multi-file refusal, next-send recovery, OCR text-only payload, history/compaction, original image asset, failed-reply preservation on refused Retry, capability changes in both directions on Retry, shutdown cleanup and Stop/duplicate-send handling while OCR waits. These HTTP/component checks are fixtures, not live model evidence.

Real native OCR: npm run test:ocr passed against tesseract.js 7.0.0. scripts/test-ocr.mjs first received a forced HTTP 503 language download refusal, then the same recogniser retried via the default CDN and recognized Binary heaps from test/fixtures/ocr.png. English eng.traineddata was cached under /tmp/treetutor-real-ocr-brLJK4/ocr. A fresh worker with language downloads unavailable recognized the fixture twice from that cache with zero language requests. This script is documented in docs/agents/testing.md, requires explicit opt-in, and is excluded from npm test; direct execution without the opt-in flag confirms it skips.

Final gates: npm test ran once: 450 tests, 445 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. npm run build passed (includes tsc --noEmit); check-size and git diff --check passed. Prettier passes on all changed code; Impeccable detector returned no issues for Attachments.tsx. Global npm run format:check reports two pre-existing unchanged files (src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs); both also fail formatting when read from HEAD, left untouched to preserve scope. Build retains the existing large-chunk warnings. No browser verify, live Claude/Codex calls or video-render tests were required or run; no docs/verification files regenerated. Git staging/commit/push left to Ralph as requested.

title: Images to models that read them
description: Image attachments (PNG, JPEG, WebP) are sent natively: Codex and Claude using the shapes from D1, custom endpoints as image_url data URLs when the model's new Accepts images switch (endpoint settings, default off) is on. Custom endpoints send an image only on the turn it was attached; history turns replace it with [image: name]. Chips show sent as image. Until D4, an image for a model that cannot read images is refused with the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provider adapter tests with existing fakes: image parts shaped per provider; custom endpoint history placeholder.
- Store and settings tests for the Accepts images flag.
- Integration: refusal when the model cannot read images.
- Component test for the Accepts images switch and chip label.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Done 2026-11-14. Server: server/attachments.mjs prepares PNG/JPEG/WebP (IMAGE_TYPES, by media type) as delivery 'image' with stored text "[image: name]", so history (tutorContext) and compaction see only the placeholder; other image types (e.g. GIF) are still refused as unsupported. send.mjs: imageRefusal() refuses before anything is saved (new send: after preparation, before files are written; retry: before the failed reply is discarded) with "<name>: this chat model can't read images. Choose Claude, Codex or a custom endpoint with Accepts images on, then send again." (until D4/OCR). This turn's images go to the adapter as tree.images [{name,type,path}] (stored file path); prompt text still includes the [image: name] line. Adapters: Claude/Codex readsImages = true; Claude adds --input-format stream-json on image turns and writes one {type:'user',message:{role:'user',content:[text, image base64 blocks]}} line, text turns unchanged; Codex appends { type:'localImage', path } after the text item; custom endpoints send the last user message as [{type:'text'}, {type:'image_url', image_url:{url:'data:<type>;base64,...'}}] only on the attaching turn, history turns are plain text with [image: name]. Endpoint adapter readsImages = saved acceptsImages. Endpoint file entries gain optional acceptsImages (default false; add/edit take a boolean, edit without the field keeps it, legacy save keeps it; list() always reports it; toggling replaces the adapter like other setting changes). Asset route serves image deliveries inline with their image type (still CSP sandbox + nosniff). Client: Accepts images Switch in the endpoint add/edit form; chips show "Image · sent as image" with a photo icon (pending and message chips). check-size forced a move: endpoint settings validators (settings, readOwned, lastTest, endpointName, EndpointError) moved verbatim to server/providers/endpointSettings.mjs; openai.mjs re-exports EndpointError.
Decision/tradeoff: Accepts images is per endpoint (applies to every model on it), not per model, because endpoint settings list no models and the model is resolved lazily after preparation; per-model would need a model list in settings. Upgrade path: store a model id list instead of a boolean if mixed vision/non-vision endpoints become common.
Evidence (fixtures/fakes, no live provider this ticket; D1 shapes were verified live on TreeTutor-9lj.1): test/providers/images.test.mjs (Claude launcher fake: stream-json args + base64 block, text turn plain; Codex protocol fixture: localImage after text; fake OpenAI server: image_url data URL on this turn, history placeholder, acceptsImages default off/persist/edit keep/off). test/providers/endpoints.test.mjs (settings route saves and clears acceptsImages; list fixtures updated). test/http/attachments.test.mjs (prep unit for png/jpeg/webp; integration: refusal for non-reading model with nothing saved, image path passed to a reading model, later turn has no images and [image: red.png] in history, asset served inline image/png sandboxed). test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs (switch default off, sent on add, shown and sent on edit). test/chat/attachments.test.mjs (image chip "Image · sent as image"). npm test: 444 tests, 439 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build passes; prettier clean on changed files.

title: Text-file attachments end to end
description: Tracer bullet for attachments. The question box accepts files by paperclip, paste and drop, showing pending chips with remove buttons. Send accepts multipart form data (JSON body still works); files are saved under the app data directory with an additive attachments table and served back through a conversation-scoped asset route with a safe content type and Content-Disposition. Text files are prepared as text with a file-name header and sent to every provider. Message chips show name, type and read as text. Attachments delete with their conversation. Compaction receives attachment text. Unsupported types are refused before sending. An attachment-only first question titles from the attachment text, or the file name.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation module unit tests for text files.
- Integration: multipart send stores and delivers text to a fake provider; JSON send unchanged; asset route headers; delete with conversation removes rows and files; unsupported type refused; compaction prompt includes attachment text; attachment-only title.
- Component tests: composer paperclip, paste and drop feed one handler; pending chips removable; message chip label.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Done 2026-11-14. Server: server/attachments.mjs prepareAttachment({name,type,bytes}) -> {delivery:'text', parts:[{text:'[Attached file: name]\n...'}]}, refuses images/PDF (until their tickets) and non-UTF-8 or NUL content with "<name>: this file type can't be attached. Attach a plain-text file."; withAttachments(text, attachments) joins question + prepared text. app.mjs parses multipart/form-data (Request.formData, no new dependency) only for POST /api/trees/:id/messages (fields text, theme JSON, files); JSON body unchanged, CSRF still required. send.mjs prepares every file before saving anything (one bad file refuses the send, nothing stored), writes files to <data dir>/attachments/<conversation>/<attachment id> (0600), saves the message then rows in the additive attachments table (id, conversation, message, name, type, size, delivery, text, created; FK to messages). Provider prompt = withAttachments(question, attachments) for every provider (no adapter change needed for text); history (tutorContext) and compaction (compactionMessages) fold attachment text into the learner message; retry resends the saved attachments. Asset route GET /api/trees/:conv/attachments/:id: looked up by conversation+id, text/plain; charset=utf-8, Content-Disposition inline with ASCII filename + filename*, CSP "sandbox; default-src 'none'", nosniff. GET tree and the saved SSE event omit prepared text. Delete removes rows in the transaction and the conversation folder after commit. Attachment-only first question: placeholder title = file names, title job reads the attachment text (capped 4000 chars, starts with the file name header). Client: src/chat/Attachments.tsx (AttachButton paperclip + hidden file input, PendingAttachments drawer chips with remove, MessageAttachments chips linking to the asset route with "Text file · read as text"); paste and drop use the Astryx ChatComposerInput onFiles prop, so all three feed one add(); both the first-question and focused composers; pending files kept per conversation in useChatState like drafts and moved with the first question; a Send button appears for files with an empty draft; useReplyStream sends FormData when files are pending.
Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) Prepared text stored in the attachments.text column so history/compaction never re-read or re-extract files (later PDF/OCR); deviation from the spec's column list, additive. (2) Text detection by content (valid UTF-8, no NUL) rather than media type, since code files arrive with empty or wrong types (.ts = video/mp2t). (3) Client relies on the server refusal for unsupported types (shown as the send error, before any provider call or save) instead of duplicating the rule in the browser. (4) shortcut: attachment folders removed after commit (crash in between leaves files); files buffered in memory during upload.
Evidence (fixtures, fake providers, no live provider): test/http/attachments.test.mjs (preparation unit tests; integration: JSON send unchanged, unsupported refused with nothing saved, multipart stores row+file and delivers text to fake provider, client JSON omits text, history carries text, compaction prompt includes text, asset headers + cross-conversation 404, attachment-only title placeholder and quick title, delete removes rows+folder). test/chat/attachments.test.mjs (paperclip/paste/drop feed one handler, chips removable, files-only Send, message chip label/link). Updated test/store/preview.test.mjs table list and chat-states fixtures. npm test: 440 tests, 435 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (an earlier full run had one timing flake in visual-detach that passed alone twice and on the rerun). tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build passes; prettier clean on changed files (format:check flags pre-existing src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs, untouched).

Record the shapes, versions and any limits as a comment and in the epic's Decisions so far. No product code.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text:
D1 image input shapes — verified LIVE 2026-11-14 (red 64x64 PNG, both models answered "Red").

Versions: codex-cli 0.167.2 (app-server), Claude Code 2.1.325.

Codex app-server (schema from `codex app-server generate-ts`, v2/UserInput.ts):
- turn/start input: [{ type: 'text', text, text_elements: [] }, { type: 'localImage', path: '/abs/file.png' }]
- optional `detail`: 'auto' | 'low' | 'high' | 'original'.
- Alternative { type: 'image', url: 'data:image/png;base64,...' } also works (or fileId).
- Live: localImage with path outside thread cwd works under sandbox 'read-only', approvalPolicy 'never', shell tool disabled (app-server reads the file itself, not the model's tools).

Claude CLI (current -p invocation + `--input-format stream-json`):
- stdin one JSON line: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."},{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":"<b64>"}}]}}
- Live with -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --max-turns 1 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands --system-prompt ... --session-id ...: success, partial stream events still emitted.
- A later plain-text `--resume <session>` turn (no --input-format) still sees the image ("Red"), so only image turns need stream-json input.

Limits: not probed; provider-side limits apply (Anthropic API documents ~5 MB per base64 image, 8000 px max side). Per spec, no app caps; surface provider errors.
Decision: Codex uses localImage with the stored attachment path (no base64 copy); Claude sends base64 image blocks via --input-format stream-json on turns with images, plain text stdin otherwise.

title: Step-through helper and visual text rules
description: The sandbox injects a small shared step-through helper before the fragment: the fragment declares steps, the helper renders previous, next and Step n of m in house style, wires Enter, Space and arrow keys, and animates between states with d3 or CSS transitions, skipping animation under prefers-reduced-motion. No network or app messaging. The visual prompt asks for the helper when an idea has stages, forbids explanatory paragraphs inside the fragment, and requires result lines in primary text at reading size; predict-then-reveal contract kept.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in jsdom: steps run in order; controls and indicator update; keys work; reduced motion skips transitions; first and last step bounds.
- Visual prompt unit tests: step helper and text rules present; predict-then-reveal kept.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. src/media/stepThrough.ts: stepThrough(root, steps, duration=300) installed as frame global in sandbox.ts (before any fragment render). Renders Previous / Step n of m (aria-live) / Next after root in .tt-steps group, styled in sandbox.html like summary chips (zero-specificity :where). Each step fn gets {index,duration}; sets --step-duration on root; duration 0 on first render and under prefers-reduced-motion. Enter/Space handled on keydown with preventDefault (plus Space keyup preventDefault) so one step per press; arrows on the group; focus moves off a disabled bound button. No messaging/network. Prompt visual.md: prefer helper for staged ideas, no own step controls, no explanatory paragraphs (predict-then-reveal answer excepted), labels inside graphic, result lines primary text at reading size; predict-then-reveal paragraph unchanged. Decision: helper places controls after root rather than inside, so fragments own root content; tradeoff: root must be an HTML element (not inside SVG). Tests: test/media/step-through.test.mjs (jsdom unit, 4) + prompt test in visuals-prompts.test.mjs. npm test 431 pass/0 fail/5 skipped (one visual-detach timing flake on first run, passed 3/3 alone and on full rerun); npm run build ok. title: Origin strip in child conversations
description: Every child focused chat shows an origin strip above the thread: the parent's address chip in branch family ink, the source (passage text, suggested term or visual title) and the learner's first question in full. notes: Done: src/chat/OriginStrip.tsx above the thread in every child FocusedChat (section aria-label 'Conversation origin', family ink via inkStyle(child ink)). title: Model-written conversation titles
description: When a conversation's first learner message is saved and its title is unrenamed, a quick thinking title job runs: a root reads the question, a child reads its inherited context and question. Output is a plain title of about 60 characters at most, in the question's language. The placeholder (question cut at 200 characters) shows at once for roots and children; the job replaces it only if still unrenamed. Unset model or failure keeps the placeholder and logs a warning. Metered as quick thinking usage. Delivered through the existing tree state refresh.
acceptance_criteria:
- Title prompt builder unit tests: root and child inputs.
- Integration with a fake quick thinking provider: placeholder saved, then replaced; rename during the job wins; unset model and failed or empty result keep the placeholder with no learner-facing error; usage recorded as a quick thinking task.
- npm test passes.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. server/http/jobs/title.mjs: titlePrompt (root {question}; child {inheritedContext:{snapshot,selectedPassage},question}), cleanTitle (one plain line, quotes/markdown stripped, <=60 chars at word boundary), titleJobs.startTitle: detached quick thinking call (no thread), waits for a child compaction, metered as usage task "title", store.retitle only WHERE title_renamed=0. send.mjs starts it on the first non-retry learner message of an unrenamed conversation; placeholder (question cut at 200; child = branch question) is saved at once by existing code. /api/state exposes titling ids; useLearningTrees adds them to activeKey so the existing state refresh polls until the title lands. app.stop aborts and settled() awaits title jobs. Schema: usage_events rebuilt once to allow task title (rows/indexes kept); Usage dashboard label "Conversation titles". Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) "unset model" = no quick thinking model pinned in the active profile; then no call, one WARN title log (no fallback to the chat provider, unlike compaction) so titles never silently spend chat-model tokens. (2) Failures, invalid selection, non-completed or empty output keep the placeholder, WARN log with redacted cause, nothing learner-facing. (3) New usage task "title" rather than reusing suggestions/compaction so the dashboard stays truthful; costs a one-time table rebuild. Evidence (fixtures, no live provider): test/http/titles.test.mjs (prompt unit tests root/child, cleanTitle, integration with fake quick provider: unset keeps placeholder + warning, replaced title, usage task title claude/quick-model 7/3, only first message titles, rename during job wins, failed and empty keep placeholder, child prompt carries inherited context; upgrade test for old usage table). Updated tests for the new extra call/warning: logging, suggestions-models daily usage, typed-effort, manim-cuts (media-only warnings). npm test: 425 tests, 420 pass, 0 fail; tsc --noEmit clean; prettier clean.

title: Empty first run
description: A fresh database creates the profiles tables empty with no active profile, and new learning trees get no default provider (not codex). - Upgrade test with an existing database shows no change.

notes: Done 2026-11-14. Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) every pre-existing database seeds Default (not only those with saved role rows) because its trees.provider is NOT NULL and its learners relied on the assumed provider: existing installs unchanged. (2) Saving a role before any profile exists creates and activates "Default" so the learner can pick a chat model straight from Settings. (3) Quick thinking unset keeps falling back to the conversation provider default (existing behaviour); Not set labels only on chat and smart. (4) createApp default defaultProvider stays codex for tests; tests calling store.create(title) now pass codex explicitly. Evidence (fixtures, no live provider): test/store/profiles.test.mjs fresh + pre-profile role save; test/store/upgrades.test.mjs existing DB keeps Default, assumesProvider, codex trees; test/http/app.test.mjs empty-first-run visual skip; test/providers/credential-boundary main-entry fresh install null provider + 409 gate; test/chat/chat-states + test/shell/chat-settings components. npm test 409 pass 0 fail; npm run build passes.

title: Typed effort for custom endpoint models
description: Every effort picker (chat default, smart, quick thinking, conversation model menu, model profiles) offers Custom... for custom endpoint models only. - Integration with the fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint: typed effort reaches reasoning_effort unchanged; remembered efforts persist and are deleted with the endpoint; profiles save typed efforts.
