title: Manim cuts
description:
## What to build
The plan may mark a math cut (equations, transforms, graphs) for Manim. The smart model writes Python scene code using a Manim house kit (dark-paper ground, palette, Archivo and Literata, margins, subtitle space). Manim renders it inside the bubblewrap sandbox to a 1080p30 clip placed on the cut timeline. If Manim is unusable, the video fails with a clear message and a log warning; chat and visuals keep working. See the spec's Manim cuts section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Integration test with a fake Manim engine: a plan with a math cut routes it to Manim and places its clip in order.
- [x] Integration test: an unusable Manim fails the video with a clear message.
- [x] npm run test:render passes with a real Manim cut.
- [x] npm test passes.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All four acceptance criteria pass.

Implementation and decisions: the smart plan can choose manim for equations/transforms/graphs alongside Remotion. Manim cuts receive an isolated Python writing prompt with only their style brief, own cut and previous planned end state. The Python house kit supplies dark-paper ground, assigned palette roles, Archivo/Literata, shared pixel coordinates/margins and measured narration timing. MathTex remains LaTeX glyphs. Existing Fontsource WOFF assets are decompressed to TTF with the Python standard library inside the sandbox because Pango silently substituted fonts when given WOFF on this machine; no package or font download was added. The house kit pads the end state through the fixed pause, using cut_duration because Manim owns Scene.duration for each animation.

AST validation runs inside bubblewrap before generated Python executes. It checks named kit imports, the Cut(HouseScene) contract, palette/font references and common style setters/dictionaries, and rejects external imports/resources and house-config changes. Bubblewrap remains the security boundary: shared rendering isolation masks home and the app data root, clears environment and disables network, while unmasking only the read-only project Python environment, its exact uv interpreter installation and trusted runner. Python runs with -I -B. Child termination, cancellation and finite render budgets reuse the existing sandbox process handling. Private renderer diagnostics are drained rather than sent to chat or the terminal.

A raw Manim 1080p30 clip is validated and saved privately as cut-N/public/manim.mp4. A server-owned OffthreadVideo component places it inside the existing Remotion wrapper, which clips content to the margins and reserves the 120px subtitle band, then applies the same narration, subtitles and eased transitions. The existing sandboxed join preserves mixed-engine plan order. Ordered private cut metadata retains engine, code, timing, status and clip; public API/tutor history still receive metadata only. Existing videos are untouched. Bad scene code/rendering uses the existing two writing attempts for that cut only, reusing narration. An unavailable runtime fails without retry, with npm start repair guidance and one WARN video terminal entry through the new injected log seam. No shared logger existed yet; this issue adds only the required warning seam, leaving broader logging to its own issue. Chat and inline visuals never probe/import Python.

Evidence:
- test/media/manim-cuts.test.mjs: five passing checks. Cheap Python AST unit checks accept kit math and reject external imports, malformed classes, off-brief colors/fonts, style dictionaries, aliases and house mutations without importing Manim. In-process createApp tests with fake providers/TTS/Manim render engine place math between two Remotion cuts, preserve measured 75-frame timing and ordered clip metadata, record plan/cut/retry usage, and rewrite only the failed math cut. Detection/runtime unavailability gives one clear failure/warning, no playable media or automatic retry, then normal chat and a newly generated inline visual both complete. These are explicitly fixtures, not native inference evidence.
- npm run test:render: PASS, 4 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped (80.33s). Real bubblewrap Remotion, three-cut join and Three.js checks remain passing. New mixed Remotion/Manim check renders actual LaTeX transforms plus Archivo and Literata from bundled fonts, saves the raw math clip at 1920x1080/30fps for 2.5 seconds and joined narrated MP4 at 1920x1080/30fps for 5 seconds with AAC. Pixel probes prove math appears in the second timeline position, raw math leaves the subtitle band empty, wrapper subtitles appear and the final pause fades to dark paper. The native Python sandbox probe denies home/app-data/repository reads, runtime/outside/narration writes and outbound network; only its workspace is writable and no host environment variables pass through. Fixed source and prerecorded tone narration are fixtures, while both renderers, fonts, LaTeX and sandbox evidence are native.
- Final focused native Manim rerun after disabling Python bytecode: PASS (25.58s). One extracted fixture frame was inspected; house text, equation, spacing and subtitles fit. No browser check claimed.
- Full-suite regression found and fixed: legacy fixtures recognize private video generation by the Remotion wording. The plan now accurately says narrated Remotion video with optional Manim math cuts, preserving that existing contract. All 24 checks in affected playback/jobs/requests/tag/deletion/usage files pass (20 passed, 4 opt-in native skips). Initial full run was stopped after diagnosing its hung playback fixture; this was repaired, not waived.
- Final npm test: PASS, 367 total, 363 passed, 4 opt-in native renders skipped (all passed separately), 0 failed (12.66s).
- npm run format:check, ruff format --check for the new Python files, 500-line JS/TS/CSS gate and git diff --check: PASS. Impeccable detector: [].

Limits: no live model or Edge TTS service requests, browser/E2E run, new live player or cursor/sketch work. Live playback remains its separate dependent feature; this issue provides the ordered clip and the MP4 timeline. No build required by testing.md: no TSX/build files changed; actual generated TSX wrappers compiled during native renders. No docs/verification files regenerated. Current master branch preserved; existing .beads/issues.jsonl changes retained. Files: server/app.mjs; server/http/jobs/media.mjs; server/media/{video-plan,video-cuts,videos,video-sandbox,manim-cut}.mjs; server/media/{manim-kit,manim-render}.py; test/media/{video-plan,videos-playback,manim-cuts}.test.mjs; test/media/manim-validation.py; test/support/video-kit.mjs; required local Beads export/progress. Nothing staged, committed, pushed, pulled or remotely synced. Ralph owns the pending implementation commit.

title: Manim install on first run
description:
## What to build
npm start creates a project-local Python environment with uv on first run and installs a pinned Manim, beside the npm install step. If Cairo/Pango headers or LaTeX are missing, startup stops with the exact apt or brew command. A usable Manim is detected for later video jobs. Chat and visuals do not depend on it. See the spec's Manim cuts section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit test: the dependency check reports the exact install command for missing Cairo/Pango or LaTeX, and passes when present (injected probes).
- [ ] Running npm start on this machine creates the environment and reports Manim ready.
- [ ] .venv/ is git-ignored.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes: Implementation decisions: pin Manim 0.22.1 (verified against PyPI/current official install guide); uv provisions Python 3.12 into git-ignored project .venv, avoiding the system Python 3.14 dependency surface. Existing environments are repaired in place, never removed. Missing Cairo/Pango/pkg-config or latex/dvisvgm stops launcher with exact apt/Homebrew commands; system packages are never auto-installed. Missing uv gives official install command. Exported detectManim returns availability, pinned version and absolute Python path without throwing; no Python dependency added to chat/visual imports. Existing built app remains accessible via node server/main.mjs during setup repair. Scope includes launcher, setup/detection modules, README, ignore rule, cheapest unit tests and existing launcher fixtures; no cut rendering implementation in this issue. Initial native npm start created .venv with CPython 3.12.12, built pycairo/ManimPango, installed Manim 0.22.1 and printed Manim ready. App responded HTTP 200 on 127.0.0.1:40725 using isolated temporary data; native Text and MathTex creation passed (Cairo/Pango plus LaTeX/dvisvgm). Final verification: focused node --test test/scripts/manim.test.mjs test/http/launcher.test.mjs passed 8/8. npm test ran once at the end: 361 total, 358 passed, 3 opt-in render tests skipped, 0 failed (12.75s). npm run format:check and git diff --check passed. A second native npm start reused Manim without installation and returned HTTP 200; both native app processes stopped afterward. git check-ignore .venv/bin/python confirmed exclusion. No docs/verification files regenerated. Linux native provisioning/text/math and restart evidence is real, while missing-dependency/macOS checks and launcher build use explicitly labelled fixtures. No browser or video render tests: this task changes installation/detection, not rendering. Existing node_modules were present during native npm start, so this is a fresh Python environment check, not a clean npm dependency installation claim. Files: .gitignore, README.md, scripts/start.mjs, scripts/manim-setup.mjs, server/media/manim.mjs, test/scripts/manim.test.mjs, test/http/launcher.test.mjs, and required local Beads export/progress. No staging, commit, push or sync; Ralph owns the pending implementation commit.

title: Live video playback
description:
## What to build
@remotion/player plays the cuts live inside an isolated sandbox iframe (opaque origin, no network, no app access), like visuals. The shell bundles the kit; each cut's compiled code loads as it becomes ready. Playback starts when cut 1 is ready and shows a buffering state at an unready cut. Once all cuts are ready the 1080p MP4 renders in the background; the video library plays the live version until the MP4 is saved. Progress phases: planning, writing cuts (n of N), narrating, playable, saving; the bar never moves backward. See the spec's Videos as cuts section (live playback, MP4, progress).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: the video becomes playable after cut 1 is ready while later cuts are pending, and reports phases in order with real counts.
- [ ] Component test: the player shows buffering at an unready cut and switches to the MP4 once it is saved.
- [ ] The live player sandbox has no network and no same-origin access (sandbox attributes and CSP asserted).
- [ ] verify-video-player smoke passes.
- [ ] npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All five acceptance criteria pass.

Implementation: a new opaque-origin player page (player.html, src/media/player.tsx) bundles @remotion/player, React, Remotion, Three, @remotion/three, r3f and the video kit (now a direct dependency pinned at 4.0.542, which was already installed transitively). The app fetches GET /api/trees/:c/artifacts/:id/cuts (pending cut-format videos only). It returns palette roles and, for each cut, its engine, timing, a playable flag and the server-compiled code (TypeScript transpileModule to a CommonJS body, given only for playable Remotion cuts). It also fetches /cuts/:i/narration and /cuts/:i/clip (Manim) as blobs, then posts everything to the frame. The frame defines each cut through an inline script its CSP allows, with require() limited to the kit and libraries. A cut is playable when it has code, measured narration and, for Manim, its rendered clip. The live composition (src/media/liveVideo.tsx) mirrors CUT_ENTRY: ground, fade, narration audio, 120px subtitle band. An unready cut renders a "Loading the next cut…" state that calls useBufferState().delayPlayback(). Model code that throws shows the bare ground.

Phases: planning, writing (n of N cuts written), narrating (cut 1 code written, narration pending), playable (cut 1 ready, n of N cuts ready), saving (MP4 cut renders plus join and publish, real render progress and frame total). They are derived from saved cut state in generateVideo. The job layer drops any earlier phase, so the step and bar never move backward. Logs: narration (with counts) and playable are now logged from cut state, and saving and 25% render steps are logged in the saving phase.

Decisions and tradeoffs: the artifact stays pending until the MP4 is saved, so Cancel and progress keep their meaning. The chat card shows the live player from playable onward, with status, elapsed time and Cancel at the top right, and switches to the native MP4 player when ready. /api/videos lists running playable or saving videos first, with live:<conversation>. Library cards play them live with no file actions until the MP4 exists. There is no autoplay, matching the ready MP4. An untimed cut holds a 3 s placeholder. A cut keeps its first narration and clip blobs; a re-rendered Manim clip appears only in the saved MP4. The narration and clip routes and cuts polling are left out of request logs. The player CSP is the visual sandbox policy plus media-src blob:. The app frame-src allows only sandbox.html and player.html.

Evidence:
- test/media/videos-live.test.mjs (createApp, gated fake provider, narration and render). It observes planning, then writing 0/2, then narrating, then playable 1/2, then saving, in order. While cut 2 is being written: cut 1 is served as compiled code (no JSX or import left), its timing is 75 frames, and its narration bytes match. Cut 2 narration, a non-Manim clip, an out-of-range index and the wrong conversation all return 404. The library lists the video live. Saving reports progress 0.2 and 150 frames and never goes backward. After ready, /cuts returns 404 and the library entry becomes a normal saved video.
- test/media/live-player.test.mjs (jsdom). A Remotion Thumbnail shows cut 1 with its caption, then the buffering state at the unready cut 2. VideoCard in the playable phase renders iframe src=/player.html sandbox=allow-scripts and no <video>, and posts cut data with a narration Blob after load. When the status becomes ready it switches to the MP4 <video src=…/media>. A live library entry gets the iframe and no buttons.
- test/http/app.test.mjs: app frame-src lists only sandbox.html and player.html. Both sandbox pages have default-src, connect-src, frame-src and worker-src 'none', frame-ancestors set to the app origin, and no unsafe-eval or remote hosts. Only player.html adds media-src blob:.
- verify-video-player smoke (production build, headless Chrome, real bubblewrap Remotion renders): 14/14 PASS. Includes new checks for the live opaque-origin player: contentDocument is null, the served CSP blocks the network, cut 1 is visible, Play then buffers at cut 2, the buffer clears once cut 2 is written, and the player then switches to the 5 s MP4. Synthetic providers and fixture narration, no native inference or speech. Output went to the ignored .verify-output; docs/verification is untouched.
- npm run test:render: PASS 4/4 (phase-order assertion updated).
- npm test: PASS, 405 tests, 401 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. npm run build: PASS. prettier --check and git diff --check: PASS.

Limits: no live provider or Edge TTS calls, and no Manim cut played live in a browser (Manim clip blobs are covered by the route and the composition only). Pixel sharpness at full screen was not measured.

title: Video emphasis tools: cursor and sketch pen
description:
## What to build
The kit gains Cursor (frame-space targets timed to sentence frames, optional label bubble) and Sketch (circle, underline, arrow, freehand with a hand-drawn wobble, drawn progressively, fading when narration moves on). They render as one overlay layer above every cut, Manim cuts included. The prompt tells the model when to use them and that Manim cuts rarely need them. See the spec's Emphasis tools section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit test: cursor position and sketch stroke progress at given frames match their timed targets and fade-out.
- [ ] The prompt documents Cursor and Sketch usage.
- [ ] npm run test:render passes with a cut using both tools.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All four acceptance criteria pass.

Implementation: the kit (server/media/video-kit.tsx) gains Cursor and Sketch components plus pure timing helpers cursorAt, sketchAt and sketchPath. Marks come from an optional per-cut `emphasis` array in the plan: cursor {sentence, x, y, label?} and sketch {shape: circle|underline|arrow|freehand, sentence, points} in 1920x1080 frame space. The cursor fades in at its first target, glides 15 frames to each target as that target's sentence starts, shows the label after it arrives, and fades 10 frames after the last sentence ends. A sketch draws over min(20 frames, sentence length) from its sentence start (pathLength dash offset), then fades over 10 frames once the sentence ends. Wobble is deterministic per mark: a circle overshoots its start, an arrow bows slightly and adds a head. One overlay layer: CUT_ENTRY renders Sketch and Cursor inside the cut's fade layer from staged emphasis.json, for Remotion and Manim cuts alike, and the live composition (liveVideo.tsx) does the same with emphasis served by GET /cuts. videoPlan validates marks (at most 12, integer sentence >= 0, in-frame coordinates, label <= 40 characters, 2 points for circle/underline/arrow, 2-64 for freehand) and rejects a malformed plan. PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS documents when to use each tool, says to use them sparingly, and says Manim cuts rarely need them. The cut and Manim writer prompts say to place the referenced content at those coordinates and not draw their own pointer.

Decisions and tradeoffs: marks live in the plan, not the cut code, so one implementation covers Manim cuts and the brief positions. The tradeoff is that the planner, not the cut writer, chooses coordinates, and the writer is told to match them. Ink is fixed (amber pen, paper cursor, raised label bubble) for one look regardless of brief roles. Marks naming a sentence that narration does not have are skipped at render time.

Evidence:
- test/media/video-emphasis.test.mjs (unit): cursor position, label and opacity at given frames (fade-in, hold until the next sentence, mid-glide, arrival at +15 frames, fade-out); sketch draw progress and fade at given frames; deterministic paths for all four shapes with a bounded wobble; plan validation of good and malformed marks; prompt text.
- test/media/videos-live.test.mjs: /cuts returns each cut's emphasis.
- test/media/videos-playback.test.mjs (npm run test:render, real bubblewrap Remotion render, fixture narration): a cut with a labelled cursor and an underline shows an amber pen pixel and a paper cursor pixel at 1 s, and the underline is faded at 2.2 s. The pixel helper is shared to keep the file under 500 lines.
- npm run test:render: PASS 5/5. npm test: PASS (410 tests, 405 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed). npm run build, prettier --check and git diff --check: PASS.

Limits: no live provider plan exercised emphasis. Overlay above a real Manim clip is covered by the shared CUT_ENTRY code path, not by its own pixel test. The live player overlay was not checked in a browser.

title: Videos as planned cuts
description:
## What to build
The smart model first returns a compact plan: title, description, style brief (layout areas, palette roles, recurring objects, exact terms) and ordered cuts (purpose, narration, engine, end state). Brief but clear. Cuts are written and narrated (edge-tts) in parallel; each cut gets the brief, its cut and the previous cut's end state. A cut's duration is its measured narration plus a fixed pause. A cut that fails validation (brief colors, fonts, imports outside the kit) or rendering retries alone within the attempt budget. The artifact stores the plan and ordered cuts. Cuts are joined with transitions into the MP4. Existing videos are untouched. See the spec's Videos as cuts section.
design: Implement plan-first private video generation with JSON styleBrief (named layoutAreas, paletteRoles mapping idea names to kit inks, recurringObjects with positions/colorRole, exactTerms) and ordered cuts. New artifacts reuse private source JSON for {plan,cuts}; HTTP and tutor history expose metadata only. Each cut gets exactly brief, cut and previous planned endState. Code and TTS for all cuts start in parallel; measured 30fps audio gains 15 frames (0.5s) silence. Follow existing visual repair convention: at most 2 writing attempts per cut, sharing the original 10-minute composition deadline; provider/auth/TTS failures stay final. Validation or native cut render failure retries only that cut, reusing narration. Render cuts separately in the existing sandbox, bake eased fade-through-ground transitions into pauses, then concatenate video streams without rerendering healthy cuts (audio remux/re-encode for continuity). This favours isolated render recovery over a single all-or-nothing composition; final video uses no added renderer/dependency. TypeScript parser is promoted from existing dev dependency to runtime for syntax/import/style validation. Live player, progressive per-cut UI and Manim runtime remain later dependent issues. Existing saved rows/files are never migrated or rerendered.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Unit test: plan and style-brief validation accepts a good plan and rejects a malformed one.
- [x] Integration test with fake provider and narration: a plan with three cuts writes all cuts and narration in parallel and stores them in order with durations including the pause.
- [x] Integration test: a cut breaking the brief is rewritten alone; other cuts are not regenerated.
- [x] Integration test: usage is recorded for the plan and each cut call.
- [x] npm run test:render passes with a multi-cut video.
- [x] npm test passes.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All six acceptance criteria pass.

Implementation: smart first returns a size-bounded JSON plan with title, description, styleBrief (layout areas, palette roles, named/positioned recurring objects, exact terms) and ordered cuts (purpose, fixed narration, engine, endState). Each isolated cut-writing call receives only the brief, its cut, and the preceding planned endState, with a fixed validation/render repair hint when needed. All writers and Edge TTS requests start concurrently. Actual narration files are measured with ffprobe; each cut adds 15 frames (0.5 seconds) at 30fps. Code validation parses TypeScript/TSX syntax and checks import/resource restrictions, declared brief inks, color literals and house fonts, including aliases. Validation or cut rendering failure repairs that cut alone, at most two writing attempts inside the original composition deadline; audio is reused and provider/auth/TTS failures remain final.

The artifact source field now privately persists {plan,cuts} with engine, code, narration timings and status in plan order, using an attempt/status ownership guard. Video source is stripped from all public representations and never enters tutor/compaction history. No schema migration or regeneration of old videos. New versions use the cut format and preserve prior library media. TypeScript was already installed; it moves from dev to runtime dependencies for validation.

Render decision: separate sandboxed cut renders, with eased fade-through-ground transitions and a silent pause, followed by a sandboxed concat using Remotion's shipped FFmpeg; video streams are copied and audio re-encoded into one MP4. This preserves per-cut render recovery and avoids rendering healthy cuts again. CPU render concurrency remains 2. Cut workspaces still mask the entire app data root and retain read-only narration. Parallel failures drain writer/audio operations before cleaning temporary files. A regression discovered in the full suite is fixed: a ready video can regenerate while its previous job cleans up, since the new version owns a different id; pending videos still return 409. A deterministic route unit test first reproduced that 409, then passed with the fix.

Evidence:
- test/media/video-plan.test.mjs: good/malformed plans and briefs, future engine vocabulary, size bounds; valid kit code and aliases, off-brief colors/fonts, unsupported imports/resources and syntax rejection.
- test/media/video-cuts.test.mjs: createApp with fake provider/TTS/render; all three writers and narrators reach gates before any are released, complete in reverse order, and persist ordered code/timing with 75-frame durations. Exactly four video usage events (plan plus three cuts); exactly five when one cut retries. Brief/render failures rewrite only cut 2 and never repeat other cuts or TTS; exhausted repair fails honestly.
- Existing video requests, frozen Claude/Codex protocol adapters/custom endpoint roles, usage, narration, Stop/Cancel, restart, ownership, publication failures, tree deletion and library preservation pass with updated plan/cut fixtures. Tag-style video requests now also assert ready completion.
- npm run test:render: PASS, 3 tests, 0 skipped. Five actual bubblewrap-isolated Remotion cut renders (2D and Three.js) plus a native three-cut MP4 join. The multi-cut file is 1920x1080 at 30fps, AAC audio, 7.5 seconds within one frame of expected length. Native pixel probes show a visible cube, dark transition during the pause, then the next visible cut. Compositions and prerecorded sine-tone narration are fixtures, not live inference/speech evidence.
- Final npm test: PASS, 355 tests; 352 passed, 3 real-render tests intentionally skipped in the ordinary suite (all passed separately above), 0 failed.
- npm run build: PASS (bundle-size advisory only). npm run format:check, 500-line code-size gate, git diff --check: PASS. Impeccable detector: [].
- Native live verification scripts were updated for plan/cut storage, bounded calls, per-cut TTS/timing and private worker context; they were not run. No docs/verification artifacts regenerated.

Limits: no live model or Edge TTS service calls, browser/E2E verification, throughput benchmark, live player or Manim runtime claimed. The latter features remain dependent issues. Existing browser subtitle-geometry coverage limits remain in docs/agents/testing.md. Current branch master preserved; nothing staged, committed, pushed, pulled or remotely synced. Ralph owns the pending commit.

title: Faster, sharper video jobs
description:
## What to build
A video request starts when its request block closes during streaming, like visuals; Stop cancels it only while the reply streams. Videos render at 1920x1080, 30 fps, with a 120px subtitle band of at most two lines; the kit frame constants, prompt and Three canvas size match. MP4 render concurrency rises above 1. Works on today's single-composition videos. See the spec's Videos as cuts section (start time, frame).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Integration test: a video request whose block closes mid-stream starts its job before the reply finishes.
- [ ] Integration test: Stop during streaming cancels the job; finishing the reply does not.
- [ ] The composition and kit frame are 1920x1080 with a 120px subtitle band.
- [ ] npm run test:render passes and the rendered file is 1920x1080.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All acceptance criteria pass. Implementation: closed valid video request blocks enter the existing detached media queue during the tutor stream; startVideo links its abort controller to that reply only, and returns its existing completion promise. Stop cancels pending videos only for the streaming reply; ready videos survive, and normal reply completion (or a later tutor failure) leaves already-started video work running. Each request starts once. A later conflicting request fails/aborts a still-pending video; late results cannot publish. Existing unsolicited/malformed/duplicate validation, frozen smart selection, explicit Cancel/Retry, ownership and saved-video behavior remain covered. Background callbacks no longer read the store after their reply has finished.

Render decision: fixed concurrency 2, the smallest increase above 1, bounds CPU/memory compared with scaling to host CPU count; no throughput benchmark claimed. New single-composition jobs render 1920x1080 at 30 fps. The wrapper takes width, height and subtitle-band height from the copied kit frame (1920x1080, subtitles 120); the prompt and ThreeCanvas fixture match. Captions retain a two-line clamp, with 40px/1.2 text and a 12px bottom inset so two lines fit within 120px. Existing saved videos are not migrated or rerendered.

title: Progressive visuals
description:
## What to build
While a visual is pending, its accumulated partial markup streams to the client and is written into the existing sandbox iframe progressively, scripts held back. On completion the final sanitized fragment replaces it and its scripts run. Partial markup passes the same sanitizer as final markup. Failure or Stop discards the partial render and shows the existing failure state. No JSONL/op format. See the spec's Progressive visuals section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Unit test: the partial-markup sanitizer removes scripts and unsafe attributes from incomplete fragments.
- [x] Integration test: a fake provider streaming a visual in chunks yields partial artifact updates before ready, then the final fragment.
- [x] Integration test: Stop or a mid-stream failure leaves the visual failed with no partial markup kept.
- [x] npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Implementation decision: reuse pending artifact.source for sanitized in-memory snapshots only (no DB writes/schema or model format change); expose via existing SSE artifact events while the reply is open and existing polling after it ends. Keep one iframe across pending/ready, replacing markup and running scripts only at final completion. Share one DOM sanitizer between server snapshots/final output and sandbox writes, retaining strict existing final validation. Stop will now use the existing failed/Retry state with null source, per this issue acceptance, rather than hiding canceled visuals. Scope: visual worker, media job live projection, reply event callback, visual Stop storage transition, iframe host/runtime, sanitizer and focused unit/component/integration tests. No video-rendering or browser acceptance changes.
Verified 2026-11-14: visual workers publish accumulated, sanitized markup through existing artifact SSE updates while the reply streams, and the existing live/polling projection after the reply ends. Pending source stays in the running job only; SQLite keeps null until ready. No schema, dependency, model-output format, video-rendering or queue-policy additions.

The shared visualMarkup sanitizer handles incomplete HTML/SVG, strips scripts and event handlers while pending, and removes embedded resources, unsafe URL attributes and external CSS resources in both modes. Existing strict final validation remains. The sandbox sanitizes again on write; one opaque-origin allow-scripts frame receives partial replacements, holds scripts and part activation until complete, then replaces the fragment and executes its scripts in order. Its completed guard ignores subsequent renders. Existing CSP, bounded height reports, theme delivery, enlarge and branch validation remain. Failure unmounts the partial frame; Stop now saves failed/null-source with a cancellation reason and the existing explicit Retry action. Ready visuals remain intact; late output cannot publish. Tradeoff: detached visuals use the existing polling cadence rather than a new persistent stream, and accumulated markup is reparsed rather than introducing operation-based rendering.

Evidence: node --import ./test/support/tsx.mjs --test test/media/visual*.test.mjs test/media/inline-media.test.mjs test/media/artifacts-stop.test.mjs passed 38/38. New sanitizer/DOM tests cover incomplete fragments, unsafe attributes/resources, inert partial writes and ordered final script execution; new fake-provider createApp tests prove multiple partial SSE artifacts precede ready, final-item replacement, partial polling, no partial persistence, mid-stream failure/Stop cleanup and late-output rejection. Component coverage proves latest-source delivery after frame load, frame identity across pending/ready, suppressed pending branching and failure/Retry. Updated Stop queue coverage proves explicit retry succeeds; the mocked deadline test now awaits provider entry after lazy parser import. An initial plain-node targeted glob lacked the repository TS loader for existing visual-parts imports; rerunning with its documented loader passed.

Final gates: npm test run once: 401 total, 397 pass, 4 opt-in native video-render tests skipped, 0 failures. npm run build passed on final source (bundle-size advisory only); npm run format:check and git diff --check passed. Video rendering was not changed, so test:render was not run. No docs/verification artifacts regenerated. Pre-existing design-sidecar notice and unrelated work left alone. Current branch retained; no staging, commit or remote operations. Ralph commit pending.

title: Server logging for npm start
description:
## What to build
npm start prints one plain line per meaningful event: API requests (method, path, status, ms; skip static assets and keepalive/polling), model calls (task, provider, model, tokens, ms, failure cause) logged where usage is metered, media job stages (plan, cuts, narration, playable, render progress every 25%, saved, failed), and warnings/errors with their cause and next step. createApp takes an injected log function defaulting to stdout/stderr. No log files, no levels flag. Never log learner text, model output or credentials. Existing startup lines stay. See the spec's Server logging section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit test: the formatter produces single-line entries with time, level, area and fields.
- [ ] Integration test via createApp with a captured log: a chat request logs the request line and a model-call line with task, model, tokens and duration; a failing fake provider logs the error cause.
- [ ] Integration test: a static asset and a polling request produce no lines.
- [ ] Integration test: learner question and reply text never appear in captured lines.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes:
Implementation decisions (2026-11-14): one terminal formatter and injected createApp log sink; INFO to stdout, WARN/ERROR to stderr. Log generation at the existing chat, suggestion and background usage boundaries without changing accounting. Keep usage task categories; add stage=visual/plan/cut to distinguish media calls. Omit static/media assets, GET state/previews/tree/artifact polling and all query strings; retain route UUIDs but mask arbitrary path segments. Unknown formatter fields are dropped, and known call inputs/output plus credential-shaped diagnostics are redacted while retaining provider causes and next steps. Video progress is monotonic in the log at 25/50/75/100; current playable means first rendered cut ready (live playback belongs to the later video slice). Existing startup lines unchanged. Scope: server/log.mjs, createApp, roles, send/suggestion/media jobs, video stage callbacks, captured-log tests and updated Manim warning assertions. No UI, dependency, storage schema, render-engine, provider-auth or startup changes. Focused formatter/HTTP/privacy/tasks/media/usage/suggestions/compaction/startup tests pass with fixture providers, narration and rendering. Full suite and formatting gate next; no native provider/browser acceptance is named.
Verified result (2026-11-14): all requested logging behavior implemented. server/log.mjs formats ISO time, level, area, event and allowlisted metadata as one plain line; default sink sends info to stdout and warnings/errors to stderr, without files or flags. createApp wraps API responses with method/path/status/ms and skips assets/media and polling. Shared generation logger covers chat, suggestions, compaction, legacy diagrams, visual attempts, video plan and cut calls, including starts, actual model, provider-reported counts or unreported, duration, failure causes and next steps; timeout differs from learner cancellation. Existing metering remains unchanged. Provider receiver is preserved for stateful/native catalog calls. Media logs plan, cut count/written count, narration, rendering, first-cut playable, 25/50/75/100 percent once despite repeated/regressing callbacks, saving/saved, warning/failure or stop. Manim warnings retain cause and repair step. Privacy checks cover question/reply/history, JSON worker input and generated markup/code, query/path content, bearer/API-key patterns and credentials in URLs; arbitrary formatter fields are discarded. No startup lines were changed.

Validation: targeted formatter/HTTP captured-log tests and existing usage-history, suggestions, compaction, diagrams/visual failures, video jobs/failures/playback, Manim and startup tests passed. npm test run once: 386 total, 382 pass, 4 opt-in native-render skips, 0 failures (13.55s); includes size gate. npm run format:check passed. No docs/verification files regenerated. Preserved pre-existing Beads export change, stayed on master, and did not stage/commit or use remotes. Ralph owns the pending commit.

title: Branch from a tagged part of a visual
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-zhf

## What to build

Workers tag clickable parts with a short label and one-line explanation; the sandbox makes them focusable and keyboard/pointer activatable and posts only a branch request. The app validates frame, ready visual and bounded strings, opens the passage box for the part, and stores the visual title, description, label and explanation as the branch passage text, marked as coming from that visual artifact (no text offsets). Inherited context compacts as today; no image input. Spec: Branch from a visual.

Load the parent epic in full, including comments, and the linked specification before starting. Deliver this slice through persistence, server/API behavior and learner-facing UI as applicable, with meaningful tests in the same slice. Use the HTTP integration seam first and focused UI checks (built UI, fixture provider, agent-browser) where needed; no broad E2E suite. Frontend work uses Impeccable, suitable Astryx components and existing theme tokens. Preserve keyboard access, both appearances, unrelated work and provider/session safety. Keep Git local; do not push, pull or sync.
design: Reuse the passage popup and branch endpoint. Visual requests carry artifactId, label and explanation; server derives immutable passage text from the ready owned visual title/description and bounded part strings. Nullable start/end distinguish visual sources without invented offsets. Persist artifactId/label/explanation for map reveal and explored-part reopening; visual regeneration retains existing child context. No image input, new provider call type, UI redesign or dependency. Verify HTTP behavior first, then focused built-UI keyboard/pointer checks in both appearances.
acceptance_criteria:
[x] Clicking or activating a tagged part opens the passage box and creates a branch whose passage carries the visual and part text (HTTP integration + focused UI check).
[x] Invalid or unknown-frame messages are ignored.
[x] Map, reopen and explored state work for visual branches.
notes:
Verified the whole visual-branch slice against the full parent epic (no initial comments), PRD.md, GLOSSARY.md and docs/inline-visuals-spec.md. TreeTutor-zhf.5 is closed. Stayed on the current branch; preserved the pre-existing reply-retry work, Ralph configuration and other dirty files. No staging, commit, push, pull or sync.

Result and scope:
- server/store.mjs migrates the immediately preceding branches schema transactionally: existing text branches keep their data/API shape; visual branches persist artifactId, label and explanation with NULL start/end. Both detailed tree and map-state APIs expose visual provenance. Deleting a child naturally removes its explored state.
- server/app.mjs reuses the branch endpoint and quick-thinking compaction. It requires a completed owned source reply and a ready visual belonging to that reply/conversation; label/explanation use the same bounded, nonempty, single-line validation as iframe messages. Visual requests cannot smuggle text offsets or suggestion anchors. Passage text is derived from the saved visual title/description plus part label/explanation; client-supplied passage text cannot replace that metadata. Child model/effort inheritance, independent sessions, recursive compaction and parent isolation stay on the existing path. No screenshot, image input, generated source or worker transcript enters child/compaction input.
- src/sandbox.ts makes valid tagged SVG/HTML parts and asynchronously added parts focusable, labelled and pointer/Enter/Space activatable. Native branch buttons activate once; ordinary controls keep their own actions. The sandbox posts only the existing fixed-shape part request (besides height); CSP, opaque origin and provider permissions remain unchanged. Explored/revealed parts use current theme tokens in sandbox.html. A one-shot pending reveal handles parts inserted after the host message.
- src/VisualFrame.tsx and src/ChatPage.tsx connect both inline and legacy-positioned visuals to the existing Astryx passage popup. Opening it makes no provider call; explicit submission creates the child. Escape returns to the source frame. Enlarged views close before opening the question so their focus trap cannot capture it. Known-frame checks, ready state and bounded messages gate activation. The host sends only label/explanation for explored/reveal state, without conversation/child IDs or passage data.
- src/TreeOverview.tsx distinguishes visual and text source reveals. Map branches remain attached to their originating reply; reveal scrolls/focuses the tagged part, and activating an explored part reopens its child without compaction or inference. Reload/server-store reopen preserve provenance and explored state.
- src/artifacts.ts shares the part type, strict message validator and passage formatter. server/prompts/visual.md clarifies that workers tag explanatory parts or dedicated branch buttons, not ordinary controls/interactive containers. No dependency or provider setting changed.

Routine decisions/tradeoffs:
- Reuse the existing inline keyboard passage form for visual questions; do not add geometry or arbitrary action fields to the iframe protocol. Keep the current completed-source/active-conversation rules for session safety.
- Part identity is artifactId plus the exact trimmed label and explanation. Passage text is frozen at creation; regeneration never rewrites a child's inherited passage. No visual version history or image capture was added.
- The branch table records artifact provenance without a new foreign-key dependency on mutable artifact rows. Existing text responses omit the new nullable visual-only fields, preserving their public shape.

Acceptance evidence:
- Full suite: rtk test node --test test/*.test.mjs passed (zero failures). After the delayed-reveal review fix and final host-state narrowing, the focused visual/branch HTTP regressions also passed: test/visual-branch.test.mjs, test/branch.test.mjs, test/branch-lifecycle.test.mjs and test/visuals.test.mjs.
- test/visual-branch.test.mjs adds three HTTP integration groups: exact frozen visual/part passage, quick-thinking and child input/session isolation, API/store reopen without inference, foreign/missing/non-ready/wrong-kind sources, malformed and boundary-sized strings, forged offsets/suggestion flag, CSRF, deletion/explored state, and migration of an existing current-version database with saved text branches. The positive case was observed failing with HTTP 400 before implementation, then passing.
- Final rtk npm run build passed TypeScript and production Vite. Only the existing large-chunk advisory remains. git diff --check passed; index remains empty.
- node scripts/verify-visual-branch.mjs passed seven focused built-UI groups using isolated SQLite, a synthetic provider and an agent-browser-owned browser. Actual keyboard/pointer events exercised SVG/HTML/dynamic/native-button activation, popup focus and Escape, ordinary control behavior, malformed and unknown-frame messages, enlarged-frame activation, explicit branch creation with child focus, source-message map attachment, source-part reveal/focus, explored reopening without inference, asynchronous source reveal, reload and all four light/dark desktop/narrow combinations. Evidence: docs/verification/visual-branch.json and .impeccable/review/visual-branch-{desktop,narrow}-{light,dark}.png. All four captures were visually inspected. The script asserts absolute screenshot paths exist.
- node scripts/verify-passage-selection.mjs passed its focused built-app mouse/keyboard selection, branch HTTP, focus, reload/reveal, Markdown/streaming and appearance checks.
- node scripts/verify-visual-sandbox.mjs passed isolation, frame protocol, app/sandbox CSP, theme/fonts, inline placement, map previews without frames, legacy Mermaid, hover/focus and enlarge/Escape checks. Its old opacity assertions targeted the button after opacity moved to the action group in the previous slice; corrected those selectors and added a bounded hover diagnostic. No production hover behavior was changed.
- Impeccable detector: []; Astryx doctor: 18 pass, 3 pre-existing warnings, 0 failures. Existing font probe/agent-doc markers and Impeccable sidecar drift were not repaired.
- Matt implementation/code-review workflow: spec review found no gaps; standards review identified delayed-part source focus, now fixed and verified with the delayed-part browser fixture.

Limits/handoff:
- Current-slice inference checks are synthetic fixtures, not native Claude/Codex inference or a screen-reader/hardware-device audit. No new native-provider acceptance is required here; the prerequisite contains its own gated native visual evidence. No broad E2E suite was added.

Hover/focus control on ready visuals and ready videos reruns that artifact's worker from the stored request plus an instruction to take a different approach. notes:

Videos receive a fresh artifact/job id by atomically updating the existing chat row, retaining its message, position, creation order and frozen request; the old video library row/file stay independently owned. A frozen differentVersion marker adds a trusted worker instruction without sending previous source or tutor sessions. Keep existing smart selection/effort, failure Retry and startup recovery. Reuse Astryx hover/focus actions and theme tokens; no redesign or version UI. Result 2026-11-11 (fixtures; no native provider needed: this slice adds no provider/prompt surface beyond a trusted instruction suffix). Implementation from d032312 (POST /api/trees/:id/artifacts/:aid/regenerate; visuals keep id, source replaced, no history; videos get a new artifact id + attempt on the same chat row, previous library row/media stay; frozen request+selection + differentVersion marker; ready-only, CSRF, ownership, one-at-a-time 409). This run: HTTP integration tests test/visuals.test.mjs + test/videos.test.mjs ("Try a different version ..."): in-place replacement, frozen selection, previous source never sent, usage metered, 403/404/409 guards, library keeps both videos, chat shows only newest. Fixed pre-existing order flake in videos.test "cancel stops only its own job" (wait for A render before B). title: Generate visuals with parallel smart-model workers as the reply streams
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-zhf

## What to build

Tutor instructions switch new replies from Mermaid to visual requests with the agreed when-to-visualize rule and early block placement. Each visual gets its own smart-model worker started when its block closes in the stream, max 3 concurrent per reply, queued in reply order, receiving earlier visual titles of the reply. Worker prompt based on CopilotKit/OpenIntelligentUI (MIT, notice kept) with the specified removals and our own appended rules; no leaked or unlicensed prompt text. Server validation of output, one automatic retry on invalid output, then failed with Retry. Stop cancels the reply and all of its pending/running visuals (canceled, placeholders removed). Worker permissions reuse existing restrictions. Spec: Visual worker.

Load the parent epic in full, including comments, and the linked specification before starting. Deliver this slice through persistence, server/API behavior and learner-facing UI as applicable, with meaningful tests in the same slice. Use the HTTP integration seam first and focused UI checks (built UI, fixture provider, agent-browser) where needed; no broad E2E suite. Frontend work uses Impeccable, suitable Astryx components and existing theme tokens. Preserve keyboard access, both appearances, unrelated work and provider/session safety. Keep Git local; do not push, pull or sync.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Workers start before the reply ends when a block closes; cap of 3 holds (HTTP integration with fake provider).
[ ] Invalid worker output retried once automatically, then failed with reason and Retry.
[ ] Stop cancels every visual of the turn; no further worker calls.
[ ] Worker uses the smart model selection and effort; usage recorded as today.
[ ] Prompt file carries the MIT notice; contains no leaked text.
[ ] Gated live smoke check renders a real visual.
notes:
Verified TreeTutor-zhf.5 on master against the full parent epic (no comments), PRD.md and docs/inline-visuals-spec.md. Both technical prerequisites are closed. Implemented this whole slice; no staging, commit or remote operations.

Result:
- New tutor instructions use treetutor-visual blocks for structures, processes, quantities, comparisons and spatial ideas; one idea per block, early placement, text-only short factual/casual replies and visuals whenever explicitly requested. Legacy treetutor-diagram handling remains compatible, and saved Mermaid diagrams are unchanged.
- A closed block immediately creates a durable positioned visual and starts an isolated smart-model worker while tutor text continues. Each reply owns a FIFO with at most three running workers. Every worker receives only its frozen bounded request and earlier visual titles, plus the frozen smart selection/effort; no tutor session, transcript or source from other visuals. Ready visual metadata alone enters later history.
- Server validation checks a 64 KiB / 32-item bound, fragment-only output, JavaScript syntax, resource attributes, network APIs/URLs, CSS resources and unavailable library/import use. Exactly one fresh automatic attempt follows invalid output; provider, model-selection and deadline failures do not automatically retry. Worker diagnostics remain private and failures have server-authored actionable reasons.
- Explicit Retry reuses the durable request on the same artifact without another learner message. It uses the existing detached-job lifecycle and ownership/CSRF/duplicate guards. Opening/restarting never starts inference. Stop aborts the reply and running workers, cancels queued/running visuals and removes their focused-chat placeholders and preview rows; ready visuals stay. Deletion cannot recreate content or stop another reply. Shutdown recovery marks unfinished visuals failed without replay.
- Inline VisualFrame now offers an Astryx Retry button, preserves keyboard context after Retry and hides canceled visuals. Retry callbacks preserve the Markdown memoization. Smart settings and usage labels explain visuals. The sandbox waits for source installation before its first height report, fixing an empty-height race found by the native smoke.
- server/prompts/visual.md is our adaptation of only the specified MIT OpenIntelligentUI main/advanced sections, pinned at 8391a94c1c3939c679e40ddd7bfc08a9ef690e70. Full MIT copyright/permission notice is in the prompt and beside it. README records provenance and excluded sections. No SVG-diagram skill, leaked or unlicensed prompt source was used.

Routine decisions/tradeoffs:
- New visuals use a new treetutor-visual tag with the existing four-field format; retain the old diagram path for compatibility rather than regenerate history. The old six-request limit remains for legacy diagrams; new visuals queue under the specified concurrency cap.
- Snapshot smart settings when a request closes and persist the resolved model before inference; queued work and explicit Retry retain that selection. Each automatic attempt has a separate usage event in the existing diagram category (UI label: Visuals and diagrams), avoiding an unnecessary usage-schema migration.
- Use an overall 60-second worker budget for the two possible attempts (120 seconds only in the gated native smoke). Output validation catches mistakes; the opaque-origin iframe and its network-denied CSP remain the actual execution boundary. No new dependency or provider fallback was added.
- Reuse existing Astryx Button/Skeleton/Dialog, theme tokens and the current inline layout. No redesign, branch-from-visual behavior, different-version action or inline-video work; those remain later slices.

Acceptance evidence:
- npm test: 202/202 passed. test/visuals.test.mjs adds ten HTTP integration groups, including streaming closure/hidden prefix, seven ordered visuals with a three-worker cap, smart model/effort freezing, per-attempt reported usage, source/transcript isolation, invalid-output repair and exhausted retry, safe model/provider failures, deadlines/late events, ownership/CSRF/duplicate Retry, no duplicate learner messages, durable malformed requests, restart without inference, concurrent reply queues and deletion isolation. description:
## Parent

## What to build

Inline borderless placement at full column width with auto-height, description as accessible label, shimmer while pending, enlarge on hover/focus. Existing Mermaid artifacts render unchanged; map previews never load the sandbox. Uses fixture visual sources; the worker comes in the next slice. Spec: Visual artifacts, Sandbox and rendering.

Load the parent epic in full, including comments, and the linked specification before starting. Deliver this slice through persistence, server/API behavior and learner-facing UI as applicable, with meaningful tests in the same slice. acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Fixture visuals render inline at their recorded position, transparent, auto-height, in light and dark.
[ ] Pending shimmer holds position without layout jump on arrival.
[ ] A hostile fixture visual cannot fetch, read app storage/DOM or send messages other than height and branch requests.
[ ] Main app CSP unchanged except framing the sandbox page.
[ ] Existing Mermaid artifacts and databases keep working; map previews unchanged.
[ ] HTTP integration covers positions and migration; focused UI check covers rendering and isolation.
notes:
Result (2026-11-11): implemented and verified with fixtures only (no live provider; none needed for this slice).

Built:
- Persistence: artifacts.kind gains 'visual'; new nullable artifacts.position. Migrated in place on every start (rebuildArtifacts marker check, inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE), same rebuild as the 'interrupted' migration; existing rows keep NULL position. finishArtifact accepts visual; restart marks pending visuals failed ("Visual generation was interrupted…").
- Positions: diagramReply records the offset in the stored text where each request block was removed; mermaid and video artifacts created from now on store it. Reply text and passage offsets unchanged.
- Sandbox: sandbox.html + src/sandbox.ts (second Vite input). Preloads mermaid, three, KaTeX, d3 (d3 7.9.2 added as a direct dependency; it was already installed via mermaid). Own CSP: default-src 'none', connect/frame/worker 'none', scripts/styles/fonts only from the app origin plus inline (the visual's own fragment), img data:/blob:, frame-ancestors app. iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" only. App sends theme tokens (all --* custom properties of the frame element + color scheme; re-sent when appearance changes) and source; sandbox posts only height. App validator (visualMessage) accepts exactly {type:'height',height} (clamped 0..4000) and {type:'branch',label<=120,explanation<=280} from that frame's window; everything else ignored. Branch requests are validated but not acted on yet (shortcut comment; branch-from-visual slice).
- Main app CSP unchanged except frame-src <origin>/sandbox.html. Opaque-origin GETs of /assets/* get ACAO: null (module scripts/fonts need CORS); all other requests keep the cross-site/origin check (API still 403 for Origin: null).
- UI: VisualFrame (Astryx Skeleton, IconButton, Dialog; theme tokens). Positioned visuals render inside the reply before the first top-level Markdown block at/after their offset; unpositioned visuals render after the reply like other artifacts. Borderless, transparent, full column width, height from reported content; description is the frame's title (accessible name); shimmer (~4 lines) while pending, with sr-only status; enlarge control shown on hover/focus opens a Dialog. Mermaid and video cards unchanged (still after the reply; inline videos are their own slice). Map previews show "Visual: title" rows and never load the sandbox. GLOSSARY gains "Visual".

Decisions/tradeoffs:
- Loading frames sit transparent (opacity 0) over the shimmer instead of visibility:hidden, because Chrome does not render hidden cross-origin frames (no ResizeObserver → no height).
- 'unsafe-inline' scripts in the sandbox: the visual's code is inline by design; isolation comes from the opaque origin + CSP network denial, not from script restrictions.
- Positions are recorded for mermaid/video too (shared parser); only visuals use them in the UI for now.
- shortcut: three ships no types; `declare module 'three'` in vite-env.d.ts.

Evidence:
- npm test: 185/185 pass. New HTTP tests in test/artifacts.test.mjs: "artifacts record where their request block was removed…" (positions 17/42, stored text exact, branch on later passage still 201) and "an existing database gains the visual kind in place…" (old schema rejects visual; reopened DB keeps user_version 1, old Mermaid row served with NULL position and source, visual insert/finish works). test/videos.test.mjs old-schema fixture gained the position column (it writes through current Store code).

Screenshots inspected for light and dark: transparent, no opaque iframe backdrop.

title: Retry failed or crash-interrupted replies in place
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-zhf

## What to build

Messages record why streaming stopped so a learner Stop is distinguishable from failure and crash/shutdown recovery. The latest assistant reply offers Retry when failed or crash-interrupted, never after a learner Stop or on earlier replies. Retry resends the preceding learner message with the current chat model and effort, replacing the failed reply in place without duplicating the learner message; the failed reply's artifacts are discarded but video library entries never are. New per-conversation action endpoint with the CSRF rule. Spec: Reply retry.

Load the parent epic in full, including comments, and the linked specification before starting. Deliver this slice through persistence, server/API behavior and learner-facing UI as applicable, with meaningful tests in the same slice. Use the HTTP integration seam first and focused UI checks (built UI, fixture provider, agent-browser) where needed; no broad E2E suite. Frontend work uses Impeccable, suitable Astryx components and existing theme tokens. Preserve keyboard access, both appearances, unrelated work and provider/session safety. Keep Git local; do not push, pull or sync.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Failed and crash-interrupted latest replies offer Retry; learner-stopped and earlier replies do not (HTTP integration).
[ ] Retry replaces the reply in place; no duplicate learner message; library videos survive.
[ ] Existing databases migrate; stop reason survives restart.
[ ] Focused UI check shows Retry and the replaced reply.
notes:
## TreeTutor-zhf.3 Retry failed or crash-interrupted replies in place (2026-11-11)
Result 2026-11-11 (HTTP integration with in-process fake providers + built UI via agent-browser fixture; no paid inference — the slice is provider-agnostic, it resends through the existing generate path).
Implementation: server/store.mjs adds nullable `messages.stopped` (additive ALTER, like `usage`): 'learner' on Stop, 'shutdown' on quit/crash (finish() while `stopping`, and startup/shutdown `interrupt()` streaming→interrupted). tree() exposes `stopped` on assistant messages when set. New `discardReply` deletes the failed reply row plus its artifacts/suggestions in one transaction; the `videos` library table is untouched. server/app.mjs: POST /api/trees/:id/retry (same CSRF/JSON guard and per-conversation action route); eligible only when the latest pair is user→assistant and the assistant is `failed` or `interrupted`+`shutdown`; refuses while the reply has pending media. It forgets the provider thread (fresh session gets saved history minus the failed pair), reuses the learner message id (no questionEvidence rerun) and streams a new reply row with the tree's current model/effort; `saved` event carries `replaced`. src/turn.ts withTurn drops `turn.replaced`; src/ChatPage.tsx send(text, target, retry) posts to /retry without touching the draft; "Retry reply" Astryx secondary Button beside the reply status for the latest eligible reply.
Decisions/tradeoffs: new reply id instead of reusing the old one, so the per-reply usage event (`chat:<id>`, INSERT OR IGNORE) of the retry is not swallowed by the failed attempt's; same position since it is the last message. Older interrupted rows (stopped NULL) never offer Retry, since a learner Stop cannot be told apart from a crash. Provider-reported `interrupted` without an abort records no reason (not retryable). Leftover video-work dirs of a discarded failed reply are not cleaned (failed replies never start video jobs).
Checks: test/reply-retry.test.mjs 3/3 (failed latest retried in place with current model, no duplicate question, earlier failed reply refused, completed refused, wrong CSRF 403, discarded artifacts gone, library video kept, usage saved; learner Stop recorded and refused; crash-interrupted survives restart as retryable, pre-column DB migrates, legacy interrupted refused); npm test 208/208; tsc + npm run build ok; scripts/verify-reply-retry.mjs PASS (no Retry after learner Stop, Retry in light+dark, Enter on Retry replaces reply in place, one question/one reply) → docs/verification/reply-retry-ui.json and reply-retry-*.png.

[ ] A malformed video block yields a visible failed video with reason and Retry; regression test replays it.

[ ] Retry reruns from the stored request; recovery never auto-retries.
notes:
Verified TreeTutor-zhf.2 against the parent epic (including its empty comments), PRD.md and docs/inline-visuals-spec.md, Request parsing and failure visibility. Reused and completed the task-owned changes already present in the checkout; stayed on master and preserved unrelated work.

Acceptance results:
- Extra keys are discarded and all four required string fields are trimmed to 120/280/600/1200 characters. HTTP regressions include 17,000-character fields. Missing, empty, wrong-type or control-bearing required fields, invalid/non-object JSON, malformed headers and unclosed fences still fail visibly.
- Every rejected diagram/video block gets a durable failed artifact of its own kind and a bounded, server-authored learner reason. Mixed, duplicate-video and over-limit groups retain every request instead of collapsing into one diagram failure. Provider exceptions and learner Stop also preserve requests; deletion cannot recreate removed content.
- Failed diagrams and videos offer explicit keyboard-accessible Retry. Diagram requests now use the existing private input column; HTTP/SSE omit input and attempt. Retry reruns the stored worker request without duplicating a learner message and ignores replacement fields sent by the browser. Ownership, CSRF and duplicate-retry guards verified.
- Shutdown interrupts a running diagram Retry; reopening only restores failed state. A subsequent explicit HTTP Retry reuses the durable request successfully. Existing video recovery checks pass. Browser opening/reload triggers no worker call.

Routine choices and tradeoffs:
- Do not salvage invalid JSON. For rejected blocks, retain readable normalized fields; fill missing intent from the originating learner question and missing title/description with neutral labels, with an empty excerpt. Store that recovery task once; explicit Retry uses it unchanged.
- Remove the raw block length rejection so long fields actually trim as specified. Only the four bounded fields reach workers/storage; unknown fields never do. Existing generated-source limits remain.
- Keep the existing six-diagram / standalone-video policy. Reject unsupported groups per request, with matching artifact kinds, rather than silently losing entries. Unsolicited videos now show a failed card and reason but start no worker; explicit Retry is the learner's opt-in.
- Reuse detached video-job lifecycle/polling for diagram Retry. No new dependency, schema migration, automatic generation retry or provider fallback. Legacy failed diagrams saved without any request return an actionable 409 asking for a new tutor request; no historical request is invented.
- This slice hardens the current Mermaid/video request channels. The new visual engine and its one automatic invalid-output retry/live smoke remain TreeTutor-zhf.5; inline video placement remains TreeTutor-zhf.6.

- [ ] HTTP/provider integration verifies routing, inheritance, validation and restart; focused UI checks verify saving, conversation controls, keyboard access and narrow/dark/light presentation.
