title: Specify workspace, model roles and narrated media refinements
description:
# Workspace, model roles and narrated video refinement

Status: agreed design synthesized from the owner's 2026-11-11 interview.
Documentation and specification publication are authorized; this task does not
implement the features. Beads records delivery order and implementation status.

## Problem Statement

Creating a child conversation can produce an answer masquerading as inherited
context. The learner needs a faithful account of prior discussion, without losing
important ideas or pre-answering the new question. Model configuration also lacks
clear roles and effort controls.

Focused chat spends too much space on its header and composer. Passage branching
has too many visible buttons and cannot be dismissed naturally. The learning-tree
rail has an intrusive scrollbar and persistent search field. Usage is presented
as today's text totals, making long-term consumption difficult to understand.
Diagrams contain too many shapes and connections to explain their ideas clearly.

The learner also needs creative educational videos with narration and subtitles,
generated without exposing scripts or production steps. Videos need a durable
library independent of their originating learning trees.

## Solution

Use a quick thinking model to recursively compact prior discussion for each child.
Offer independent model and effort settings for quick thinking, chat and smart
roles. Let children inherit their parent's current chat choice and effort.

Give reading more space through a slim header, floating composer and compact
passage popup. Move title-only search into a floating window and restyle the
rail's scrollbar. Show usage through historical charts that survive content
deletion. Present diagrams as small, colorful explanatory steps.

On an explicit video request, a smart-model worker privately creates a script and
custom 2D/3D scenes. Edge TTS creates narration and subtitle data; Remotion and
Three.js produce the finished local video. A video-sized loading rectangle offers
Cancel, then becomes the finished player. A shared video library provides playback,
Show in folder and trash actions. Creative freedom takes priority over introducing
a reusable scene library in this version.

## User Stories

### Inherited context

1. As a learner, I want a child to receive background rather than an answer to its new question, so that its tutor can answer in the child conversation.
2. As a learner, I want the quick thinking model to compact context, so that background preparation uses the role I configured for it.
3. As a learner, I want compaction to combine the parent's inherited context and parent conversation, so that earlier ancestors remain represented without rereading every ancestor transcript.
4. As a learner, I want important ideas, constraints and conclusions preserved, so that branching does not lose the reasoning I need.
5. As a learner, I want repetition removed without adding new knowledge, so that the inherited account stays concise and faithful.
6. As a learner, I want one compact paragraph with enough length for the subject, so that an arbitrary tiny word target does not discard important ideas.
7. As a learner, I want my selected passage preserved exactly beside that paragraph, so that the child knows what I pointed at.
8. As a learner, I want my new question sent separately, so that the summarizer does not treat it as a question to answer.
9. As a learner, I want the same rule at every nesting depth, so that grandchildren work like children.
10. As a learner, I want inherited context frozen when a branch is created, so that later parent messages do not change an existing child's background.
11. As a learner, I want unrelated branches excluded and child discussion kept out of the parent, so that conversations stay independent.
12. As a learner, I want original messages preserved, so that compaction does not replace my saved source history.

### Model roles and effort

13. As a learner, I want quick thinking, chat default and smart choices in Settings, so that each role has a clear purpose.
14. As a learner, I want each role's model independently configurable, so that background work can use a different model from chat.
15. As a learner, I want each role's effort independently configurable, so that sharing a model does not force identical reasoning effort.
16. As a learner, I want every role to offer models from any connected provider, including my custom endpoint, so that configuration is consistent.
17. As a learner, I want effort choices limited to what the selected model supports, so that the setting is meaningful.
18. As a learner, I want quick thinking to handle suggestions and compaction, so that both use its configured model and effort.
19. As a learner, I want the existing suggestion-model choice retained as quick thinking, so that the role rename does not discard my preference.
20. As a learner, I want unconfigured quick thinking to retain the existing inexpensive provider default, so that it does not silently become the chat model.
21. As a learner, I want new learning trees to use the Settings chat model and effort, so that I control their starting configuration.
22. As a learner, I want children to inherit their parent's current provider, model and effort, so that branching keeps the current conversational choice.
23. As a learner, I want to change model and effort inside a conversation, so that I can adjust its next response without changing global defaults.
24. As a learner, I want configuration changes to preserve visible messages and inherited context, so that switching does not reset a discussion.
25. As a learner, I want changes to Settings defaults to leave existing conversations unchanged, so that saved conversations retain their choices.
26. As a learner, I want smart initially to follow the Settings chat model and effort, so that it works without separate setup.
27. As a learner, I want to override smart's model and effort independently, so that it can share chat's model while using a different effort.
28. As a learner, I want smart's following behavior to use global chat defaults rather than a conversation override, so that its configuration is predictable.
29. As a learner, I want smart to create video scripts, scenes and animation code, so that creative video work uses that role.
30. As a learner, I want settings saved locally and restored, so that I do not configure roles again after restarting.
31. As a learner, I want unavailable selections explained without silent provider substitution, so that work uses the provider I chose.

### Focused chat and passage popup

32. As a learner, I want one slim header row, so that controls leave more room for replies.
33. As a learner, I want a shortened title with the full title available on hover or keyboard focus, so that long titles stay readable without a tall header.
34. As a learner, I want a compact model/effort picker, expand and close controls, so that common actions remain directly reachable.
35. As a learner, I want token stats and secondary header controls under a quiet overflow menu, so that they do not occupy a permanent extra row.
36. As a learner, I want automatic saving to continue without a permanent saved-status line, so that metadata does not crowd the header.
37. As a learner, I want a floating rounded rectangular composer with a circular send button beside it, so that asking a question takes less visual space.
38. As a learner, I want the composer to leave the last reply readable and remain usable in narrow windows, so that the floating layout does not hide content.
39. As a learner, I want a passage popup containing the passage, question field and a small send control, so that branching feels lightweight.
40. As a learner, I want outside click or Escape to dismiss that popup, so that I need no Cancel branch button.
41. As a learner, I want familiarity corrections under a small overflow menu, so that I retain them without two prominent buttons.
42. As a learner, I want branching to retain passage anchoring, keyboard access and failure recovery, so that compact presentation preserves the existing learning flow.
43. As a learner, I want submission still to require my question, so that dismissing or opening a popup never creates a branch.

### Learning-tree navigation

44. As a learner, I want a search icon instead of a persistent search field, so that the rail has more room for learning trees.
45. As a learner, I want that icon to open a floating search window, so that search appears only when needed.
46. As a learner, I want search to match learning-tree titles only, so that a large collection stays simple to search.
47. As a learner, I want choosing a result to open its learning tree, so that title search takes me directly to saved work.
48. As a learner, I want keyboard navigation and an understandable empty state, so that floating search remains accessible.
49. As a learner, I want a thin rounded scrollbar thumb with subtle theme-matched color and no heavy track, so that the rail feels less crowded.
50. As a learner, I want the scrollbar to appear on hover or scroll, so that it stays quiet while remaining discoverable.
51. As a learner, I want mouse, touch and keyboard access to every saved learning tree, so that scrollbar styling never hides functionality.

### Usage history

52. As a learner, I want a usage trend chart, so that I can see how consumption changes over time.
53. As a learner, I want a cumulative view, so that I can see accumulation over months and years.
54. As a learner, I want stacked input, output and cache-read bars, so that I can understand the reported token categories.
55. As a learner, I want breakdowns by model and task, so that I can distinguish chat, suggestions, compaction and video work.
56. As a learner, I want today, week, month, selected-year and all-time filters, so that usage stays useful over years of learning.
57. As a learner, I want precise values on hover or keyboard focus and an accessible textual equivalent, so that graphs do not hide their numbers.
58. As a learner, I want usage to survive learning-tree, conversation and video deletion, so that historical totals do not shrink.
59. As a learner, I want only counts, dates, provider/model and task attribution retained for deleted content, so that historical accounting does not retain deleted text or video.
60. As a learner, I want reported background-model usage counted, so that hidden production work is not hidden consumption.
61. As a learner, I want unavailable measurements identified rather than estimated, so that charts do not invent usage.
62. As a learner, I want historical usage restored after restart without rerunning calls, so that viewing the dashboard spends no model tokens.

### Diagrams

63. As a learner, I want a complex explanation split into small visual steps, so that one crowded graph does not overwhelm me.
64. As a learner, I want few main ideas, clear labels and fewer connections per diagram, so that its point is easy to follow.
65. As a learner, I want meaningful colors and simple visual metaphors, so that diagrams are approachable even to children.
66. As a learner, I want technical detail in the accompanying explanation, so that simpler visuals preserve accuracy.
67. As a learner, I want diagrams readable in both appearances and accessible without color alone, so that colorful presentation remains usable.
68. As a learner, I want existing safe rendering, text alternatives and passage interactions preserved, so that visual improvement does not weaken existing behavior.

### Video generation

69. As a learner, I want video generation only when requested, so that ordinary explanations do not start expensive background work.
70. As a learner, I want smart to generate a script and creative scenes without showing its working steps, so that I receive an educational video rather than a production workflow.
71. As a learner, I want custom scenes without a predefined scene-component vocabulary, so that explanations have creative freedom.
72. As a learner, I want the model to choose 2D or 3D unless I specify, so that the visual form serves the subject.
73. As a learner, I want 2D for ordinary explanations and 3D where spatial relationships help, so that depth has an explanatory purpose.
74. As a learner, I want videos to aim for one or two minutes and run longer when needed, so that explanations are concise but complete.
75. As a learner, I want an explicit duration request to guide generation, so that I can ask for a shorter or longer explanation.
76. As a learner, I want Edge TTS narration from the generated script, so that videos explain ideas aloud.
77. As a learner, I want synchronized subtitles, so that I can follow the explanation with sound off or alongside narration.
78. As a learner, I want setup to install the narration client and rendering dependencies, so that video generation needs no separate manual setup.
79. As a learner, I want generated narration, subtitles and videos saved locally, so that ready videos can be reopened without regeneration.
80. As a learner, I want a video-sized rectangular loading placeholder, so that I know where the video will appear while work runs.
81. As a learner, I want Cancel on that placeholder, so that I can stop unwanted generation.
82. As a learner, I want the finished player to replace the placeholder in place, so that completion does not move focus or disrupt reading.
83. As a learner, I want to continue chatting and navigating during generation, so that production does not block the learning workspace.
84. As a learner, I want scripts, source code, engine details and production logs hidden, so that I only see the loading state and finished video or a simple failure.
85. As a learner, I want a failed generation to stay failed without automatic repair or retry, so that it does not keep spending tokens in the background.
86. As a learner, I want an explicit Retry action after failure, so that another attempt happens only when I request it.
87. As a learner, I want canceled or interrupted jobs never to publish late results or restart automatically, so that stopping work actually stops it.
88. As a learner, I want reopening a ready video to reuse its saved files, so that playback never triggers another model call.

### Video library

89. As a learner, I want one library of generated videos across learning trees, so that I can find them independently of their original conversations.
90. As a learner, I want library playback, so that I need not reopen the source conversation to watch a video.
91. As a learner, I want Show in folder, so that I can locate a video in my file explorer.
92. As a learner, I want explicit deletion through the system trash, so that removal is recoverable through the desktop's trash workflow.
93. As a learner, I want videos retained when their learning tree or conversation is deleted, so that deleting discussion does not delete my video collection.
94. As a learner, I want unavailable media represented honestly, so that a removed or missing file is never shown as playable.
95. As a learner, I want deletion to leave historical usage intact, so that removing a video does not erase the consumption that produced it.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Authority and delivery.** This is the final interview specification for the named refinements. It supersedes conflicting earlier workspace notes, visual layout rules, suggestion-model naming and video proposals only within this scope. Unrelated map behavior, appearance tokens, provider/authentication rules and release prerequisites remain binding. Implementation issues are separate from specification publication.
- **Existing seams.** Extend the existing application server, provider adapters, local store, focused-chat components, Settings window, learning-tree rail, diagram worker, video worker and local renderer. Reuse current session isolation, artifact lifecycle, authentication and request protection rather than introducing another orchestration system.
- **Role settings.** Persist provider/model selections and supported effort choices for quick thinking, chat default and smart. Offer the same connected-provider model choices across roles, including the custom endpoint. Migrate the existing suggestion selection into quick thinking. An unset quick thinking model retains the existing inexpensive provider default; the interview did not choose a new numeric or named quick thinking effort default.
- **Following versus overriding.** Smart model and effort each initially follow their corresponding Settings chat default. Each can be overridden independently; overriding effort does not pin the model, and overriding the model does not itself pin effort. Following is dynamic and uses global chat defaults, not a conversation override. Resolve compatibility against the selected provider/model's supported capabilities; do not send invented effort levels or silently substitute a provider.
- **Conversation configuration.** New roots resolve and save chat defaults. Child creation snapshots the parent's current provider, model and effort. Conversation controls can change model and effort for subsequent work without replacing history or inherited context. Settings changes do not retroactively alter saved conversations. Preserve existing provider-specific defaults for older records without effort rather than fabricating a historical value.
- **Compaction source and purpose.** Use the configured quick thinking model and effort in an isolated summarization call. Combine the parent's fixed inherited background with its completed conversation, identifying the exact passage as source context. Earlier ancestors arrive through the inherited snapshot; unrelated sibling histories and private worker transcripts do not enter the input. The new child question remains separate from the compaction task and is delivered as its own learner message.
- **Compaction result.** Request one coherent compact paragraph containing existing important ideas, constraints and conclusions, with repetition removed. Explicitly prohibit answering the new question, extending the explanation or inventing facts. Preserve the exact passage separately. Do not impose the rejected 80–150-word target, silently truncate important ideas, or treat the old 1,200-word/character limits as an agreed product requirement. Provider context/output ceilings still exist and must fail clearly rather than silently discard history. No replacement numeric product cap was selected.
- **Snapshot consistency.** Keep existing exact-passage validation and atomic branch persistence. Freeze source context at creation, leave original messages unchanged and preserve parent/child isolation. A compaction failure must not create a partly initialized branch or erase the learner's submitted question.
- **Compact surfaces.** Use one slim header row for shortened title, compact model/effort picker, expand, close and overflow. Full titles are available on hover/focus. Move token stats and secondary controls under overflow; remove permanent autosave text while keeping autosave. Keep the existing stats and inherited-context content reachable.
- **Composer.** Use the requested floating rounded rectangular input and adjacent circular send control. Preserve sending, interruption controls, typing accessibility and narrow-screen behavior. Ensure the latest reply and focused input are not obscured. No new attachment, voice-input or editing workflow is implied.
- **Passage popup.** Show the passage, question input and small send control; familiarity actions remain under overflow. Remove Cancel branch and dismiss through outside interaction or Escape with correct focus handling. Preserve existing requirements for nonempty questions, exact anchors, keyboard submission, failed-submit recovery and explored suggestions. Opening or dismissing a popup alone creates no branch.
- **Search and scrolling.** Replace the persistent field with an icon-triggered floating search window. Change the current title-and-message search behavior to title-only search, retaining case-insensitive matching and ordinary local queries without model calls. Do not scan saved conversation text to produce results. Selecting a result opens its learning tree. Retain list grouping, current-tree state and keyboard behavior. Style a thin rounded theme-aware thumb with no heavy track, visible on hover or scroll, without disabling scroll or making touch/keyboard access depend on hover.
- **Usage storage.** Extend local storage with durable usage records independent of message and artifact deletion. Records contain reported counts, occurrence time, actual provider/model and task attribution without retained deleted text, scripts, media or inference transcripts. Migrate available historical measurements once without duplicates; do not reconstruct usage that was never saved or invent missing provider/model attribution.
- **Usage collection.** Capture provider-reported model consumption for chat and background work, including suggestions, compaction, diagram and video generation. A failed/canceled call may still consume tokens; retain a measurement if actually reported and distinguish unavailable measurements. Track logical calls/attempts so repeated events, reopening and migration cannot double count. Edge TTS and local rendering do not become invented LLM-token counts.
- **Usage presentation.** Offer trend/cumulative views, stacked input/output/cache-read bars, model/task breakdowns and today/week/month/selected-year/all-time ranges. Give exact values through hover/focus and an accessible nonvisual equivalent. Respect provider counter semantics so cached tokens are not counted twice in totals. Currency pricing and estimated token counts are not part of this decision.
- **Diagram explanation.** Keep Mermaid but change the generation instructions toward several small explanatory diagrams rather than one crowded graph, with few main ideas, clear labels and purposeful connections. Pair simple visual metaphors and meaningful theme-aware colors with accurate explanatory text. Preserve safe syntax/rendering constraints; use trusted app styling instead of enabling arbitrary generated script, HTML or unsafe styling. No fixed node count or new diagram engine was selected.
- **Video ownership of work.** The chat model handles the learner conversation. An isolated smart-model worker uses smart effort for the script, visual planning and custom composition code. Resolve model/effort into the job's frozen input alongside its existing relevant conversation context. Production transcripts and source remain outside chat, suggestions and inherited context. Preserve the tutor-visible concise finished-artifact representation without exposing production details to the learner.
- **Rendering and creativity.** Extend the existing Remotion pipeline with Three.js through its supported React integration for spatial scenes. The model may freely author custom compositions; a reusable scene/component library and constrained storyboard language are explicitly deferred. Generic safety validation is still required and must not be confused with a creative template restriction. Do not migrate to HyperFrames or add a second renderer for this version.
- **Narration and subtitles.** Install the Edge TTS client as part of setup and save its returned audio/subtitle data locally. Edge TTS uses Microsoft's online service; the owner explicitly accepted that in place of offline synthesis when no paid account/API key is needed. This requires no downloadable offline voice model. Generate speech and subtitle data from the same script and align the animation with actual audio timing, avoiding a second transcription-model call merely to recreate known narration. Provide synchronized subtitles without exposing the script as a separate product surface.
- **Duration and local media.** Aim for 1–2 minutes, extending when the explanation warrants it or the learner specifies another duration. Replace the current short-video-only limits with support for this target; no unlimited resource promise or new fixed upper duration was agreed. Persist ready media and subtitle assets locally for reuse. Keep playback paused initially and retain accessible native player controls.
- **Loading, cancellation and failure.** Reserve a video-sized rectangle during preparation/rendering, with a small Cancel control. Replace it in place with the ready player. No script approval, intermediate previews, code view or technical progress stages are exposed. On failure, report a simple actionable failure. Never automatically repair, retry or regenerate. A new attempt requires explicit learner Retry; successful generation is not automatically replayed on reopen. Keep interruption/restart semantics and reject late publication from canceled or superseded attempts.
- **Network and renderer boundary.** Edge TTS is the narration network stage; chat/smart/quick thinking requests use their selected providers. Rendering remains local and isolated. Stage narration/media for the renderer instead of granting generated code unrestricted network or filesystem access. Extend the existing allowlist and rendering support for the selected 3D/audio features without weakening isolation.
- **Library persistence.** Decouple ready video ownership from originating conversations so conversation/tree deletion preserves library media. Store enough library metadata for playback, title and media location without retaining deleted conversation text or the private production transcript. Existing videos should appear without regeneration; removing a conversation must not strand its saved video behind a conversation-only media route.
- **Library operations.** Provide a global list and playback, a server-owned reveal operation for the selected video and a trash operation for the video and its owned playback assets. Resolve files through server-issued video identity, never an arbitrary client path or shell command. Remove library entries only consistently with media removal, and report missing files honestly. Usage records survive both content deletion and trash actions. Do not silently regenerate a removed video or invent a permanent-delete fallback if trash fails.
- **Visual implementation.** Reuse suitable Astryx components and theme tokens; inspect available loading/dialog/input components before inventing equivalents. Use Impeccable for frontend implementation. Preserve both appearances, keyboard access, reduced-motion behavior and the current optional Vim focus boundaries. No new visual theme or fixed pixel dimensions were agreed.

## Testing Decisions

The owner confirmed the following plan during specification writing: existing HTTP
integration tests are the main seam, with focused UI/component checks for visual
behavior and accessibility, plus real renderer/TTS smoke checks. A broad E2E suite
is not requested. Test observable behavior rather than component internals, prompt
wording alone, private functions or assertions that merely mirror implementation.

- **Prior art.** Existing branching and branch-lifecycle tests run the application server against a real temporary local database and controlled providers. Usage tests already cover provider events, restart and date boundaries. Suggestion/provider tests exercise subscription adapters and a fake custom endpoint. Video tests already inject a controlled renderer and verify artifacts, frozen input, cancellation, media serving and restart. Extend those seams rather than creating a second test harness.
- **Roles and effort.** Through Settings/conversation HTTP operations, verify independent role values, partial smart overrides, dynamic following, custom endpoint choices, supported effort validation, root defaults, parent-to-child inheritance, conversation overrides and reopening. Verify captured adapter requests receive the selected role's actual effort and settings changes do not reroute active jobs or mutate existing conversations.
- **Recursive compaction.** Create root, child and grandchild with distinct important facts. Observe the quick thinking call and saved child context: inherited snapshot plus completed parent discussion, exact passage retained, new question separate, no sibling leakage or parent mutation. Include a paragraph longer than the rejected tiny target to catch accidental truncation. Provider fixtures establish wiring and persistence; a real provider check must separately assess whether summaries preserve meaning and avoid answering. Do not claim a mocked response proves summarization quality.
- **Usage history.** Exercise reported and unavailable counts across calendar/year boundaries and chart ranges, task/provider groupings, restarts, deletion and one-time migration. Delete learning trees and videos and assert the same historical totals with no retained deleted content. Verify no double counting after repeated completion events, retries or reopening, including providers with differing cache-counter semantics. Include reported usage on failed work without inventing missing measurements.
- **Focused chat and popup.** Use focused UI/component checks for slim header, overflow access, title hover/focus, effort/model controls and floating composer fit. Verify outside-click/Escape dismissal, familiarity overflow, keyboard submission, failed-submit recovery and focus return. Check narrow/wide windows and both appearances; screenshots support layout assessment but do not prove all interactions.
- **Title search and scroll.** Integration tests must prove a message-only match no longer appears while title matches still do. UI checks cover opening/dismissing the floating window, result activation and empty states. Verify thumb appearance on hover/scroll and full mouse/touch/keyboard reachability without relying on a visible scrollbar track.
- **Diagrams.** Exercise safe server generation and actual Mermaid rendering of multiple small diagrams with theme colors, text alternatives and existing passage interactions. A real example review assesses simplicity and readability; a syntax fixture or shape count alone does not prove a child can understand the explanation.
- **Video lifecycle.** Through HTTP, use controlled smart provider, narration and render results to verify exactly one job per request, frozen model/effort/context, hidden production data, local media/subtitle delivery, no automatic repair/retry, explicit retry, cancellation and late-event rejection. Fail script generation, TTS and rendering separately and assert no automatic second attempt. Check restart marks unfinished jobs interrupted without restarting inference.
- **Library and desktop operations.** Verify existing/new videos list and play, survive source conversation/tree deletion and reopen without calls. Use injected desktop/trash boundaries in integration tests for safe path ownership, failed trash operations and missing files. A supported-desktop check must actually open the selected folder and move a disposable video to system trash; a mocked launcher does not establish desktop behavior.
- **Real media smoke boundary.** After implementation, generate representative 2D and 3D narrated videos near the target duration using the actual isolated renderer and Edge TTS, inspect frames and listen to audio, verify subtitles and synchronization, and play the saved results after restart. Confirm no hidden repair attempt and no source/transcript leakage. Record provider, hardware, rendering time and actually reported token usage; make no unmeasured quality, speed or savings claim.
- **Setup and regression.** Verify a clean project setup provisions required clients, render dependencies and 3D/audio support, and that reopening ready media works without calling a provider. Run relevant integration tests and the existing build/token checks during implementation. Use focused UI checks, not the whole historical E2E runner by default. Documentation publication itself requires link, requirements, dependency-graph and diff checks, not model generation or a runtime build.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing or running the new features as part of this documentation task.
- A reusable scene/component library, template-only creativity or a constrained storyboard renderer in this version.
- Automatic repair, automatic retries, restart-triggered generation or silent model/provider fallback.
- Offline TTS models, paid narration accounts, voice cloning, soundtrack generation, a public script editor or script approval workflow.
- Conversation-message/full-text search, embeddings or model-powered learning-tree search.
- A second rendering engine, HyperFrames migration, interactive 3D playback or a full video editor.
- A new visual theme, unrelated map/knowledge-graph changes or a general application rewrite.
- Invented token counts, billing estimates, guaranteed unlimited free Edge TTS availability or a new fixed duration/word limit.
- A new broad E2E suite, cloud-hosted media storage or remote Git publication.

## Further Notes

- This specification replaces the earlier partial [workspace notes](workspace-media-refinement.md). It refines the [visual identity](visual-identity-spec.md), [Break down](break-down-spec.md), [video proposal](video-flow-proposal.md) and [diagram artifacts](diagram-artifacts.md) only where its decisions differ; the PRD remains the product entry point.
- Source inspection found an existing compactor using the parent model with the new question in its input and a 1,200-word prompt limit; suggestion selection is separate from chat and has no effort configuration. Usage totals are currently tied to saved messages/suggestions. Search currently includes message text. Videos already use isolated local Remotion rendering, but support short 2D compositions, use the conversation model and are removed with their conversation. These are starting points, not completed refinements.
- [Remotion's 3D integration](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/three) and [caption support](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/captions/) support the selected direction. [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/hyperframes-vs-remotion) was considered; no demonstrated benefit justified replacing the renderer already integrated into this app.
- [Edge TTS documentation](https://pypi.org/project/edge-tts/) describes the online service and audio/subtitle output. It does not require the user's own paid account/API key in its documented workflow. Its maintainer states that the exact [service quota is unknown](https://github.com/rany2/edge-tts/issues/219). Setup installs a client, not Microsoft's speech model; narration text leaves the machine for synthesis. Ready playback uses local files.
- Freeform compositions may consume more tokens than template-driven scenes. The owner chose creative freedom first. No runtime benchmark, listening test, subtitle synchronization test or new UI verification was performed during this interview/specification task.
- Exact effort defaults for previously unconfigured quick thinking/chat roles, subtitle presentation (player tracks versus embedded captions), video dimensions, numeric resource ceilings and the library's precise navigation placement were not selected in the interview. These are implementation details to resolve against supported capabilities; they must not be presented as owner-agreed requirements. Any material change in cost, behavior or creative scope requires clarification rather than an invented decision.

title: Search across learning trees
description:
## Parent

notes: Implemented 2026-11-10. Server: Store.search(query) in server/store.mjs + GET /api/search?q= (query capped at 200 chars). Case-insensitive (toLocaleLowerCase) substring match on root tree title or raw message text in any conversation of the tree (recursive CTE over branches); one result per tree, newest first; title match wins (opens tree as saved), else earliest matching message gives {conversation, plain-text snippet ~120 chars around match}. Client (src/ChatPage.tsx): Astryx TextInput type=search, hidden label "Search learning trees", magnifier + clear button, under New chat. Non-blank query replaces dated list with result rows (saved-tree-row style, muted 2-line snippet); deleted roots filtered client-side; empty → role=status "No learning trees match “q”.". openTree gained optional focus arg: message match selects that conversation with chat open. Keyboard: ArrowDown/Up move field<->results, Enter on result opens, Enter in field opens first result. Spec sidebar rule updated (replaced "no placeholder field" sentence with the search rule). Decisions/tradeoffs: one row per tree (not per message) to keep list calm; search runs server-side per keystroke without debounce (local SQLite; shortcut acceptable for single-user DB); title match does not focus a conversation. Evidence: test/tree-search.test.mjs (integration, real Store + HTTP) PASS; npm test 168/168 incl. token lint; npm run build pass; scripts/verify-tree-search.mjs (fixture, fake provider, not live) PASS: THYLAKOID message match + snippet, ArrowDown/Up/Enter opens branch conversation in chat, roman+Enter opens title match, quasar empty state, clear restores dated list; screenshots docs/verification/tree-search-{dark,light}.png. npm run verify: 39 pass, 2 flaky (break-down-ui, inherited-context; passed on retry), 0 new failures, 1 known (tree-overview TreeTutor-wpc); canvas-positions now PASS (TreeTutor-wpc may be partly closable). Other verification screenshots regenerated by the runner (sidebar now shows the search field). title: Record evidence and let familiarity choose underlines
description:
## What to build

Record evidence per concept: met in a saved reply, asked about (a branch created from its passage), used in the learner's own question, and ignored underline as weak evidence. Derive a familiarity estimate from evidence and send relevant familiarity in the suggestion call so likely-confusing passages are underlined first. Corrections recorded later outrank inference. Spec stories 47–48, 50–51.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Meeting, asking about, using and ignoring a concept each add evidence, visible through the server API.
- Familiarity changes as evidence accumulates; an ignored underline moves it only slightly.
- The suggestion call's input includes familiarity for the reply's relevant concepts.
- Integration tests cover each evidence kind and the familiarity effect.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. Additive global SQLite table evidence(concept, kind met|asked|used|ignored|known|unknown, source, at, UNIQUE(concept,kind,source)). Recording: met = each concept the suggestion call returns for a reply (source = reply id, once per reply; addGraph(graph, message)); asked = any branch (suggested or highlighted) from a passage, resolved to the concept the suggestion call tagged on that passage (new optional suggestion.concept field) plus concepts met in that reply whose name the passage contains (source = child id); used = concept names whole-word/case-insensitively mentioned in a learner question (Store.questionEvidence before the user message is saved); ignored = when the learner sends the next question, the previous reply's ready, unexplored underlines' concepts (source = that reply, so once). Familiarity is derived, not stored: min(1, 0.1*met + 0.2*asked + 0.3*used + 0.05*ignored), rounded to 2 decimals; if any correction exists the latest wins (known=1, unknown=0) and outranks all inference. Store.correct(name, kind) records corrections; UI/API controls left to 5ut.9/5ut.8. GET /api/graph concepts now carry familiarity, evidence counts and correction. Suggestion call input gains familiarity {name: value} for concepts named in the selected passage, question or answer; prompt says mark low-familiarity concepts first and skip near-1 ones. Decisions/tradeoffs: asking raises familiarity (learner received a focused explanation) but less than using; relevance by whole-name mention misses reworded concepts (shortcut comment, upgrade with 5ut.11); evidence stays when a tree is deleted (the learner still met it). Evidence: fixture-backed integration test in test/suggestions.test.mjs covers met (0.1), asked via tagged suggestion branch (0.3), no-concept highlight adds nothing, cross-tree met reuse, used (+0.3), ignored (+0.05 only) with no double count, familiarity sent to the call ({Peterson's algorithm: 0.5}, then {Mutual exclusion: 1} after correction), correction outranking later used evidence, restart persistence, latest correction wins. npm test 142/142; npm run build OK. No live provider run; no UI change.

title: Knowledge tab with corrections and merge
description:
## What to build

A separate Knowledge tab, outside the map and chat layout, lists topics with their concepts, familiarity and evidence. Each concept offers "I know this" and "I don't get this", which outrank inferred familiarity, and duplicates can be merged, combining their evidence and links. Fully keyboard-accessible. Spec stories 49–50, 54, 57–60.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tab lists every topic and concept with familiarity and evidence from all learning trees.
- Both corrections persist and outrank inference in later suggestion calls.
- Merging two concepts keeps one with combined evidence, topics and links.
- Every action works from the keyboard with visible focus.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-10: implemented stories 49-50, 54, 57-60.

Behavior: top-level Learning/Knowledge tabs, separate Knowledge main panel backed by GET /api/graph. Learning map/chat stays mounted while hidden; returning preserves the selected conversation, draft and map transform. Topic-grouped Astryx List rows show every concept (repeated in each membership), evidence counts, familiarity and concept links. Empty/loading/error states and refresh are present. Both correction buttons use CSRF-protected POST /api/graph/correct; explicit known/unknown values persist and outrank inferred evidence in subsequent suggestion inputs.

Merge: searchable dialog chooses the existing name to keep; POST /api/graph/merge atomically unions memberships and incoming/outgoing links, removes self-links and duplicate events sharing kind/source, retains correction row order so the latest correction wins, updates saved passage tags and keeps former names as transitive local aliases. Aliases prevent later extraction from recreating duplicates and preserve use/passage/familiarity matching. Failed transactions roll back all graph and passage changes. New used evidence carries the saved question ID so a question naming both duplicates counts once after merge. Legacy NULL-source use events cannot be reliably deduplicated and are retained rather than guessed.

Routine decisions/tradeoffs: familiarity is shown as an estimate using unfamiliar (<0.35), some familiarity (<0.8), familiar (otherwise), or the explicit correction; no mastery score. Merge keeps the chosen existing name and latest correction across either concept, warns that it cannot be undone, and preserves aliases locally. Evidence uses times-in-questions wording to accommodate historical unsourced events. No new dependencies, no visual identity change, no work beyond this issue. Token padding around TabList prevents its negative margins causing phone-width overflow. Merge success focuses the surviving concept after native dialog close to avoid focus-restoration races.

title: Extract concepts, topics and links from the suggestion call
description:
## What to build

Extend the same suggestion call to return the reply's concepts, their topics (a concept can belong to several) and concept links ("related" or "builds on"). Store them in one knowledge graph across all learning trees, kept locally. Send the existing concept names of the reply's topics and reuse a matching concept rather than creating a duplicate. No embedding model. Settings warns when a call's concept-name list exceeds about 2k tokens. Spec stories 7, 43–46, 53, 55–56.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- One suggestion call per reply returns suggestions and graph data together; no extra model call.
- Concepts, topics, memberships and links are stored globally and survive restart.
- A concept met under a matching name in another learning tree is reused, not duplicated.
- The Settings warning appears when the name list passes the threshold.
- Integration tests over the fake provider CLIs cover extraction, reuse across trees and the warning.
notes: Implemented 2026-11-10. Suggestion call prompt now also returns concepts (name, topics[]) and links (from,to,kind related|builds on); one call, no extra model call. Global SQLite tables concepts/topics (UNIQUE NOCASE names), concept_topics, concept_links (additive, survive restart). GET /api/graph exposes {topics,concepts,links}. Decision: the reply topics are unknown before the call, so v1 sends every topic with its concept names (knownConcepts) and tells the model to reuse known names; server also reuses case-insensitive name matches. Tradeoff: list grows with the whole graph, which the warning flags (embedding pre-filter is 5ut.11). Each call records nameTokens (~chars/4 shortcut); /api/state.conceptNameTokens = latest; Settings shows a warning Banner above 2000. Invalid concepts (no topic/empty name) and links (unknown kind, missing end, self) are dropped without failing suggestions. Evidence: npm test 139/139 pass (fixture-backed: test/suggestions.test.mjs graph extraction, restart, cross-tree reuse on Claude then Codex, isolation, warning); npm run build + astryx doctor --built dist pass (0 fail); live check: app on seeded temp data dir with nameTokens 2600 rendered the Settings warning in the browser. Evidence/familiarity left to 5ut.7.

title: Choose the suggestion model and switch suggestions off
description:
## What to build

Settings lets the learner pin one suggestion model instead of the per-provider default, and switch automatic suggestions off. Only signed-in subscription providers are offered; never substitute API-key access. Spec stories 22, 25.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pinned model is used for new suggestion calls across conversations; unpinning restores the per-provider default.
- With suggestions off, saved replies start no suggestion call; existing saved suggestions stay visible.
- A signed-out provider is not offered as a working choice.
- Integration tests cover pinned, default and off.
notes:
Implemented and verified 2026-11-10.

Decisions/tradeoffs:
- Persist one global {enabled, model: {provider, model}|null} in an additive SQLite suggestion_settings table. Defaults: enabled, unpinned. Server-side storage makes the setting apply to new suggestion calls across conversations and survive app/browser restart, without changing tutor model choices.
- Read settings when a completed reply is saved. Off prevents new suggestion records/calls; existing saved suggestions stay visible. Calls already started finish and save their usage/results. Re-enabling never backfills. This avoids discarding paid in-flight results.
- Unset model follows the conversation's existing subscription default (Claude Haiku; catalog Luna for Codex). A pin captures one subscription provider/model across conversations, including conversations whose tutor uses another provider. Unpin restores the per-provider default.
- Settings offers only signed-in Claude/Codex catalog entries. Save and inference both validate subscription access; unavailable/stale pins remain saved, show disabled in Settings with sign-in/unpin guidance, and fail visibly through the existing Suggestions unavailable state. No provider substitution and no custom/API-key fallback. A custom-endpoint conversation must explicitly pin a subscription model to get suggestions.
- Settings uses existing Astryx Switch/Selector primitives with loading, saving, error, refresh and unavailable states. Existing saved suggestions/rendering and manual passage selection remain unchanged. Partial setting updates preserve the other value, including while model validation awaits.

Evidence:
- test/suggestions.test.mjs: 15/15 passed. Three added HTTP integration checks use real Store, app server and Claude/Codex adapters over fake provider CLIs (plus real OpenAI adapter over fake HTTP endpoint): both provider pins, cross-conversation use, persistence/restart, unpin to Haiku/Luna, tutor choice unchanged, off with in-flight calls, saved suggestions preserved, no backfill, signed-out provider omitted, invalid/missing/custom model rejection, CSRF, stale pin with no provider/API fallback, off/unpin while signed out, and custom endpoint used only for its explicit tutor request.
- Extended protocol fixture accepts explicitly requested pin models while retaining cheap-model verification by default. Updated the existing preview schema assertion for the additive settings table; preview checks pass.
- npm test: 148/148 passed, 0 failed (38.6s; /tmp/treetutor-5ut5-tests.log). npm run build: TypeScript and Vite production build passed.
- npx astryx doctor --built dist: 20 pass, 0 fail; 2 existing theme/font warnings. Impeccable detector: [] for changed UI sources. git diff --check passed.
- Vite-loaded Settings component in jsdom: enabled state loaded, real switch click issued {enabled:false} and displayed off. This was a component smoke check with fixture API data, not browser/E2E or native provider inference. Required provider behavior above is fixture integration evidence; no new live Claude/Codex inference was claimed.

title: Branch from an underline or highlight through the passage textbox
description:
## What to build

Clicking or pressing Enter on an underline, or highlighting any reply text, opens a small empty textbox above that passage. An empty box cannot be sent; Enter sends, Escape closes. Sending uses the existing branch-creation flow with the passage and the learner's prompt, so a short prompt such as "explain" works. The suggestion becomes explored once the child is saved: its underline turns solid and activating it opens the existing child. A highlight overlapping an underline wins. A failed branch keeps the typed prompt. Works at every nesting depth. Spec stories 28–42.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Underline and highlight both open the same empty textbox above the passage; empty input cannot be sent.
- Sending creates one child with the exact passage and inherited context; it opens in the chat panel as any branch does.
- The explored underline is solid; activating it opens that child, with no duplicate created.
- Manually highlighting the same text can still create a second branch.
- Escape closes the box and returns focus; a failed branch keeps the prompt for retry.
- The whole flow works from the keyboard, including in a grandchild.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. Server: branching with suggestion:true stores child id on the matching ready passage (same transaction as the child; Store.branch); a live child is never overwritten; tree() drops refs to deleted children so the underline reads unexplored again. Manual branches never mark. Client: underlineRanges keeps child; explored underlines render u.suggestion.explored (solid) named "Explored passage: X. Opens its chat". Passage: click/Enter/Space on an underline opens the passage textbox (unexplored) or openConversation(child) (explored). Pointer highlight (mouseup with a selection) opens the textbox directly and sets a flag so the following click never activates an underline: highlight wins. Box floats above the passage (.passage-box, absolute, translateY(-100%)); keyboard selection-mode path keeps Ask about selection and an inline box. Box is a small TextInput "Question about this passage" with the passage as description + Create focused chat/Cancel branch; Enter submits natively, and the disabled submit blocks empty prompts. Escape refocuses the underline (or the reply section for highlights). A failed branch keeps the prompt (existing flow). Decisions/tradeoffs: dropped the Follow this passage heading, quote block and footnote for a small box; the box can cover the line above the passage; a stale duplicate suggestion:true request still creates a branch but does not steal the reference. Evidence: test/suggestions.test.mjs new integration test (explore, no overwrite, manual not marking, grandchild, delete resets); test/turn + test/markdown explored cases; npm test 141/141; build OK; astryx doctor 0 fail. Browser (agent-browser, built app, in-process fake provider fixture, not a live provider): new scripts/verify-suggestion-branching.mjs passes 3/3 after fixing a script race. It covers: click opens an empty box above the underline; empty Enter sends nothing; Escape refocuses the underline; Enter on the underline opens the box; failed branch keeps "fail me"; "explain" creates one child "mutex" and marks it explored; solid vs dotted computed style; Enter on the explored underline opens the child with no duplicate; grandchild by keyboard; highlight inside an explored underline creates a second branch "ute". Updated verify-passage-selection.mjs (highlight opens box directly) and verify-keyboard-journey.mjs (INPUT); both PASS.

title: Save suggestions for new replies
acceptance_criteria:
- A completed saved reply triggers exactly one suggestion call; failed, partial and canceled replies trigger none.
- Saved suggestions are exact slices of the saved raw reply; invalid, mismatched and overlapping candidates are discarded.
- Reopening the tree or switching provider/model starts no new suggestion call; replies saved before this feature get none.
- Suggestion instructions and results never appear in tutor history or inherited context.
- Two conversations can run suggestions concurrently while chat stays usable.
- A failed call shows "Suggestions unavailable" and manual highlighting still works.
- Integration tests over the fake provider CLIs, extended to answer suggestion calls, cover the cases above.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. server/suggestions.mjs (reused stash anchored/suggest; dropped stash's 3-cap and proposed questions): after a completed non-empty reply, app starts one detached thread-less call (instructions separate from TUTOR_INSTRUCTIONS) with {inheritedContext, question, answer}. Model: Claude 'haiku'; Codex = first catalog model matching /luna/ (live catalog via ~/.codex/models_cache.json: gpt-6-luna, also gpt-5.6-luna; falls back to conversation model); custom endpoint keeps conversation model. Passages validated as exact UTF-16 slices (no surrogate split), overlapping/duplicate/mismatched dropped, no cap; unparseable output = failed. Store: additive table suggestions(message PK, conversation, status pending|ready|failed, passages, usage) created outside migrate so older builds still open DB; INSERT OR IGNORE = once per reply, so reopen/provider switch never rerun; no backfill; pending -> failed on restart; deleted with conversation. Usage of the call (also on failure) saved with the row; reply token line sums it ('…, including suggestions'); today's total includes it, reply count does not. tutorContext strips suggestions. UI: state.suggesting polls like videos; failed shows 'Suggestions unavailable' under the token line; manual highlighting unchanged. createApp suggestions flag defaults false (tests), main.mjs true; 5ut.5 adds Settings switch. Evidence: test/suggestions.test.mjs (5 tests over fake Claude/Codex CLIs: once-only + haiku, exact passages, usage, isolation of tutor/compaction prompts, reopen/switch/pre-feature none, failed/interrupted none, Codex luna, failure + manual branch, concurrency of two conversations with chat usable, stop mid-call -> failed no rerun); npm test 135/135; tsc + vite build OK; astryx doctor 0 fail. title: Draw suggestions as dotted underlines in replies
description:
## What to build

Render saved suggestions as subtle dotted underlines in the formatted reply, using a pure mapping from the reply's canonical text and its suggestions to underline ranges that matches the offsets manual selection uses. Underlines are reachable with Tab, have descriptive accessible names, and their arrival is announced once, politely. They never move focus, scroll or open anything. Spec stories 8–10, 12, 14–16, 39–40.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Underlines appear only after the reply is saved and cover exactly the saved passages, including in Markdown, code, emoji and repeated phrases.
- Tab reaches each underline; screen readers hear one polite availability announcement.
- Arrival of underlines does not change focus or scroll position.

title: Verify the finished product and record release evidence
description:
## What to build

The final acceptance pass for the finished product: every PRD criterion plus the media and suggestion checks, run on the shipped build with live providers, and a release record.

## Work order

1. Regression: `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and every fixture script.
2. Live journey on Claude and on Codex: New chat, first question, branch, nested branch, concurrent replies, provider switch in both directions, restart, and resume. Compare saved messages, anchors, snapshots, positions, viewport, folds, selection and panel mode before and after the restart.
3. Later increments: a tutor-chosen diagram, a requested video and suggestions each work in a nested child; their generation context stays out of tutor history, verified by inspecting submitted histories and branch snapshots before and after generation, a provider switch and a restart.
4. Optional additions that shipped (rich replies, rename and delete, custom endpoint, Vim bindings): run their acceptance once more inside the full journey. State plainly which optional items did not ship.
5. Local delivery: loopback-only listener, local save location, no credentials in responses, first-run command from a clean checkout.
6. Write docs/verification/product-release.md: a pass or fail row per PRD criterion with links, the providers and models actually used, known limitations and anything unverified. Set the version in package.json to 1.0.0 and add a short changelog.
7. Close the epics whose children are all closed. Leave open, with the reason, anything that did not pass.

PRD.md acceptance criteria and its media paragraph, docs/verification/text-release.md, docs/verification/later-increments.md, scripts/verify-release-journey-live.mjs.

New features and fixes larger than a release defect; file those as separate issues. Pushing, publishing or tagging on a remote.

title: Package first run: one start command, preflight checks and a user guide
description:
## What to build

Make TreeTutor something a learner can start and trust on their own machine without reading the source: one command, clear preflight messages, safe upgrades of saved data and a user guide.

## Work order

1. Start: a single documented command builds when the built assets are missing or stale, starts the loopback server and prints the address. A busy port gives a clear message and an option to choose another. Binding stays loopback-only.
2. Preflight: on start, report the Node version requirement, whether the Claude Code CLI is installed and signed in, and whether Codex is connected, each with the exact next step. A missing provider never blocks opening saved trees.
3. Saved data: record a schema version, and copy the database to a dated backup before any migration that rewrites data. A database from each earlier commit's schema still opens. Print the data directory location, and document backup and restore.
4. Shutdown: stopping the server ends active replies cleanly and marks them interrupted, as the store already does on start.
5. User guide in README.md: install, start, providers and sign-in, the learning journey, keyboard controls, where data lives, privacy (what leaves the machine) and troubleshooting. Remove stale development-only instructions from the user path.
6. Tests: an integration test for start-up on an old-schema database, the backup, and the busy-port message.

## Start here

server/main.mjs, server/store.mjs (constructor migrations), package.json scripts, README.md, scripts/verify-local-delivery.mjs.

## Out of scope

Hosted deployment, a desktop installer, auto-update and telemetry: the PRD keeps TreeTutor a local web app.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a clean checkout one documented command ends with the app reachable on a loopback address and the address printed.
- Preflight names each missing prerequisite with its next step, and saved trees open with no provider connected.
- A database created by an earlier schema opens with all trees intact, and a backup file exists before a rewriting migration.
- A busy port produces the clear message; the listener is never bound beyond loopback.
- README covers every listed topic and matches the shipped behaviour.
- `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
2026-11-10T07:32:40.771298+00:00 — VERIFIED first-run packaging.

Implemented npm start as the single launch command: checks Node >=24, installs missing dependencies/build tools with npm ci --include=dev, fingerprints source/config/lockfile and built outputs, builds only when missing/stale/damaged, launches the server, forwards stop signals and propagates failures. --port takes precedence over TREETUTOR_PORT; --port 0 chooses an available port. Busy-port and duplicate-data-directory errors are actionable. Binding remains hardcoded 127.0.0.1.

Preflight listens before local CLI checks so saved data is immediately readable. Reports actual Node requirement, Claude CLI availability/native sign-in and Codex CLI availability/saved app-owned ChatGPT connection, with next steps and no account identifiers or raw CLI diagnostics. A saved connection is not claimed as entitlement/quota evidence. Sign-in instructions use reload TreeTutor where the existing Settings check button may not yet be shown; no frontend changes were needed.

Persistence uses PRAGMA user_version=1, consolidating all unversioned historical schemas. Existing databases receive a dated owner-only SQLite VACUUM INTO snapshot, including committed WAL data, before any schema/data migration writes. Completed snapshots publish by rename; migrations and the version update commit atomically. Failed upgrades roll back and retain/print the backup; newer schemas are refused. Startup and graceful stop share interrupted-work recovery, keeping partial text and marking pending videos interrupted before storage closes. Stop drains final reply events and provider/video work with a bounded five-second fallback before closing storage and releasing the directory lock.

README rewritten as a learner guide: install/start, sign-in, learning journey, keyboard controls, data locations, upgrades, manual and automatic backup/restore including WAL/SHM precautions, privacy/data flow and troubleshooting. Development workflow is a separate end link.

Final gates: npm test PASS 115/115 (zero failures/skips); npm run build PASS; npx astryx doctor --built dist PASS 20 checks, 2 existing font warnings, 0 failures; git diff --check PASS. Existing large-chunk build warning retained; frontend source unchanged.

Evidence: docs/verification/first-run.md and first-run-checks.json summarize acceptance and limits. first-run-live.json: actual source copy without node_modules/dist, NODE_ENV=production, real npm install/build/start, stale-source rebuild, unchanged-build reuse, HTTP 200, native installed/signed-out CLI diagnostics, owned loopback listeners and SIGINT lock release in all three runs. All 68 copied source hashes match current shipped source before the deliberate temporary source edit. first-run-delivery.json: 9/9 PASS using the production launcher/main process; dated version-0 backup, busy-port diagnostic, exact full-field process restart preservation, local request boundary and bounded credential-pattern scans, SQLite 0600/directory 0700.

Integration fixtures: literal schemas captured from all 16 historical Store commits (12 distinct schemas), populated with nonempty trees/messages, optional model/session/layout/rename fields, branch snapshots, artifacts and committed WAL data. Verify original backup contents/status/version, all preserved fields, one-time backup, failed migration rollback and newer-schema rejection. Real main process opens the oldest saved schema with both CLIs missing and refuses duplicate data-directory startup. Launcher build regression uses a small build subprocess fixture; the separate live report supplies real TypeScript/Vite evidence. Signed-in/saved connection and Node-22-version states are explicitly synthetic; concurrent reply interruption and video recovery use fixture providers over real HTTP/SQLite. No fresh provider inference, OAuth sign-in, browser layout/focus, native Node 22/24 runtime or exhaustive egress audit is claimed or required for this packaging issue.

Routine choices/tradeoffs: stdlib hashing rather than timestamp-only checks/new dependencies; explicit alternate-port flag rather than silent port switching; one aggregate schema version rather than invented historical version numbers; SQLite snapshot plus one migration transaction instead of a custom migration framework; retain backups; ordinary interrupted-job recovery does not create a migration backup. Applied Ponytail and Matt Pocock TDD guidance at the user-specified launcher/HTTP/SQLite integration boundaries, plus codebase-memory navigation. Recovered test failures by marking the manually downgraded video fixture version 0 and updating its shutdown expectation to immediate interruption, then reran the full suite. No separate microtasks, new product features or external blocker.

Stayed on the current branch, preserved pre-existing tracker changes, no .git mutations/staging/commit or remote operations. Ralph owns the pending local commit. Only this issue was worked. Results appended to .ralph-tui/progress.md before close/export.

title: Rename and delete chats and branches
description:
## What to build

Let the learner rename any conversation, delete a whole chat, and delete a branch together with its descendants.

## Work order

1. Rename: an inline rename for the chat header title and the sidebar entry, saved through a new endpoint with the existing 200-character bound. A renamed root is never retitled by a later first question.
2. Delete a chat: removes the root, every descendant, their messages, branches, artifacts and layout in one transaction, after a confirmation that names the chat and its number of conversations. Deleting the open chat moves to the next saved chat or the New chat state.
3. Delete a branch: removes that conversation and its descendants only; the parent conversation and its messages are untouched. Selection moves to the parent.
4. Stop any active reply in a conversation being deleted and ignore its late events. Remove artifact files that belong to deleted conversations.
5. Confirmation is keyboard accessible, focuses the safe choice first and returns focus sensibly afterwards. There is no undo, so the confirmation says so.
6. Integration tests for cascade, transaction rollback on failure, active-reply handling, ownership and CSRF.

## Start here

server/store.mjs (schema, foreign keys), server/app.mjs (POST routes, CSRF check), src/ChatPage.tsx (sidebar list, chat header, map menu).

## Out of scope

Undo, trash, archive, bulk delete, export.

- Deleting a branch removes it and its descendants only; the parent's messages and other branches are unchanged and its remaining edges still attach correctly.

description:
## What to build

Show tutor replies as formatted text: headings, lists, emphasis, tables, code blocks with highlighting and math. Passage selection, branch anchors and source reveal must stay exact against the saved raw message text, which remains the canonical source.

## Work order

1. Renderer: choose a Markdown renderer that exposes source positions and add it with the smallest dependency set; record the choice. Raw HTML in replies is not rendered. Links open safely in a new tab and never navigate the app. The Content-Security-Policy stays free of unsafe script sources.
2. Offsets: every rendered text node carries the start offset of its source text. Map a DOM selection back to raw UTF-16 start and end offsets through those markers, so the anchor's text is still an exact slice of the saved message and the branches endpoint's validation is unchanged. A selection that crosses hidden syntax resolves to the raw span that covers it.
3. Reveal: highlight a saved anchor inside the rendered reply, including anchors that start or end inside formatting or code, and anchors saved before this change.
4. Keyboard selection: keep the read-only raw-text selector as the keyboard path, with its offsets unchanged.
5. Streaming: render partial Markdown without flicker or layout jumps; an unfinished code fence displays as code.
6. Map node previews stay plain text; strip syntax for readability without persisting anything.
7. Tests: offset mapping across emphasis, lists, code, tables, math, emoji and repeated phrases; old anchors still reveal. Update scripts/verify-passage-selection.mjs.

## Start here

docs/architecture-proposal.md (canonical-text indexing), src/ChatPage.tsx (`Passage`, `captureSelection`, reveal), server/app.mjs (branches endpoint validation).

## Out of scope

Rendering learner questions as Markdown, raw HTML, Mermaid (its own artifact path) and editing replies.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Headings, lists, emphasis, tables, fenced code and inline and block math render readably in both colour schemes; raw HTML is shown as text.
- Selecting rendered text with the mouse produces an anchor whose text is the exact slice of the saved raw message at its offsets, across emphasis, list items, code, tables, math, emoji and repeated phrases; the server accepts it unchanged.
- Anchors created before this change, and new ones, reveal at the correct place after reload.
- The keyboard selection path still works and yields the same offsets.
- A streaming reply renders progressively without layout jumps; links cannot navigate the app or run script.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the passage fixture pass.
notes:
2026-11-09: accepted by the owner in TreeTutor-sh8.1; the requirement is in PRD.md.
2026-11-10 checkpoint: resumed partial worktree implementation. Review found failing TypeScript build, heuristic code-line offsets and line-wide code reveal. Decision: mdast-util-from-markdown + GFM table/math extensions for source-position AST; reuse Astryx tokenizer and Code/Text/Heading primitives for exact mapped code text, KaTeX MathML for native math. Raw messages and branches endpoint unchanged. Integration seam: rendered DOM Range -> UTF-16 raw anchor -> real branches HTTP validation/persistence; browser fixture for native selection, focus, reload, theme/layout and streaming stability. No staging/commit; Ralph owns commit.
2026-11-10 VERIFIED: Implemented source-position Markdown rendering with mdast-util-from-markdown + table/math extensions, micromark decoder, existing Astryx Text/Heading/Code/tokenizer and KaTeX native MathML (trust:false). Choice/tradeoffs recorded in docs/architecture-proposal.md. No extra React Markdown wrapper or highlighting dependency. Every text leaf resolves to UTF-16 source markers; transformed escapes/entities/newlines and math carry complete atomic raw spans. Mouse selections take outer raw bounds across hidden syntax; raw keyboard textarea and server/app.mjs branches validation unchanged. Code reveal splits exact characters inside syntax tokens. Pre-change syntax-only anchors display their exact raw source beside the owning formatted element. Stable source keys and one Passage/Reply component preserve DOM through streaming/completion; unfinished fences stay code. Saved and live map previews strip syntax before truncation, without persisting derived text; learner questions stay literal. Raw HTML stays escaped text. HTTP(S)/mailto links have target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer; CSP script-src remains self only. Native fixture link activation opened a separate local tab with window.opener null and left original app URL unchanged.

Evidence: npm test PASS 97/97, 0 skipped, 0 failures (full log /tmp/treetutor-sh8.2-tests.log); npm run build PASS (TypeScript + Vite, non-failing chunk-size warning); npx astryx doctor --built dist PASS 20, WARN 2, FAIL 0 (theme/theme-fonts external-font proof warnings; existing Vite alias self-hosts Figtree); Impeccable detector returned []. node scripts/verify-passage-selection.mjs PASS against final built app with isolated SQLite and deterministic provider. Native Chrome mouse: plain repeated emoji, repeated emphasized phrase, list span and partial highlighted code. Browser DOM Range cases: hidden emphasis syntax, table cells, inline/block math. All created real HTTP branches with unchanged exact raw slices/offsets; keyboard editing/cancel/focus and raw UTF-16 offsets passed. Old formatting-to-code and syntax-only fence anchors plus new partial-code anchors revealed and focused correctly after reload. Streaming heading/code DOM identities and scroll-adjusted layout position remained stable across appended chunks and completion. Map previews stayed plain while raw reply persisted unchanged. Visual inspection and overflow/highlighting/math checks passed at 1280x1000 and 390x1000 in light/dark; captures /tmp/passage-markdown-8JB7B7/. Integration tests also cover entities, escapes, nested continuation lines, CRLF, indented literal fences, safe reference links, inert HTML/unsafe links/math, source markers on all text, element-boundary ranges and branch re-fetch persistence.

Evidence boundary: these are integration and built-app browser fixtures with real DOM/layout/focus/HTTP/SQLite, not live Claude/Codex inference or new provider/auth evidence. Both prerequisites verified closed. No acceptance remains. Preserve unrelated initial tracker changes. No staging or commit performed; Ralph owns the pending local commit. No push/pull/sync.

description:

The 2026-11-09 backlog expansion proposed three additions that the PRD does not yet require. The project owner decides each one; standing implementation authorization does not select them and elapsed time is not agreement.

For each accepted item, add the requirement to PRD.md, then close this issue with the list of accepted and rejected items. Close or defer the tasks of rejected items. The dependent tasks become ready once this issue closes.
