title: Generate Mermaid diagrams in an isolated worker and save finished artifacts
description:
## What to build

The server half of Mermaid diagrams. When the tutor decides a diagram would help, it asks for one; a separate worker with its own provider session produces Mermaid source from a minimal frozen task; the server validates the result and saves it as an artifact owned by the originating conversation and message. Only the artifact id, title and a concise description ever enter tutor context.

## Work order

1. Contract: decide and record how the tutor signals a request (for example a fenced directive in its reply that the server removes from the visible reply) and the frozen task handed to the worker: the diagram intent and the minimal relevant excerpt. Never pass the full transcript, the tutor thread id or credentials.
2. Worker: run through the conversation's provider with `thread: null`, as branch compaction does, separate from the tutor session, abortable, and bounded in time and output size. It must work through both server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs.
3. Validation: accept only Mermaid source that parses. Reject click, href and script directives, HTML labels and oversized output. Store nothing executable.
4. Storage: add an artifacts table in server/store.mjs (id, conversation, message, kind, status, title, description, source, created) with at least pending, ready and failed. Return a conversation's artifacts with its messages. Check ownership so one tree cannot read or attach another tree's artifact by id.
5. Tutor context: later tutor turns, provider switches and branch compaction see only a short marker with the title and description of a ready artifact; never the worker prompt, the source or the worker transcript.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for request, context isolation, validation rejects, ownership and both provider adapters.

## Start here

PRD.md "Isolated media generation". server/app.mjs (message handler, branch compaction as the model for a separate `generate` call), server/store.mjs, server/claude.mjs, server/codex.mjs.

## Out of scope

Rendering in the chat (next task). Restart and failure recovery hardening and live evidence (TreeTutor-vm4.1). Video. A diagram editor.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tutor reply that asks for a diagram produces one saved ready artifact linked to that conversation and message, and the visible reply contains no directive text.
- The worker receives only the frozen minimal task: a test asserts the tutor thread id and unrelated messages are absent, and that worker output does not appear in tutor history or the next tutor prompt.
- Invalid, executable or oversized output is rejected and saved as failed with an honest reason, and the chat stays usable.
- An artifact of another tree cannot be fetched or attached.
- Provider-switch history and branch-compaction input contain only the title and description of ready artifacts.
- No API-key path is introduced. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
Contract decision: one fenced treetutor-diagram JSON object per completed tutor reply with title (120 chars), description (280), intent (600), excerpt (1200). Only those allowlisted strings form a frozen worker task; no full transcript, tree/message/thread ids or credentials. Strip directive before SSE/storage, including partial fences. Worker uses originating provider/model, thread:null, no messages/branch, dedicated instructions and no saved worker session. Bound generation/parse to 60 seconds and 16 KiB output; reject unsafe content before real Mermaid parse. Artifacts are conversation/message-owned pending/ready/failed records, with source only on ready and bounded public failure reasons. Provider-facing history projects ready artifacts to id/title/description markers only. Drop native tutor sessions after directives so raw request data cannot re-enter subsequent resume context. Existing worker/session APIs and SQLite are reused; no UI or API-key path. Integration seams already requested by owner: loopback HTTP + SQLite and both provider protocol adapters. Deferred: rendering, recovery hardening and native media evidence under vm4.8/vm4.1. Preserve startup edits; no staging/commit/remote; Ralph owns commit.
Implementation checkpoint: contract + isolated generation + real parse-only Mermaid worker + scoped SQLite artifacts and metadata-only tutor/compaction projection are complete. Both provider adapters accept dedicated worker instructions; Codex now skips pre-aborted inference and releases stalled interrupted turns. Tutor sessions are cleared before media generation to keep raw directives out of future resumes. HTTP/provider protocol fixtures cover requests, incremental hiding, normal fences, 22 source/status/output-limit rejects, 6 malformed requests, 6 valid syntax families, ownership, cross-provider context, compaction, cancellation/timeouts and late callbacks. Full suite passed 75/75, build passed, Astryx doctor 20 pass/2 pre-existing font warnings/0 fail. Final full suite is rerunning after separating the honest 32-item limit reason from the 16-KiB reason; no native inference or browser/rendering/recovery acceptance claimed. Evidence/contract: docs/diagram-artifacts.md and docs/verification/diagram-artifacts.md plus command/hash JSON. No external blocker; no task split, next issue, staging, commit or remote operation. Existing issue is already in_progress under Ralph (bd --claim refuses that state); lifecycle remains in_progress until final evidence is saved.
Verified result: TreeTutor-vm4.7 acceptance PASS. Implemented the documented hidden four-string task contract, independent Claude/Codex worker sessions, abort/deadline/output limits, conservative unsafe-content rejection plus real Mermaid parsing, pending/ready/failed conversation/message-owned artifacts, scoped GET/no client attachment, and ready-only id/title/description tutor/compaction projection. Dedicated compaction instructions cannot request media; tutor native sessions are discarded before diagram generation and after interrupted hidden prefixes. Worker transcript/source/prompt, unrelated messages, tutor ids and credentials stay out of the worker task or later tutor projection as appropriate. Saved canonical reply text and passage anchors remain separate from artifact markers. Codex pre-abort and stalled-turn cleanup defects reproduced and fixed.
Evidence: docs/diagram-artifacts.md; docs/verification/diagram-artifacts.md and diagram-artifacts-checks.json with outputs/source hashes. FINAL npm test 75/75 PASS, no skips (46.9s); npm run build PASS; Astryx built doctor 20 pass/2 existing font warnings/0 fail; git diff --check PASS; evidence links/hashes PASS. Includes 22 validation/status/size/item-limit rejects, six malformed requests, six valid Mermaid syntax families, both protocol adapters, ownership, same/both-provider context, compaction, cancellation/deadline/late-callback cases and saved-artifact reopen. These are fixture providers with real local HTTP/SSE, SQLite, parse worker and protocol subprocess execution. No live media inference or browser/rendering acceptance claimed; vm4.8 and vm4.1 retain rendering and recovery/native gates. New dependencies pinned to Mermaid 12.3.0 and JSDOM 29.1.1; no previously locked dependency version changed.
All 31 protected startup files remain byte-identical; pre-existing app viewport change preserved; master and recorded HEAD unchanged. No new issue, next-task work, staging, commit or remote operation. Beads/Ralph already initialized. Ralph owns the pending local implementation commit after close/export.

title: Render saved Mermaid diagrams inline in the originating chat
description:
## What to build

The client half of Mermaid diagrams: show each saved artifact inline at its message, rendered safely, with a text alternative and keyboard access, and restore it on reload with no new inference.

## Work order

1. Add the `mermaid` package, loaded lazily so the map and chat bundle stay small. Render with the strict security level, no HTML labels and no links. Keep the Content-Security-Policy in server/app.mjs free of unsafe script sources; adjust only what rendering provably needs and record why.
2. Inline card at the originating message: title, diagram, the description as the text alternative, and a disclosure for the Mermaid source. Pending and failed states. The card is focusable; a large diagram scrolls or zooms inside the card. Use theme tokens so both colour schemes work.
3. In the map node transcript, show a compact "Diagram: title" row instead of the drawing.
4. Reload and reopen restore the same artifact without calling a provider. A render error falls back to the description and the source.
5. Passage selection and branching on the reply text keep working around the card, with unchanged offsets.
6. Tests: integration coverage for the artifact payload and render-state logic, plus one browser fixture for render, keyboard focus and reload.

## Start here

PRD.md "Content rollout" and "Isolated media generation". src/ChatPage.tsx (message list, `Passage`), src/TreeOverview.tsx (transcript rows), the artifact payload from the previous task.

## Out of scope

Failure, interruption, late-event and restart recovery and the live isolation evidence (TreeTutor-vm4.1). Editing diagrams. Export.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- A ready artifact renders inline at its originating message in the chat it came from, and nowhere else.
- The description is exposed as the text alternative; the card and its source disclosure are reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus.
- Source containing links, scripts or HTML labels does not execute or navigate; the page's CSP has no unsafe script source.
- Reload and server restart show the same diagram with no provider request. A render failure shows the description and source instead of a blank card.
- Selecting a passage and branching from the same reply still produces exact anchors.
- The map node shows the compact diagram row.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixture pass.
notes:
Verified result: TreeTutor-vm4.8 acceptance PASS. Saved Mermaid artifacts render only after their owning assistant reply and in their originating conversation. Cards sit outside Passage, keep the description visible and as the image alternative, provide keyboard focus, native scrolling for large drawings and an Enter/Space source disclosure. Pending generation/rendering, generation failure, renderer failure and invalid/unsafe saved sources remain honest; renderer failure opens the saved source. Failed generation has no source under the existing contract. Map messages carry only id/title/status and show compact Diagram: title rows. SSE pending/final records reconcile by id; conversation/message guards reject foreign attachments and reopen overlays retain in-flight artifact state without changing canonical reply text.

Decision/tradeoff: Mermaid 12.3.0 was already pinned by vm4.7; no package/lockfile changes. Dynamic import runs only for a ready artifact in an open chat; initial map requests no Mermaid renderer. Shared 16-KiB/plain-label source guard keeps browser and server rules identical. Strict Mermaid security, HTML labels disabled globally/flowchart, no callback binding, no error SVG; reject HTML/link/script/image output and display SVG through a data image rather than inserting HTML. Existing CSP is byte-identical: script-src self and existing img-src self data suffice, with no new script/style permission. Classic/base appearance uses computed Astryx color/font tokens; serialized renders keep theme config with each diagram and system color changes rerender it. Plain labels and noninteractive images intentionally retain the conservative vm4.7 contract. Explicit .ts imports are enabled in the existing no-emit TypeScript configuration so Node and browser share checks/state logic.

Evidence: docs/diagram-artifacts.md; docs/verification/diagram-rendering.md, diagram-rendering-results.json and diagram-rendering-checks.json. Final npm test 76/76 PASS, no failures/skips/cancellations (38.3s); npm run build PASS; Astryx built-output doctor 20 pass/2 existing font warnings/0 fail; Impeccable detector []; git diff --check PASS; source/evidence hashes and local links PASS. Browser fixture 10/10 PASS: real flowchart/sequence/class/state/ER/pie rendering, focus and both scroll axes, keyboard disclosure, light/dark/narrow containment, actual repeated-emoji mouse branch at UTF-16 [10,19), canonical keyboard selection, live pending-to-ready events, descriptions/source fallbacks, four unsafe persisted-source probes with no executable DOM/navigation/probe request/CSP violation, exact saved artifacts after reopen/reload and separate server-process restart. PIDs 3217755 -> 3219388 reopened the same SQLite file; all 3 root artifacts/messages identical and synthetic generate-call count stays 4 across reload/restart (prior compaction, child reply, tutor reply, worker). Existing passage-selection browser regression separately PASS, including keyboard branch/cancel/focus. Desktop/dark/narrow captures inspected.

Evidence boundary: fixture providers and seeded unsafe records; actual Chromium, production assets, HTTP/SSE, SQLite, Mermaid parse/render and process restart. Integration render-state callback is substituted; browser rendering is real. No live native inference/semantic diagram quality, media context-isolation evidence or pending-worker restart/failure/late-event recovery claim; vm4.1 retains those gates. Existing Vite large-chunk advisory and Astryx font warnings remain. Ponytail and Matt Pocock skills unavailable in checked paths/catalog; Caveman, RTK, codebase-memory, Beads, Impeccable, Astryx and agent-browser used. Beads/Ralph already initialized.

Preserved all 40 protected startup files byte-for-byte, including the original server/app viewport/CSP and package/workflow edits. Existing changes in shared files remain; master/HEAD unchanged. title: Deliver isolated Mermaid diagrams with persistence and recovery
description:
## What to build
After the text release, deliver the whole isolated diagram path: tutor-chosen request, minimal frozen runtime-worker context, validated inline artifact, persistence and failure/restart recovery. Reuse existing chat/storage/provider paths; keep generation work outside tutor history.

2. Restore the same artifact without replay/duplication; keep chat and other jobs usable on failures/interruption and reject late cross-conversation events. Provider switching and compaction receive only relevant finished-content information.
3. Verify transcript isolation and actual worker permissions separately, plus keyboard-accessible inline rendering/text alternatives. Use integration tests and required quality gates; record runtime boundary evidence.

## Start here

## Context and execution
One agent invocation owns this complete task in a 200k context window. Aim for about 140k working context and reserve about 60k for startup, tools, verification and repair; this is a planning estimate, not a measured token guarantee. Read relevant code/evidence on demand, work through internal steps in the same run, and fix recoverable failures here. Create another issue only for a genuinely separate deliverable, external/user gate or evidence that the remaining work cannot fit. Existing implementation authorization and local-only commit rules apply. Prefer integration checks; use browser/E2E checks only where the inherited acceptance requires them. Use Impeccable and Astryx for UI changes.

title: Check-yourself predict-then-reveal visuals
description: Deferred from the inline visuals epic TreeTutor-zhf (grilling 2026-11-11). Small predict-then-reveal questions embedded in replies on the visual engine. Needs tutor guidance on when to quiz before implementation. Do not start until the visual worker ships and the owner revisits.
design: This invocation revisits the deferred issue after TreeTutor-zhf.5 shipped. Smallest implementation: reuse ordinary treetutor-visual requests and the existing isolated smart worker/sandbox, with tutor and worker guidance for an optional predict-then-reveal interaction. Offer at most one brief check per reply only for a useful next-step/cause-and-effect prediction after enough context; honor explicit requests and opt-outs, skip short factual/casual turns, and never gate continuing the conversation. Put the prediction and correct result plus a concise why into intent/excerpt; keep surrounding prose and metadata spoiler-free. Render an initially closed native details/summary labelled Reveal answer, with the question visible, answer/visual outcome/explanation inside. Reveal/close is local, ungraded and unsaved; reload resets it without inference. No new schema, endpoint, score, model call type, or app controls. Tradeoff: generative tutoring policy is prompt-guided rather than a deterministic quiz scheduler; reveal state does not persist.
acceptance_criteria: Tutor guidance defines when to offer/skip a prediction and respects learner requests/opt-outs. Worker guidance provides a visible question and initially hidden correct outcome plus explanation, keyboard-accessible reveal without grading or app/network access. Existing four-field requests stream inline, persist and reopen through the visual engine without duplicate messages or inference. HTTP integration verifies actual request/worker/persistence/history boundaries. Focused built-UI checks verify hidden/revealed states, Enter/Space, no reveal provider calls or branching, light/dark, narrow/desktop and reload reset; native smoke verifies real tutor and worker output, distinct from fixtures. Relevant tests/build and diff checks pass; evidence recorded before closure.
notes:
Verified TreeTutor-zjq against AGENTS.md, PRD.md, the full TreeTutor-zhf epic/comments, closed prerequisite TreeTutor-zhf.5 and docs/inline-visuals-spec.md. This invocation revisits the deferred issue under current implementation authorization; removed stale deferred title/needs-design label. No other issue started.

Result and scope:
- Added tutor guidance for at most one brief optional prediction when a next step or cause/effect outcome helps test an idea, after enough context. Explicit requests and quiz opt-outs take precedence; short factual/casual turns and direct explanations stay unquizzed. No answering/reveal gate, grading or familiarity inference.
- Reused the ordinary four-field treetutor-visual request, isolated smart worker, persisted source and sandbox. Intent/excerpt carry question, correct result and reason; title/description/surrounding prose remain spoiler-free. Worker guidance uses a visible initial state/question and initially closed native details/summary labelled Reveal answer, with answer/result/reason inside. Native Enter/Space, visible focus and automatic frame height; no submitted answer, timer, storage, network or app messages from reveal. Ordinary visuals do not add quizzes.
- Found and reproduced a real interaction regression: explicit source reveal of a saved branch from an answer focused a part inside a still-closed disclosure (assertion false !== true). Three added lines in src/sandbox.ts open containing native disclosures only during explicit source reveal, before focusing the part. Final built regression passes. Ordinary reload remains closed.
- Updated only server/diagrams.mjs, the check guidance section of already-dirty server/prompts/visual.md, three added lines in already-dirty src/sandbox.ts, docs/inline-visuals-spec.md, test/visuals.test.mjs, scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs, the two new check-yourself evidence reports and progress handoff. Decisions/tradeoffs:
- The selected work request revisits the old deferral after its technical prerequisite shipped. Tutor timing is prompt-guided, not a new deterministic quiz scheduler. Existing model/effort, cancellation, retry, worker isolation and permissions remain the engine contract.
- Native disclosure provides keyboard/accessibility semantics without another library or host protocol. Disclosure state is deliberately local and unsaved; reloading resets to closed without inference. Explicit saved-source reveal opens the answer because the learner requested that exact source.
- Hidden answers are educational disclosure, not a secret from the owner inspecting generated source. No quizzes are graded or reported to the knowledge graph.

- npm test passed, including final full suite after the sandbox fix (0 failures). node --test test/visuals.test.mjs: 12/12 passed before the sandbox-only fix. Added HTTP integration checks real request -> smart-worker input, inline position, answer-free metadata/history, source persistence and reopen without worker replay. Existing Claude/Codex native-protocol fixtures retain no-tool/fresh-session/effort checks.
- npm run build passed after final sandbox fix (TypeScript plus production Vite; existing large-chunk advisory only). git diff --check passed; no staged changes.
- node scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs --check-yourself: final PASS, eight focused built-UI groups with synthetic providers and isolated SQLite. Covers visible question, answer/explanation hidden in visual and accessibility tree; Enter opens and Space closes without branching; automatic height; desktop/narrow (1280/390) light/dark; reload resets without inference; no duplicate learner messages/source changes; worker retry/Stop regressions; explicit saved-branch source opens its answer and focuses the exact part without inference. Actual fragment renders a binary-search prediction, keeps result and reason out of initial prose/labels/accessibility, and reveals the correct remaining range plus explanation by keyboard. Both appearances/widths, auto-height and reload without calls passed. Two additional real tutor turns verified a short factual reply and explicit no-quiz direct explanation remain text-only. Evidence docs/verification/check-yourself-native-codex.json and eight corresponding check-yourself-native-codex captures inspected. title: Add an OpenAI-compatible provider adapter with locally stored endpoint settings
description:
## What to build

The server half of the custom endpoint from IDEA.md: a third provider that talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API, configured with a base URL and API key kept on this machine. It is an explicit learner choice and never a silent fallback for Claude or Codex.

## Work order

1. Design note: record in docs/ the API surface used (chat completions with streaming, model listing), how history is replayed, and where the key is stored. Keep the key in a file in the local app-data directory with owner-only permissions; it is written through the server and never returned to the browser, logged or placed in SQLite.
2. Adapter: server/openai.mjs with the same `models()` and `generate()` shape as server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs. The API is stateless, so each turn sends the saved discussion plus the fixed inherited branch context; honour the abort signal; map stream chunks to the existing delta and status events.
3. Settings endpoints: save, test and clear the endpoint with CSRF and the existing loopback checks. Report only whether an endpoint is configured and its base URL.
4. Wiring: register the provider in server/main.mjs only when configured. Branch compaction and provider switching work through it with no special cases.
5. Integration tests against a local fake OpenAI-compatible server: streaming, history replay including inherited context, abort, model catalogue, error mapping, compaction, and that no response body or log contains the key. Extend test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

## Start here

server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs (adapter shape), server/app.mjs (`providers`, `/api/models`), test/provider.test.mjs, test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

## Out of scope

The settings form and model-menu entry (next task). Provider-specific extras such as tools, vision or the responses API.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- With an endpoint configured, a conversation streams a reply through the adapter, and a follow-up turn shows the earlier discussion and inherited context were sent.
- Stop interrupts the request; endpoint errors surface as an honest message and the conversation stays usable.
- Branch compaction and switching to and from Claude or Codex work through the adapter with the fake server.
- The key is stored only in the owner-only file and appears in no HTTP response, log line or SQLite row; a test scans for it.
- With no endpoint configured, behaviour is unchanged and no API-key path exists for Claude or Codex.
- `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
2026-11-09: accepted by the owner in TreeTutor-sh8.1; the requirement is in PRD.md.
2026-11-10T07:50:48+00:00 - TreeTutor-sh8.4 VERIFIED. Design/route/storage contract: docs/custom-endpoint.md. Acceptance matrix and evidence boundaries: docs/verification/custom-endpoint.md.
Implemented server/openai.mjs using built-in fetch: GET models, streaming POST chat/completions, full completed role history plus frozen inherited branch context every turn, optional compaction instructions, stateless session/model persistence, abort/timeout/error/status mapping. New provider id openai is registered in main only when configured and dynamically on save/clear; Claude remains default. Missing providers now fail visibly rather than fall through to another provider. The shared video job promise also catches missing-provider selection so a cleared endpoint cannot leave a retry pending.
Settings: GET/POST /api/settings/endpoint, POST /api/settings/endpoint/test, POST /api/settings/endpoint/clear. Existing Host/Origin/cross-site/JSON/CSRF boundaries apply. Successful settings responses contain only configured/baseUrl. URL root includes any API path prefix; reject embedded credentials and query/fragment, including empty delimiters. Save requires a nonempty header-safe key and makes no network request or provider selection; test lists models from saved settings. Routine defaults: first catalogue model when none selected, identifiers as labels, no new SDK, 30-second catalogue timeout and five-minute generation timeout. title: Offer the custom endpoint in settings and the model menu
description:
## What to build

The learner-facing half of the custom endpoint: a settings form to add, test and remove it, and its models in the compact model menu next to Claude and Codex.

## Work order

1. Settings: in the existing Connections area add base URL and API key fields with Save, Test connection and Remove. The key field never shows a saved key back. State plainly that requests go to that endpoint and are billed by its owner.
2. Model menu: a third group listing the endpoint's models. When it is not configured or failing, show an actionable item instead of a dead choice, as the menu already does for a signed-out provider.
3. Switching: change a conversation between the custom endpoint, Claude and Codex in every direction; visible history stays intact and the next reply uses the prior discussion and inherited context. Children inherit their parent's provider and model as today.
4. Keyboard: the whole configure, select and switch path works by keyboard alone.
5. Update README.md and the help text; record evidence under docs/verification. Use the fake server for fixtures; run one live check only if the owner has supplied an endpoint, and say so either way.

## Start here

src/ChatPage.tsx (Connections block, model `DropdownMenu`, `changeModel`), the settings endpoints from the previous task, scripts/verify-model-switch.mjs.

## Out of scope

Multiple custom endpoints, per-conversation keys, usage or cost display.

## Context and execution

title: Show video status and a paused native player inline
description:
## What to build

The learner-facing half of requested videos: an artifact entry at the request's position in the chat with honest status, and a paused native player once the file is ready, without interrupting chat.

## Work order

1. Insert the artifact entry at its original position with a descriptive title and the states from the proposal's table that generation can reach today: Preparing, Rendering, Ready and Failed. Show render progress only when the renderer reports it.
2. Ready state: title, concise text explanation and an inline native `<video>` player, initially paused, kept within the chat width with its aspect ratio. No autoplay.
3. Completion must not move keyboard focus, scroll the conversation or inject generation messages. The learner can keep chatting and navigate elsewhere while a job runs; the result appears only in the originating conversation.
4. Accessibility: one labelled status announcement per state change, not per progress tick. Tab reaches the player. The player owns its keys while focused, so map and chat handlers must not intercept them.
5. Map node transcript shows a compact "Video: title" row with its status.
6. Reload restores a ready video from the local file with no provider request.
7. Browser fixture for the status sequence, keyboard playback, no stolen focus or scroll, and reload.

## Start here

docs/video-flow-proposal.md "Learner flow" and its acceptance checks 1 and 6. src/ChatPage.tsx and the Mermaid artifact card.

## Out of scope

Cancel, Retry, Interrupted and Unavailable handling (TreeTutor-vm4.3). Captions unless speech was added.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Request a video inside a nested child, navigate away and chat elsewhere while it generates: the finished player appears only in its original conversation.
- The player starts paused; play, pause, seek, volume and fullscreen work by keyboard through native controls; focus and scroll position are not taken when the result arrives.
- Status changes are announced once each; progress ticks are not announced.
- The text explanation is present alongside the video.
- Reload shows the ready video with no provider request.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixture pass.
notes:
2026-11-10 implemented and verified (TreeTutor-vm4.10). Evidence: docs/verification/video-player.md, docs/verification/video-player-results.json.
What: src/VideoCard.tsx inline entry (Preparing/Rendering/Ready/Failed; progress bar only when renderer reports; paused native <video controls>, no autoplay, chat width, 16:9 frame reserved while pending so completion does not shift layout; card aria-live=off with one role=status line per state). Server: in-memory job phase/progress merged into tree GET and previews, /api/state.videos drives client polling after the reply; renderer prints 5% progress; media endpoint serves single byte ranges for seeking. Map row "Video: title · status". Chat Escape ignores focused video.

title: Offer grounded branch suggestions after saved replies
description:
## What to build

The first half of automatic suggestions, following docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md: after a reply completes and is saved, evaluate it once for zero to three grounded passages, show them in a compact "Explore further" group under that reply, and let the learner turn one into a branch through the existing editable branch form. This is the original idea's one-click break-down of a subproblem.

## Work order

1. Trigger: evaluate once per successfully saved completed reply, using the provider and model captured at completion and only the completed answer, its question and the fixed inherited context. Run it as a separate `generate` call with `thread: null` so nothing enters tutor history. Never evaluate partial, failed, cancelled or interrupted replies, and never rerun on focus, reopen or provider change.
2. Validation: each candidate is one contiguous passage with message id, exact text and UTF-16 start and end offsets into the saved reply. Reuse the boundary and exact-slice checks from the branches endpoint in server/app.mjs. Discard mismatches, duplicates, overlaps and ungrounded candidates rather than guess. Cover repeated phrases and emoji.
3. Storage: save completed candidates with their source message, separate from tutor messages.
4. UI: the group appears after its source reply without popups, focus moves or scrolling, with one polite availability announcement. Choosing a suggestion opens the existing branch form with the exact passage and an editable question; only submitting creates and focuses a child through the normal compaction flow; cancelling creates nothing and returns focus to the suggestion. Manual selection keeps working throughout.
5. Failure: show a brief non-blocking "Suggestions unavailable" status; no automatic retry.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for trigger rules, validation, isolation and the submit boundary; a browser fixture for keyboard choose, edit, cancel and submit.

## Start here

docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md (selected design) and its acceptance checks 1, 2, 3 and 5. server/app.mjs (reply completion in the message handler, the branches endpoint), src/ChatPage.tsx (`Passage`, branch form).

## Out of scope

Dismissals, accepted-child reuse, restart and late-event handling, and the learning-example quality review (TreeTutor-vm4.5). Learner profiles, ranking, preferences, automatic child creation.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Complete replies in two conversations at once: each receives zero to three candidates only after its own saved completion, while typing, navigation and focus stay uninterrupted. Failed, partial and cancelled replies trigger nothing.
- Every displayed candidate's offsets resolve to its exact text in the saved reply; repeated text, emoji, invalid offsets, duplicates and overlaps are handled and invalid candidates never appear.
- Choose, edit, cancel and submit by keyboard alone: cancel creates nothing; submit creates exactly one focused child with the ordinary fixed snapshot.
- Model requests and saved histories show only the stated input reaching suggestion generation; candidates and diagnostics stay out of tutor history, including in a nested child.
- An empty result shows no group; a failure shows the non-blocking status and manual branching still works.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixture pass.

title: Generate a requested video in a bounded isolated worker
description:
## What to build

The generation half of requested videos, following docs/video-flow-proposal.md: an explicit learner request creates a job; an isolated worker writes a Remotion composition and renders a finished local file; the server validates and publishes it as an artifact. No player UI yet beyond what tests need.

## Work order

1. Request: detect an explicit video request in the conversation and save a job with the frozen input from the proposal's contract (exact request, relevant saved excerpt, fixed inherited context, source ids). An ordinary explanation never starts a video. When intent is unclear the tutor asks first.
2. Worker: a dedicated workspace per attempt under the local app-data directory, outside the repository, with no tutor credentials, no access to unrelated learning files, bounded run time and controlled network access. Record the actual sandbox and provider permission settings used; context isolation and execution isolation are checked separately.
3. Render: add Remotion and render programmatically to a private temporary output. Validate that the output path stays inside the workspace, the media is readable and the job owns it, then move it to its final location before marking the artifact ready. A failed save never shows a playable success.
4. Storage and serving: reuse the Mermaid artifacts table for job, attempt, status and result description. Serve finished media only through a same-origin artifact endpoint with ownership checks; never accept a generated absolute path or URL as a media source.
5. Tutor context: only artifact id, title and the concise finished-content description. No source code, logs, transcript or filesystem paths.
6. Integration tests for the job lifecycle to ready, path and ownership validation, and context isolation. One real render, kept short, as recorded evidence.

## Start here

docs/video-flow-proposal.md (selected design), PRD.md "Isolated media generation", and the artifact pipeline delivered for Mermaid.

## Out of scope

The inline player and status UI (next task). Retry, cancel and restart recovery (TreeTutor-vm4.3). Narration, captions, editing, gallery.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- An explicit request in a conversation creates exactly one job with the frozen input; an ordinary explanation creates none.
- The worker runs in its own workspace without tutor credentials or unrelated learning files; the evidence note records the real permission and network settings and how each was checked.
- A finished render is validated and published as a ready artifact served only through the same-origin endpoint; an out-of-workspace path, unreadable media or a failed save publishes nothing.
- Tutor history, provider-switch history and branch snapshots contain only id, title and description.
- One real short render completes and its evidence is recorded. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
Implemented 2026-11-09 (TreeTutor-vm4.9).

What: tutor requests a video via a hidden fenced `treetutor-video` block (same JSON shape as diagrams); the server starts a job only when the learner's own message names a video/animation/clip/movie (asksForVideo), so an ordinary explanation never starts one even if the model emits the block. Tutor instructions tell it to ask first when intent is unclear. Job = artifacts row (kind 'video', attempt, frozen `input` JSON: request, intent, excerpt, inheritedContext {snapshot, selectedPassage, question}, sources {conversation, requestMessage, replyMessage, parentConversation, parentMessage}). The job runs detached from the reply stream (learner can keep chatting); app.stop aborts it. Files: server/videos.mjs, server/video-render.mjs, store migration (CHECK kind IN mermaid/video; old Mermaid DBs rebuilt in place, verified with a HEAD-schema DB), app media endpoint GET /api/trees/:tree/artifacts/:id/media.

Isolation settings actually used:
- Composing agent (context isolation): existing provider adapters with a fresh session (thread null), separate WORKER instructions, input = frozen JSON only. Claude: `-p --max-turns 1 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands`, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN stripped, cwd <appdata>/claude-workspace. Codex: shell/apply_patch/js_repl/code_mode/apps/skills off, web_search disabled, every tool request rejected. The agent has no file, shell or network tools; it returns source text, which the server validates (imports only react/remotion, no dynamic import/require/fetch/network APIs/URLs/media elements, ≤64 KiB, required `// Description:` line) and writes into the attempt workspace.
- Render (execution isolation): `bwrap --ro-bind / / --tmpfs $HOME --tmpfs <appdata> --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /run/user --ro-bind <repo>/node_modules --ro-bind server/video-render.mjs --bind <workspace> --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session --clearenv` (env HOME/PATH/TMPDIR only + PWD), SIGKILL after 180 s; composition step bounded at 120 s. Chromium = pre-installed node_modules/.remotion chrome-headless-shell (no download in sandbox). Checked by test "render sandbox hides home and app data…": app-data DB, ~/.claude and repo files denied, writes outside workspace denied, TCP to 1.1.1.1:443 denied, env = HOME,PATH,PWD,TMPDIR.
- Workspace: <appdata>/video-work/<attempt> (outside repo; default ~/.local/share/treetutor). After each attempt bundle/tmp/out are removed (41 MB bundle); Video.tsx/index.tsx kept as private work.
- Publish: server-chosen out/<uuid>.mp4; realpath must equal <realpath workspace>/out/<name>, regular non-symlink file, 1 KiB–200 MiB, `ftyp` header, duration 0–60 s, row still pending with same attempt → rename to <appdata>/videos/<artifact id>.mp4 → finishVideo; DB failure unlinks the file. Media path is derived from artifact id only; endpoint requires conversation ownership + kind video + ready. fs errors are replaced with generic messages (no paths).
- Tutor context: ready videos appear as `Ready artifacts (artifact metadata): [{id, kind, title, description}]` in tutor/provider-switch history and compaction prompts.

Evidence:
- Fixture (npm test, test/videos.test.mjs): lifecycle to ready with frozen input in nested child, ordinary explanation creates none, worker gets only frozen input, same-origin media + wrong-conversation 404, tutor/switch/branch histories hold only id/title/description (no source marker, paths, attempt or input); symlinked output, replaced out dir, missing/unreadable media, render failure, lost ownership and failed save publish nothing; failed job is marked failed and media 404s.
- Live (sandboxed render, no provider): real Remotion render in bwrap, 1 s composition, ~8.4 s, in npm test (skips only if bwrap/browser missing).
- Live end-to-end with Claude (sonnet, subscription CLI): composition written by Claude, rendered in sandbox, published ready: 8 s, 67 KB MP4, 30.7 s total; description "A tournament tree with four players: two semifinal matches each produce a winner, and the two winners slide up along the branches into the final node, where the champion is highlighted." Frame at 6 s inspected: tree with Ana/Dan advancing (some label overlap — generated quality, not validated). Codex not exercised live for video.
- npm test 84/84 pass; npm run build pass; astryx doctor --built dist: fail 0.

Decisions/tradeoffs: invalid or non-completed video requests create no job (no failed card) — simplest; status UI is next task. Media served whole-file without Range (shortcut comment; add with player). Status set stays pending/ready/failed (no preparing/rendering split yet). Restart marks pending videos failed with a video-specific message; full interrupted/retry semantics remain TreeTutor-vm4.3. Remotion 4.0.542 (remotion, @remotion/renderer, @remotion/bundler) added; browser fetched once via ensureBrowser into node_modules/.remotion (needs `npx remotion browser ensure`-style step on fresh installs — currently manual).
